title: DRAUGHT ANIMAL POWER UTILIZATION ON SMALLHOLDER FARMS IN KADUNA STATE, NIGERIA

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the age distribution of people who own and use a certain type of work helper on small plots of land, and compares it to the age distribution of people who do not own these helpers. It also explains the constraints faced by these helpers' owners.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data from a small group of people who own and use these helpers, using a pre-made questionnaire to gather information about their age, the type of helper they use, and the challenges they face.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The pattern of household-level use of working livestock for agricultural tasks is estimated from observed activity and demographic data collected across a defined rural population.
descriptions.approach: A structured data collection method is applied to households with working livestock, recording age, initial herd size, breed preference, and task types. Responses are aggregated and analyzed to identify trends in usage, starting conditions, and constraints affecting performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: PROMOTION OF RABBIT PRODUCTION AMONG THE PEOPLE OF FADA AND DAMBO COMMUNITY OF ZARIA LOCAL GOVERNMENT OF KADUNA STATE

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the profitability of a certain type of animal production, comparing the costs and revenues of a specific venture. It predicts the potential benefits of this venture, including improved nutritional status and skill acquisition.
descriptions.approach: The study used a group of 16 members, each from two communities, to teach them about the production of a certain type of animal. They were trained on various skills, including breeding, feeding, and disease prevention, and were given a foundation stock of animals to work with.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of individuals is evaluated to determine the economic viability and practicality of raising a small-animal livestock system for income and household nutrition improvement.
descriptions.approach: A structured training program is delivered to teach key husbandry practices, including breeding management, animal care, and disease prevention, using a defined set of animals as a model. Performance is measured through output volume, cost input, and revenue generated over a set period.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Numerical data processing from a laser flash experiment on thin graphite layer

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the thermal properties of a thin, flat material attached to a material with known properties. It compares the material's thermal behavior to a theoretical model to make predictions about its thermal properties.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves collecting data from a series of high-energy events that cause the material to heat up quickly. The collected data is then used to solve a mathematical problem that describes how heat moves through the material.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's ability to transfer heat through a thin film attached to a conductive base is estimated from temperature measurements taken over time after a sudden heat input.
descriptions.approach: Temperature signals are fitted to a mathematical model of heat flow through three distinct regions. Parameters are adjusted to minimize the difference between predicted and observed temperature changes using iterative optimization.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Selling with evidence

descriptions.problem: This work studies how to make a fair and profitable deal between two people who have different information about something they want to trade. It tries to find the best way to share the value of the thing being traded.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a mathematical model to figure out the best way to make a deal. They start with a set of rules and test them with different types of data to see if they work.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A seller with private knowledge of a good's traits designs a rule to assign it to buyers based on their signals, aiming to maximize total gains while ensuring buyers trust the disclosed traits and act accordingly.
descriptions.approach: The seller proposes a rule that maps buyer signals to a good's features and assigns it to buyers, adjusting the outcome based on how much information is shared and how buyers value the revealed traits.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Contracting Sequentially with Multiple Lenders: The Role of Menus

descriptions.problem: A decision-maker interacts with multiple parties over time, each offering a set of options to influence future actions. The outcome depends on how these options are structured and selected, and the goal is to determine whether a simpler rule—offering one option per party—fully captures the resulting behavior.
descriptions.approach: Each party presents a range of possible agreements, and the decision-maker chooses one based on anticipated future performance. The selection process is evaluated under uncertainty, and the resulting behavior is compared to what would occur if only one option per party were available.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study of mould hardness for alpha set type resin bonded moulding sand system using Taguchi approach for metal casting applications

descriptions.problem: A quantitative measure of a material's resistance to deformation under pressure is estimated under varying conditions of chemical addition and time-based curing.
descriptions.approach: An experimental design with a structured set of input variables is used to test combinations of chemical concentration and time. Results are analyzed to identify which inputs most influence the output, with validation tests confirming the observed trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Can The Subaltern Tweet? Reflections on Twitter as a Space of Appearance and Inequality in Accessing Visibility

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the potential of a particular platform to facilitate social engagement and activism, but notes that this potential is hindered by unequal access to its benefits. It compares the effectiveness of this platform in different contexts.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a theoretical framework to explore the relationship between a particular economic system and the ability of individuals to express themselves and be heard. It follows a procedure of first examining the potential for this platform to facilitate social engagement, and then analyzing how unequal access to its benefits affects its effectiveness.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is analyzed to determine how different actors—based on resources, location, and social networks—gain or lose opportunity to be seen and heard in public discourse.
descriptions.approach: A model maps how access to platforms and communication tools influences the frequency and reach of individual expressions, using patterns of interaction and participation over time to identify structural biases in representation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Neuro-Electronic Interface: Interrogating Neuronal Function and Circuitry with Innovative Approaches

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the function of complex systems that control movement and learning, and to compare the effects of damage to these systems on their overall performance. It also seeks to optimise the design of systems that can monitor and control these complex systems.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves developing new tools that can detect and characterise the activity of individual cells and networks, and then use this information to understand how these systems work and how they can be improved.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system observes and tracks patterns of activity across interconnected cellular units over time, aiming to detect, classify, and respond to changes in behavior under both normal and disrupted conditions.
descriptions.approach: A sensor network continuously records signals from individual units and their collective interactions, applying real-time analysis to identify structural or functional shifts, then adjusts stimulation or feedback based on observed dynamics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Confidence Scoring Using Whitebox Meta-models with Linear Classifier Probes

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of a model on unseen data by comparing its predictions to a set of known outcomes. It also optimises a scoring mechanism to predict the confidence of the model's predictions.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a two-model system: a base model that makes predictions, and a meta-model that learns from the base model's successes and failures. The meta-model uses a subset of the base model's features to make its predictions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how reliably a complex model performs on new inputs by analyzing internal signals across its layers.
descriptions.approach: A secondary model learns to assign a reliability score based on patterns in intermediate layer outputs, using simple, interpretable rules to evaluate consistency and stability of the primary model's internal activity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Impact of Sex Differences on Odor Identification and Facial Affect Recognition in Patients with Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how individual differences in cognitive performance affect the accuracy of identifying sensory cues and interpreting social signals, comparing outcomes across individuals with varying levels of cognitive load and demographic factors.
descriptions.approach: It uses a multivariate model that adjusts for age and cognitive resources, then evaluates how baseline sensory processing and social cognition interact, revealing distinct patterns based on biological sex and cognitive demands.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Structural and functional characterization of the Curli adaptor protein CsgF

descriptions.problem: This work characterizes the properties of a protein that helps attach large, protein-based structures to the surface of cells. It estimates the structure of this protein and how it interacts with other proteins and lipids.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of biochemical and biophysical techniques to determine the structure of the protein. They then analyze the protein's interactions with other molecules to understand its role in attaching large protein structures to the cell surface.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A mechanism is inferred by which a surface-anchoring protein links a fibrous, self-assembling protein complex to a cellular membrane, enabling controlled deposition and structural stability.
descriptions.approach: A protein is studied in a lipid-like environment to reveal its dynamic, extended regions. Its interaction with a fibrous polymer is mapped through physical and chemical assays to determine how it mediates surface attachment and structural integrity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Prediction of the Pharmacokinetics of Pravastatin as an OATP Substrate Using Plateable Human Hepatocytes With Human Plasma Data and PBPK Modeling

descriptions.problem: The rate and affinity of a drug's uptake by liver cells are estimated from in vitro experiments involving human-derived cellular systems and biological fluids. These values are used to predict how the drug behaves in living organisms across different dosing levels.
descriptions.approach: A computational model integrates experimental uptake rates and binding affinities to simulate drug concentration over time in a living system, adjusting for physiological differences without requiring empirical scaling factors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Association of serum prolidase activity in patients with isolated coronary artery ectasia

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the relationship between a certain condition and a biomarker, comparing the levels of the biomarker in two groups to see if there is a correlation. It also predicts the presence of the condition based on the biomarker levels.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a statistical analysis approach, comparing the levels of the biomarker in two groups and using various tests to determine the significance of the correlation and the accuracy of the predictions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative measure is estimated to determine its association with a specific vascular condition characterized by abnormal dilation. The strength and independence of this relationship are assessed using clinical and laboratory data from matched patient groups.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model compares two groups on a continuous biomarker level, using tests for differences and correlations. It evaluates the predictive power of the biomarker through regression and diagnostic performance metrics like sensitivity and area under the curve.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Advancements in PLL and VCO Technologies
title: Session 25 overview: Clock generation for high-speed links: Wireline subcommittee

descriptions.problem: A system generates a stable, high-frequency timing signal from a lower-frequency source, while minimizing irregularities in the signal's timing and maintaining precision across varying operating conditions.
descriptions.approach: It uses feedback to adjust timing based on real-time signal differences, applies adaptive correction to reduce timing noise, and leverages frequency multiplication with controlled phase alignment to enhance signal consistency.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Highly Conserved Motif within the Amelotin Protein Controls the Surface Growth of Brushite

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a protein on the growth of a mineral surface, comparing the growth rates at different concentrations. It predicts the optimal concentration range for growth and identifies a specific part of the protein that inhibits growth outside of this range.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of microscopy and spectroscopy techniques to directly measure the growth of the mineral surface and the binding of the protein to it. They analyzed the data to identify the kinetic and energetic basis for the protein's effect on growth.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system detects how a specific protein fragment influences the rate at which a mineral surface expands under varying concentrations, revealing a narrow range where growth is enhanced and elsewhere it is suppressed.
descriptions.approach: The interaction between the protein fragment and a mineral surface is measured through force-dependent binding events, with growth rates and binding strength analyzed across concentration gradients to identify thresholds and mechanisms of surface modulation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Semi-Random Access in Small Cells With User Priority

descriptions.problem: This work aims to balance the performance of two types of users with different control modes: those that require centralized control and those that can manage on their own. It estimates the optimal balance between these two types of users to maximize the overall system performance.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using randomized power control and a step-by-step process to optimize the system within a predetermined level of performance for the users that require centralized control. The goal is to find the best balance between these two types of users to achieve the highest overall performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system must manage dynamic user access patterns where some users stay stable and others move in and out frequently. The goal is to balance performance between stable and transient users while maintaining efficient communication for all.
descriptions.approach: A randomized power allocation method is applied to incoming users. Stable users are served with consistent signal strength, while transient users are handled with adaptive signal strength adjustments based on current network conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Structural Influences on the Urban and Rural Residents' Spiritual Consumption in China after China's Entry into WTO

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the differences in spending patterns between people living in urban and rural areas of China, and compares these differences to changes in spending patterns over time. It aims to explain how economic changes have affected people's consumption habits.
descriptions.approach: The research uses data from census records to compare spending patterns over 20 years. It then uses this data to model changes in spending patterns and compare the impact of economic changes on urban and rural areas.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The relative allocation of resources between tangible and intangible services is compared across two distinct population groups, assessing how changes in economic exposure influence spending patterns and shifts in service-oriented consumption behavior.
descriptions.approach: A model tracks how economic integration affects spending decisions by analyzing income distribution, service demand, and regional differences in consumption priorities over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Left circumflex coronary artery from the pulmonary artery in scimitar syndrome

descriptions.problem: This work investigates the frequency of a rare heart condition in a specific group of patients, and estimates the prevalence of this condition. It compares the results to a known incidence rate and suggests a new investigation method.
descriptions.approach: The researchers reviewed medical records and imaging data from patients with a specific heart condition, and analyzed the results to estimate the prevalence of a rare variation. They used a statistical method to calculate the confidence interval of their findings.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The frequency of a rare vascular anomaly where a major blood vessel arises from a pulmonary artery branch is estimated in a group of patients with a complex congenital heart and lung condition.
descriptions.approach: Medical records and imaging data are reviewed to identify cases where a major vessel originates from a pulmonary artery branch. The rate of occurrence is computed from the total number of patients and the number of such anomalies observed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: ENDOSCOPIC MANAGEMENT OF COLONIC INTUSSUSCEPTION BY ESD- CASE SERIES

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new technique for removing a type of bowel obstruction that is caused by one part of the bowel telescoping into another. It predicts that this technique is safe and feasible for carefully selected patients.
descriptions.approach: The technique involves using a special tool to remove the obstruction, and then examining the removed tissue to determine its cause. The procedure is repeated for each patient, and the results are compared to determine the effectiveness of the technique.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A procedure is performed to remove a localized, often recurrent, intraluminal mass that has telescoped into an adjacent segment, with the goal of determining whether the mass originates from the mucosal layer and can be safely excised without surgical intervention.
descriptions.approach: A patient is first evaluated with imaging to confirm the mass's location and depth. A reduction technique is applied, followed by a complete removal of the mass using a specialized endoscopic tool under general anesthesia, with real-time monitoring for bleeding and healing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Temporal Coupling of Subsurface and Surface Soil CO 2 Fluxes: Insights From a Nonsteady State Model and Cross‐Wavelet Coherence Analysis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between the amount of carbon dioxide produced by microorganisms and roots in the surface layer and the amount of carbon dioxide produced by microorganisms and roots in the deeper layers. It compares these amounts using historical data.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a mathematical model to analyze the data and a statistical method to examine the patterns and relationships between the amounts of carbon dioxide produced by microorganisms and roots in different layers.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's response to environmental drivers is assessed over time to determine how well surface observations reflect underground processes, especially under varying moisture and texture conditions.
descriptions.approach: Temporal patterns in surface and underground emissions are analyzed using a dynamic model that tracks how changes in environmental conditions propagate through layers. Coherence and delays are evaluated across time scales to identify when and how surface signals align with deeper processes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Time-Dependent Shear Stress Distributions during Extended Flow Perfusion Culture of Bone Tissue Engineered Constructs

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the distribution of forces within complex structures over time, comparing the effects of different designs on these forces. It also predicts how these forces change as the structures mature and optimizes the design for better performance.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a computer program to simulate the behavior of these complex structures, analyzing the forces within them at different time points. They take samples and use imaging to monitor changes over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The rate at which a material undergoes internal structural transformation is estimated over time, based on changes in its physical properties observed across multiple time points.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic simulation models how fluid interactions with a porous structure evolve, using time-varying inputs to track how internal forces shift as the material develops new physical characteristics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: INFLUENCE OF MANGANESE FERTILIZER ON GRAPES EFFICIENCY ON SANDY SOILS OF THE SOUTH RUSSIA

descriptions.problem: A quantity of interest in a crop system is measured under varying input conditions to determine how it changes with time and resource application, especially during a key growth phase.
descriptions.approach: A treatment is applied at a specific growth stage with a defined input level, and the resulting output is compared across different input doses to identify the most effective dose for improving yield and quality metrics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
title: Entanglement manipulation via Coulomb interaction in an optomechanical cavity assisted by two-level cold atoms

descriptions.problem: A system of interacting components is studied to manipulate and tune the strength of quantum correlations between distinct parts, adjusting one correlation while affecting others, and evaluating how these relationships persist under varying environmental noise levels.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic control mechanism adjusts the interaction strength between components, enabling selective enhancement or suppression of specific quantum-linked behaviors based on external modulation, while monitoring stability under thermal disturbances.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study on Viscoelastic Deformation Monitoring Index of an RCC Gravity Dam in an Alpine Region Using Orthogonal Test Design

descriptions.problem: This study aims to estimate the maximum amount of movement that a certain type of concrete structure can withstand before it becomes unsafe. It also predicts the likelihood of this movement occurring and compares it to the actual movement to determine the structure's safety.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of mathematical models and statistical methods to analyze the structure's movement. They break down the movement into different components, such as temperature, time, and pressure effects, and then use these components to estimate the maximum movement and predict the likelihood of it occurring.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A threshold value is estimated to represent the maximum expected response of a structure under combined environmental and operational stressors, based on statistical analysis of historical and simulated conditions.
descriptions.approach: A structured testing framework evaluates multiple stressor combinations, using probabilistic and entropy-based methods to refine the threshold. The final value is derived by balancing rare event likelihood and uncertainty in input variables.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Anti-inflammatory effect of xanthomicrol, a major colonic metabolite of 5-demethyltangeretin

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a substance on a biological process, comparing the levels of the substance and its effects on a specific outcome. It predicts the outcome of a substance on a biological process, comparing the levels of the substance and its effects.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a specific method to identify the substance's effect on a biological process. They fed a group of mice with a substance, collected samples, and analyzed them to identify the substance's effect on a specific outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of a compound derived from a dietary substance on cellular responses to a stressor is estimated, specifically its influence on the production of reactive molecules and the expression of genes involved in stress response and cellular protection.
descriptions.approach: A compound is administered to an organism over time, and tissue samples are analyzed to measure its concentration. In vitro, the compound is exposed to a stress signal, and outputs such as molecule levels and gene activity are monitored to assess its impact on cellular behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Psychometric evaluation of the Thai translation of the Self-Efficacy for Diabetes Scale in delaying the progress of diabetic nephropathy in adults with T2DM

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine whether a new self-assessment tool, developed to measure an individual's confidence in managing their condition, is effective in slowing the progression of a serious complication in adults with a chronic health issue.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from a study involving adults with a chronic health issue, and compared the results to a similar study in a different cultural setting to ensure the tool is reliable and unbiased.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A scale is evaluated to determine how well it measures a person's confidence in managing a chronic health condition across diverse cultural contexts.
descriptions.approach: The scale is tested for consistency, fairness, and reliability using responses from individuals in a new linguistic and cultural environment, with statistical methods to assess how well it preserves its original structure and predictive power.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Optical design of a holographic head-mounted display with enhanced efficiency

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the efficiency of a system that displays images to a user's eyes. It predicts how well the system will work for different viewing angles and pixel sizes.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a special kind of image display that concentrates energy onto a small area. It records and plays back images in a way that varies across the surface, causing a decrease in efficiency. A revised design is presented to improve efficiency and image quality.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system generates a visual image for a user's eye using light scattered from a structured volume. The performance is evaluated across different viewing positions and angles, measuring how effectively light is redirected to form a clear, stable image.
descriptions.approach: A spatially varying pattern is recorded using two distinct light sources. The system adjusts the pattern's geometry based on viewing position to improve light redirection and maintain consistent image quality across the field of view.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Analysis of the Changing Laws and Influencing Factors of Social and Economic Indicators in the Upper Reach of Han River Basin

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and compares the impact of a large-scale project on economic indicators in a specific geographic area. It predicts changes in these indicators over time and optimizes the effects of the project.
descriptions.approach: The study uses statistical methods to analyze data on economic indicators, such as population, GDP, and land use. It applies techniques like linear regression and trend analysis to understand the relationships between these indicators and the project's effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of economic and demographic metrics from 29 administrative regions is examined over time to detect shifts in growth patterns and identify when and how those shifts occur.
descriptions.approach: Time-series data is analyzed using linear trend fitting and statistical tests to detect abrupt changes. Growth rate trajectories are compared across regions to identify periods of structural change, and patterns are used to infer underlying drivers of change in economic and population dynamics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Morfoanatomía de las plántulas de dos especies de lupinos graníferos: Lupinus albus y L. angustifolius (Fabaceae, Faboideae)

descriptions.problem: The structure and dimensions of early plant growth stages are measured and compared across two cultivated species to identify differences in tissue organization and developmental patterns.
descriptions.approach: Seeds are grown under controlled conditions; key growth features are recorded and tissue samples are sectioned, examined, and imaged. Anatomical features are analyzed and cross-referenced with known patterns in related species and environmental influences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Correlation of Collagen Type I and III in the Skin and Lungs in Patients with Bullous Emphysema Complicated by Spontaneous Pneumothorax

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the relative content of two types of connective tissue in the skin and lungs of individuals with a lung condition complicated by a spontaneous air leak, and compares it to a group without the condition. It also explains the correlation between the two types of connective tissue in both groups.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a comparison method to analyze the content of two types of connective tissue in skin and lung samples. It employs a specialized microscopy technique to reveal the correlation between the two types of connective tissue in both groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative comparison of structural protein ratios is made between two biological tissues in individuals with a specific disease and a healthy reference group.
descriptions.approach: A measurement technique is applied to assess the relative abundance of two distinct protein forms in tissue samples. The results are then analyzed for consistency across tissues and individuals, identifying a strong linear relationship between the two tissues' protein profiles.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Review of Agro-waste Materials as Partial Replacement of Fine Aggregate in Concrete.

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment of how naturally occurring, byproduct materials can substitute for small-grained construction components in building materials, based on global case studies and performance data.
descriptions.approach: A systematic compilation and analysis of empirical results from diverse regions, evaluating physical and mechanical properties under varying conditions to identify patterns and potential thresholds for substitution.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Care Coordination for Pediatric Patients at Federally Qualified Health Centers in Arizona

descriptions.problem: The extent to which health teams implement integrated support for patients with long-term conditions is assessed, comparing outcomes across locations with differing resource availability.
descriptions.approach: A structured framework evaluates how well teams manage patient needs across medical and personal domains, analyzing patterns by location and identifying key operational constraints affecting service delivery.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Persepsi Peternak Terhadap Aspek Reproduksi Ternak Kambing di Kabupaten Lombok Utara

descriptions.problem: A pattern of knowledge is assessed regarding reproductive practices in a rural livestock population, comparing current understanding to historical data on breeding cycles, offspring numbers, and genetic selection.
descriptions.approach: Data is gathered from a selected sample of individuals, then organized and analyzed to identify gaps in knowledge about gestation length, offspring timing, and breeding strategies based on observed outcomes and reported practices.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Deep soil water recharge response to precipitation in Mu Us Sandy Land of China

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how much of a given input event penetrates deep into a subsurface medium over time, depending on the initial state of the medium. It compares outcomes under different starting conditions to determine how much of the input reaches a defined depth.
descriptions.approach: It tracks the movement of an input signal through a medium, measuring how far it travels based on the current state. It then computes the total volume that reaches a target depth, adjusting for the initial conditions and the rate of signal propagation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 1 Knowledge desired by ems managers of their ambulance clinicians

descriptions.problem: This work estimates what types of knowledge are most valuable to professionals who provide emergency medical services, and compares these types across different individuals. It aims to explain the importance of this knowledge in their work.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a survey method, where 36 individuals rated and ranked different types of knowledge, and then compared the top 10 types. The top types were then identified as the most valuable knowledge for these professionals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies the types of expertise deemed most valuable by decision-makers in emergency response settings, based on input from experienced personnel. It evaluates and ranks these expertise areas by assessing their perceived importance and interdependence.
descriptions.approach: A structured iterative process collects and refines qualitative inputs from experts. Responses are grouped, scored, and reorganized through consensus-based ranking to highlight the most prioritized forms of knowledge in high-pressure operational environments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Coal-fired Utility Boiler Operation Factors Analysis and Optimization Measures

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of various factors on the efficiency and safety of a complex system, comparing different variables to identify the most influential ones. It aims to explain how these factors interact and affect each other.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves analyzing data from multiple sources, including temperature readings, equipment performance, and environmental measurements. It uses a model to identify patterns and relationships between the variables, and then applies adjustments to achieve the desired outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's performance across multiple objectives—efficiency, safety, and environmental impact—is assessed under varying operating conditions and interdependent subsystem behaviors.
descriptions.approach: A model integrates real-time operational data from auxiliary systems and load variations to simulate how changes in input mix and process parameters affect overall system stability and resource use.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A rare case of Histoplasma Keratitis in an immunocompetent patient

descriptions.problem: An unusual case of a fungal infection in a healthy individual is reported, where a common type of fungus is found to cause an infection in the eye. The infection is treated and resolved, but the individual is otherwise healthy.
descriptions.approach: A sample from the eye is sent for microbiological analysis, and the fungus is grown in a culture. The individual is then treated with a medication that is effective against this type of fungus, and the infection is resolved.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rare form of fungal infection affecting the eye surface is identified in a person with normal immune function, based on laboratory growth of a fungus from a tissue sample.
descriptions.approach: A tissue sample is collected and cultured to detect fungal presence. If the fungus grows, treatment with a specific topical antifungal agent is administered, and recovery is confirmed after a defined period of symptom resolution.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: Abstract 747: A new class of DNA alkylating indolino-benzodiazepine agents (BIAs) linked with a DNA binding moiety for use with antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new class of compounds that can damage a specific type of molecule in cells, and compares their effectiveness to a similar but less effective class of compounds. It also predicts that these new compounds can be used to improve the therapeutic index of a treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of structure-activity relationship studies and experiments to identify and modify compounds that can damage the target molecule. They then tested these modified compounds in various cell lines and found that they were highly effective.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A molecule is designed to bind selectively to a specific cellular target and deliver a cytotoxic payload to cells expressing that target, with potency and specificity tuned through structural modifications.
descriptions.approach: A scaffold is engineered to bind a target site with high affinity, and its structure is modified to enhance binding strength and stability. Linkage to a targeting agent is achieved through chemically defined connections, preserving activity while enabling selective delivery.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Exploring Consumers' Repeat Purchase Intentions in Green Economy

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood that people will buy the same thing again based on their feelings about the environment and the quality of the product. It compares these feelings to the value people get from buying the product.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a mathematical model to connect these feelings to the likelihood of buying the same thing again. They tested this model using data from a large group of people who filled out a survey online.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how strongly individuals are likely to choose products aligned with environmental values, based on their beliefs about those products' quality, trustworthiness, and overall benefit.
descriptions.approach: The model uses structured surveys to collect responses from users, then applies statistical analysis to test relationships between perceived attributes and behavioral tendencies, identifying key drivers through a validated framework.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Tough Egg to Crack

descriptions.problem: An expert's thought process is described by presenting a real case, where sequential pieces of information are given to someone who doesn't know the case. The goal is to understand the expert's thought process.
descriptions.approach: The expert's thought process is revealed by presenting a real case, where sequential pieces of information are given to someone who doesn't know the case. The focus is on the thought processes of both the team caring for the person and the person presenting the case.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A sequence of observations is presented, and a pattern of change over time is inferred from them, with the goal of identifying a likely underlying mechanism driving the observed behavior.
descriptions.approach: The information is processed step by step, with each new piece integrated into a developing narrative. The narrative is refined as more data arrives, and the most plausible explanation is selected based on consistency with prior observations and known patterns of behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Representaciones, recursos y estrategias comunicacionales del MOCASE-VC en las TIC

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a social movement's online presence in addressing land ownership debates, comparing its reach and engagement to that of other movements. It predicts the potential for online activism to influence policy changes.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a theoretical-methodological approach to analyze the movement's online activities, focusing on how information is shared and acted upon within a networked society. They examine the movement's use of virtual space to inform its actions and strategies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of people uses digital tools to share and refine their understanding of land rights, adapting their views based on interactions across connected platforms.
descriptions.approach: They gather input from diverse participants, refine shared interpretations over time, and adjust how information is presented based on how it is received and reused in different digital environments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Desire Work

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a specific type of self-improvement program in changing people's behaviors and identities, and compares the outcomes of participants who underwent this program to those who did not. It also examines how these changes relate to broader societal issues.
descriptions.approach: The researchers followed a group of individuals who used a particular method to try to change their behavior and identity, and analyzed the results to see how it affected them. They also looked at how these changes were connected to other social and cultural factors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of individuals seeks to transform their sexual identity through structured behavioral and spiritual practices, aiming to align with societal expectations of moral and social order in a context marked by intense social and cultural pressures.
descriptions.approach: They engage in daily self-monitoring, follow prescribed routines in speech and movement, and interpret their personal transformation as contributing to broader societal stability and moral renewal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Simple and Label-Free Fluorescent Detection of Melamine Based on Melamine–Thymine Recognition

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the presence of a toxic substance in a product, comparing its levels to a safe threshold. It predicts the outcome of consuming the product if the substance is present.
descriptions.approach: The method uses a reporter molecule to detect the presence of the substance, which changes its behavior in the presence of the substance. The approach involves combining the reporter molecule with a specific sequence of molecules to produce a detectable signal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the presence and concentration of a specific contaminant in a biological fluid by measuring a change in signal intensity that occurs when the contaminant binds to a structured molecular probe.
descriptions.approach: A probe forms a stable, folded structure in the presence of the contaminant, shielding it from degradation. This folding enhances a reporter molecule's interaction with the structure, producing a measurable signal proportional to the contaminant's concentration.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Analytical methods of optimization of operational parameters of the main gas pipelines (gas mains)

descriptions.problem: This work aims to find the best settings for managing a network of pipes that transport a vital resource, by using mathematical models to identify the most efficient way to operate the system. It estimates the performance of the system under different conditions.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves developing a mathematical model to analyze the system's performance, testing it on real data, and comparing the results with those from a different method that uses complex calculations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's performance is evaluated under varying conditions to determine the range of operating settings that maintain efficiency and stability without exceeding physical or safety limits.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical framework is built to simulate how system behavior changes with input variables. It identifies the set of conditions where performance remains consistent and robust, using known operational patterns and constraints.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Consistent Color Generation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates a unique color for a given string of information, ensuring consistency across different systems. It predicts the color based on the string, and compares it to colors generated by other systems.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves mapping the string to a numerical representation, using a predefined mapping, and then applying a color generation rule to produce a consistent color. The rule is based on a mathematical formula that takes the numerical representation as input and produces a color output.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A unique visual signal is derived from a textual input to ensure identical output for identical inputs across different systems or contexts.
descriptions.approach: A deterministic function maps input text to a standardized output value using a fixed set of rules based on character patterns, sequence length, and predefined encoding schemes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The influence of silviculture investment in fixed assets on forest water conservation in China

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the relationship between the amount of water saved by forests and the amount invested in fixed infrastructure. It predicts the amount of water saved from 2014 to 2020 based on historical data.
descriptions.approach: The study uses statistical methods to analyze the correlation between the amount of water saved and the investment in fixed infrastructure. It then uses these results to make predictions about future water savings.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantity representing long-term environmental stability is estimated based on historical patterns and external conditions, showing a strong, consistent relationship with investment in long-term infrastructure.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model correlates the observed environmental stability with cumulative investment over time, adjusting for delays in effect and other influencing factors such as land cover and regional development.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Facial Nerve Paralysis Treatment and Research
title: Comparison of Objective Outcomes in Dynamic Lower Facial Reanimation With Temporalis Tendon and Gracilis Free Muscle Transfer

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and compares the effectiveness of two different surgical procedures to improve the physical function of patients with a specific condition. It aims to determine which procedure is better for each patient.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed data from 28 patients who underwent one of two surgical procedures. They measured and compared the results of each procedure to see which one produced better outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to evaluate how effectively two different surgical techniques improve the balance and movement of a side of the face during a natural expression, measuring symmetry and range of motion in multiple directions.
descriptions.approach: A model compares outcomes across two interventions by analyzing changes in spatial alignment and movement range before and after treatment, using repeated measurements from patients during expressive actions to quantify differences in performance and consistency.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Hidden diagnosis behind viral infection: the danger of anchoring bias

descriptions.problem: This work aims to identify and rule out a specific type of infection that may be hidden behind more common symptoms, such as shaking and swollen areas. It estimates the likelihood of this hidden infection based on available data and evidence.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a model to compare and weigh the evidence from various sources, including symptoms and test results. The goal is to identify and rule out this hidden infection, and to provide a more accurate understanding of the patient's condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of symptoms is observed, and a common explanation is assumed based on prior experience. The likelihood of a less frequent but serious underlying cause is underestimated despite conflicting evidence.
descriptions.approach: A set of symptoms is evaluated using a dominant initial hypothesis. A second, more severe but rare condition is assessed by reweighting evidence against the initial assumption, using clinical data to challenge the first interpretation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The digital notion of the citizen-centred media ecosystem

descriptions.problem: A system is inferred that maps how user behavior and technological changes influence public engagement and trust in information flow across diverse communities.
descriptions.approach: A structured framework evaluates trends in access, interaction, and response patterns using historical and real-time data, adjusting predictions based on feedback loops between individuals and digital platforms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Identification of functional group present in Andrographis paniculata (kalmegh) leaves by FTIR analysis

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify the types of molecules present in a plant's dried leaves by analyzing the way they absorb and emit infrared light within a specific range of frequencies. It estimates the types of molecules based on the patterns of absorption and emission.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a technique that involves mixing the plant material with two different liquids and then heating it to separate the molecules. They then analyze the infrared light emitted by the mixture to identify the types of molecules present.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The presence and relative abundance of specific molecular features in a natural plant material are determined from spectral signatures across a wide range of vibrational frequencies.
descriptions.approach: A sample is treated with two different liquid environments to alter its surface chemistry, then analyzed using a technique that maps how bonds vibrate. Peaks at distinct frequencies are matched to known molecular patterns to identify key chemical components.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: RTHP-35. SURVIVAL IMPACT OF DELAYS PROLONGING THE OVERALL DURATION OF ADJUVANT RADIATION THERAPY FOR PATIENTS WITH GLIOBLASTOMA

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of delays on the overall duration of a treatment on the survival of individuals with a specific type of brain cancer. It compares the survival outcomes of individuals who complete the treatment within a certain timeframe to those who experience delays.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a large dataset to identify a threshold for the treatment duration. They then analyzed the data to determine the relationship between the treatment duration and the survival outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A survival outcome is estimated based on the time it takes to complete a prescribed treatment regimen after initial surgery. The effect of delays beyond a certain threshold on long-term survival is compared across groups.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model identifies a critical time point separating better and worse outcomes. Survival probabilities are then calculated for individuals who finish treatment within or beyond that time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Influence of foliar application of phenylalanine and urea at two doses to vineyards on grape volatile composition and amino acids content

descriptions.problem: The effect of external nutrient inputs on the chemical profile of plant-derived products is assessed, specifically how these inputs alter the concentration of volatile organic compounds and key nitrogen-containing molecules.
descriptions.approach: A controlled experiment applies two levels of a nitrogen-based compound and a specific organic compound to plants, then measures resulting changes in volatile emissions and internal molecular concentrations across different treatment groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics
title: Equivalent Circuit Model of an Optomechanical MEMS Electric Field Strength Sensor

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of a device that converts light into a physical signal, allowing for precise measurements of a physical property. It compares the device's performance to a theoretical model, aiming to explain the observed effects.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a mathematical model to describe the device's behavior, taking into account the properties of the materials used. They then use this model to identify and minimize the effects that were observed in the actual measurements.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's response to external stimuli is estimated under real-world conditions, where unintended signal distortions arise due to material and structural imperfections.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical framework maps input variations to output behavior, incorporating physical constraints and non-ideal material responses. It enables prediction and correction of deviations by simulating how internal components interact under operational conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A mathematical model of bowel sound generation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the characteristics of a physical phenomenon that occurs when a certain system is subjected to various activities. It aims to explain the underlying mechanisms and provide a general framework for understanding this phenomenon.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a mathematical framework to describe the system's behavior, with four key parameters that influence the phenomenon's characteristics. The parameters are adjusted to fit different types of data, and a comprehensive example is created to demonstrate the framework's accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to reproduce complex temporal patterns of physiological activity by combining dynamic waveforms with varying pressure, frequency, and timing characteristics across different segments of a biological process.
descriptions.approach: A physical system with four adjustable parameters is used to generate time-varying signals. These signals are composed by blending wave components with distinct amplitude, pressure, duration, and spacing to replicate observed patterns in real-world data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Experimental Comparison Between the Impact of using Two Types of Bio Diesel on Compression Ignition Engine Performance and Emissions

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine the best energy source for a specific type of machine, given a scarcity of another common energy source and high costs. It estimates the impact of blending a certain percentage of a plant-based substance with a common liquid on the machine's performance and emissions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers varied the percentage of the plant-based substance added to the common liquid and tested the machine's performance and emissions at different speeds and equivalence ratios. They used data from these tests to compare the effects of the different blends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment is made of how substituting a biological feedstock into a conventional hydrocarbon fuel affects key performance indicators and exhaust byproducts under varying operational conditions.
descriptions.approach: A series of controlled trials are conducted across different operational loads and mixture ratios, measuring output variables and comparing them to baseline conditions using statistical analysis to identify trends and thresholds.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Matter of Equality: Linear Pricing in Combinatorial Exchanges

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of different rules on the efficiency of a system where buyers and sellers can offer packages to each other. It aims to compare the efficiency of different systems and explain how the number of buyers and package size affect the outcome.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using mathematical models and numerical experiments to analyze the system. It follows a procedure where the model is applied to different scenarios, and the results are compared to determine the most efficient system.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The performance of a market mechanism is evaluated under different price rules, comparing how well trade outcomes align with optimal allocation across multiple participants offering bundled goods or services.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical model assigns a single price to all bundles, then simulates trade outcomes under various price structures, measuring how much value is lost when prices are uniform versus individually adjusted across buyers and sellers.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Control of a STATCOM‐assisted self‐excited induction generator‐based WECS feeding non‐linear three‐phase and single‐phase loads

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and optimises the performance of a system that supplies energy to various devices at different locations, taking into account the variability of the energy source and the devices' power demands. It aims to maintain the energy supplied to these devices at their rated levels with minimal distortion.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a combination of feedback control and pitch angle control to regulate the energy supplied to the devices. It also employs a technique to eliminate distortion in the energy supplied to the devices, ensuring that the devices receive energy at their rated levels with minimal distortion.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system maintains stable output power and frequency despite fluctuating input energy and variable demand from complex, non-linear consumer devices.
descriptions.approach: A feedback loop adjusts a power conditioning element in real time based on system state, while a separate mechanism modulates input energy capture to stabilize output. Both actions work together to suppress distortions and maintain consistent performance under changing conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Consideration of Alternative Event-causal Libertarian Models of Basic Free Actions

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the probability of an event being caused by a free action, given some data about the agent's desires and intentions. It compares different models of how this event-causal view works, and optimizes the model to avoid certain problems.
descriptions.approach: The author develops two new models to think about self-forming acts. One model keeps the idea of dual efforts, but thinks of them as keeping both options alive during deliberation. The other model thinks of the agent as actively assigning weights to reasons before making a choice.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine whether decisions emerge from internal dynamics or are influenced by external factors during the moment of choice, based on observed patterns of agent behavior and reasoning processes.
descriptions.approach: The system models decision moments as involving two competing internal states that either persist together during deliberation or dynamically shift in weight based on real-time evaluation of available inputs.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Involvement of JAK/STAT Signaling and a Basement Membrane-Associated Protein during Air Sac Primordium Development in Drosophila Melanogaster

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the importance of a specific process in the development of a complex structure, compares its effects on different parts of the structure, and optimizes its role in the structure's functioning. It explains how this process affects the structure's growth and development.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of genetic manipulation and observation to study the role of a particular process in the development of a complex structure. They applied specific genetic tools to manipulate the process and observe its effects on different parts of the structure.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The development and morphogenesis of a specialized tissue structure is studied, focusing on how specific molecular cues influence growth and patterning during early developmental stages.
descriptions.approach: A genetic manipulation system is used to alter expression levels of a key regulatory factor in specific cell populations. Tissue outcomes are assessed through phenotypic changes and structural integrity tests across different developmental time points.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment
title: Mutation Assessment Model for the Potential of Clean Energy Development

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood that a given geographic area will experience significant growth in sustainable resource utilization based on environmental, infrastructural, and economic indicators.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates how rapidly and consistently conditions improve over time by comparing current states to historical baselines, assigning weights to key factors, and detecting sudden shifts in performance patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Green Database : An Initiative to Enhance Renewable Energy Efficiency

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the most efficient way to store and manage information, using a limited amount of a valuable resource, to minimize waste and optimize its use. It compares different methods to achieve this goal.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves designing a new method that integrates a valuable resource with the storage and management of information, using a combination of data analysis and optimization techniques to achieve the best results.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how much resource consumption is tied to data storage and retrieval operations, aiming to reduce the environmental impact of information handling processes.
descriptions.approach: It models operations based on environmental conditions and adjusts processing loads dynamically to minimize resource use during data access and storage tasks.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pulmonary sclerosing pneumocytoma, a rare tumor of the lung

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the presence of a rare, benign tumor in a patient's body, based on imaging data and tissue samples. It compares the tumor's characteristics to those of normal cells to determine if it's malignant or not.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of imaging data and tissue samples to identify the tumor. They then examined the tumor cells under a microscope to look for signs of malignancy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A solid, well-defined mass is identified in a patient's body through imaging. The nature of the mass—whether it is benign or malignant—is assessed using tissue analysis and specific molecular markers to determine its biological behavior and potential for recurrence.
descriptions.approach: A tissue sample is removed and examined under a microscope. Specific protein expression patterns are tested to classify the mass and guide long-term monitoring, with no signs of aggressive cellular behavior observed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Kikuchi–Fujimoto disease with relapsing polychondritis

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the severity of a disease in a patient, compare it to a control group, and explain the underlying cause of the symptoms. It predicts the outcome of a treatment and optimizes the patient's condition.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a medical imaging technique to visualize the patient's body and identify areas of inflammation. They then analyzed the images and biopsy results to determine the underlying cause of the disease and track the patient's progress over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of inflammation is identified in cartilaginous and connective tissue, characterized by recurrent episodes of redness, swelling, and metabolic activity hotspots, alongside tissue necrosis and immune cell infiltration.
descriptions.approach: A longitudinal assessment tracks changes in tissue metabolism and structural damage over time, using imaging and histological markers to detect inflammatory flares and recovery, with treatment response monitored through repeated scans and clinical symptom resolution.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Imidazoporphyrins as supramolecular tectons: synthesis and self-assembly of zinc 2-(4-pyridyl)-1 H -imidazo[4,5- b ]porphyrinate

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the ability of a certain type of molecule to assemble itself into a larger structure, and compares it to the same molecule in different states (solid vs solution). It also optimises the conditions for this assembly to occur.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a synthesis procedure to create the molecule, and then test its ability to self-assemble in two different environments. They compare the results to see if the conditions affect the assembly.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system forms ordered structures through repeated interactions between molecules in both liquid and solid phases, with the arrangement depending on molecular shape and binding preferences.
descriptions.approach: Molecules link together via specific non-covalent interactions, forming predictable patterns. The structure emerges consistently under varying conditions, showing stability and reproducibility across environments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Cue utilization differentiates resource allocation during sustained attention simulated rail control tasks.

descriptions.problem: This study estimates how well participants can use information to guide their actions during a long, complex task that involves following a pattern of activity. It compares performance and resource use in two different conditions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of self-reported data and physiological measures to compare performance and resource use in two conditions: one where participants had to follow a pattern, and one where they had to follow a more complex pattern.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how effectively an individual uses environmental signals to manage cognitive effort over time during a prolonged task involving repetitive and predictable dynamics.
descriptions.approach: It monitors behavioral and physiological indicators over time, comparing patterns of attention focus and mental resource consumption across individuals with varying levels of signal responsiveness.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Advancements in PLL and VCO Technologies
title: Low Power 16 Phase Ring Oscillator and PLL for Use in sub-ns Time Synchronization over Ethernet

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the accuracy of a timing system, predicting the minimum time difference between two signals. It compares this prediction to the actual time difference, aiming to optimise the system's performance.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves designing a timing system that can accurately measure and control the timing of signals, using a buffer stage to reduce energy consumption. The system is built using a specific type of semiconductor technology and is tested for its performance and accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates timing precision across multiple signal phases, predicting phase deviations with sub-nanosecond accuracy using periodic waveform measurements and real-time phase comparisons.
descriptions.approach: It uses a cascaded phase detection structure with low-loss signal buffering to maintain phase coherence, adjusting phase relationships dynamically based on measured timing fluctuations and minimizing energy expenditure during operation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Identifying Procedural Core Competencies for Undergraduate Emergency Medicine Education at the University of Zimbabwe College of Health Sciences

descriptions.problem: Estimate and predict the quality of emergency medical procedures in low-income countries, where resources are limited and clinical skills are suboptimal. Compare the quality of procedures to a standard or ideal.
descriptions.approach: Use a consensus-building process to gather expert opinions on a list of procedures, with multiple rounds of feedback and evaluation to reach a final list of essential procedures.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of essential clinical skills is identified for training medical students in high-pressure, resource-limited healthcare settings, based on expert input and iterative agreement.
descriptions.approach: An iterative process gathers input from experienced instructors, refines a list of skills through repeated evaluation, and finalizes a set of widely agreed-upon procedures through structured feedback and consensus building.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Holographic four-point functions in Toda field theories in AdS2

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the form of a mathematical object that describes how certain quantities behave in a specific kind of problem. It predicts that these quantities take the same form as a similar object in a different kind of problem.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a mathematical model to compute the object's behavior in a specific situation. They follow a procedure that involves applying a set of rules to the model to obtain the desired result.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The structure of correlation patterns among four observable events in a two-dimensional space is analyzed to determine whether they follow a consistent mathematical form across different physical systems.
descriptions.approach: A model is constructed that maps the interaction strengths between four events to a known symmetric pattern, and checks whether this pattern holds uniformly across distinct sets of data derived from the same underlying physical rules.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Parvovirus B19‐induced severe anemia in heart transplant recipients: Case report and review of the literature

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the presence of a specific virus in patients with severe blood loss, predicts the likelihood of this virus causing the blood loss, compares the effectiveness of different treatments, optimizes treatment protocols, and explains the underlying reasons for the blood loss. It does so using data from patient blood samples.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves testing patient blood for the presence of the virus, treating patients with a specific medication, and monitoring their response to treatment. The approach follows a step-by-step process of investigation, diagnosis, and treatment, using a combination of laboratory tests and clinical observations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A condition causing rapid decline in red blood cell count is identified in individuals with suppressed immune function, and the likelihood of this condition being triggered by a specific pathogen is assessed using biological and clinical data.
descriptions.approach: A detection method measures the presence and concentration of a pathogen in bodily fluids. Clinical outcomes are evaluated after intervention, and patterns in patient history and response are analyzed to determine the probability of the pathogen being the root cause.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study of sorption isotherm and isosteric heat of Kepok Banana (Musa paradisiaca F.) slice

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the relationship between the amount of water in a substance and its ability to hold water, and optimizes a model to describe this relationship. It predicts the amount of water in a substance at different temperatures and water activities.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses a combination of experiments and mathematical models to describe the relationship between water content and water activity. They test different models to find the best fit for the data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A relationship is estimated between the amount of water bound by a material and the water activity at constant temperature, across a range of environmental conditions.
descriptions.approach: Data from static weight measurements under controlled humidity are fitted to mathematical models to determine binding behavior. Thermodynamic changes during water uptake and release are derived from temperature-dependent equilibrium measurements.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Growth potential of primed Moringa oleifera varieties under nursery and field conditions of Potohar region-Pakistan

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the growth potential of a specific type of tree, comparing its performance under different conditions. It predicts the effect of a treatment on the tree's growth and compares the results to a control.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a procedure involving treating seeds with different liquids, then planting them in bags and measuring their growth over time. They analyzed the data using statistical techniques to identify any patterns or differences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The growth performance of different seed treatments is evaluated across controlled and open environments, measuring height, stem thickness, and development speed in response to varying pre-planting seed conditioning methods.
descriptions.approach: Seeds are exposed to distinct pre-planting treatments, then planted in contained and open settings. Growth metrics are recorded over time and compared using statistical analysis to determine which treatment yields the most consistent and rapid development.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effect of combined optical radiation on tomato seeds

descriptions.problem: The effect of varying exposure duration, intensity, and environmental temperature on a biological response rate and subsequent growth outcome is estimated from experimental observations under controlled conditions.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical model links input variables to a response metric using a regression function, calibrated to ensure statistical reliability at a defined confidence threshold.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Abstract P081: Applying Precision Public Health Tools to Address Health Disparities Among African-Americans in Alachua County, Florida

descriptions.problem: Estimate, predict, compare, optimise or explain the health disparities between different age groups in a specific geographic area, using data on hospitalizations, insurance rates, and community resources.
descriptions.approach: Use a combination of demographic data, hospitalization records, and community resource data to identify specific geographic areas with high concentrations of individuals at risk, and then apply a practical focus to develop interventions that address these disparities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of community-specific health outcomes is estimated across defined geographic areas, comparing patterns of risk and access to services among different population subgroups over time.
descriptions.approach: Data from health records and local service availability are integrated and analyzed by location to identify clusters of high risk and low access. Interventions are then proposed by linking these clusters to locally available support networks and service providers.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Recycling and utilization of industrial and municipal waste in materials production
title: Using Calcined Waste Eggshells to Remove Sulfate in Nonpotable Concrete Mixing Water

descriptions.problem: This work investigates the effectiveness of using a certain type of material to remove a specific type of contaminant from water. It aims to estimate the amount of contaminant that can be removed and the conditions under which this removal occurs.
descriptions.approach: The researchers first test the material in a laboratory setting to see how it affects the contaminant's removal. They then use a computer program to simulate the process and predict the results, validating the simulation with the actual laboratory data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman
