descriptions.problem: A model estimates how inherited and learned traits from a household influence an individual's chances of being selected for a structured learning program, based on observed behaviors and household characteristics.
descriptions.approach: The model evaluates household traits like income, parental background, and engagement in structured activities, then maps how these traits correlate with selection outcomes through statistical analysis of reported behaviors and outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Therapeutic anti-glioma effect of the combined action of PCSK inhibitor with the anti-tumoral factors secreted by Poly (I:C)-stimulated macrophages

descriptions.problem: A system's response to a stimulus is measured to determine how effectively it suppresses uncontrolled cell growth and reprograms surrounding cells toward a protective state.
descriptions.approach: A compound is combined with a signal that activates immune-like cells to release protective factors. The combined effect is tested in a complex environment to assess suppression of growth and reprogramming of cell behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Psychometric properties of the Turkish version of “Healthy Eating and Physical Activity Self‐Efficacy and Recall Questionnaires for Children”

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the reliability and validity of a questionnaire to measure the ability of a group to make good food choices and engage in regular physical activity, using data from 233 students aged 9-14.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data through a survey and a questionnaire, then used statistical methods to evaluate the data and determine the questionnaire's reliability and validity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of behavioral indicators is assessed to determine consistency and reliability across a group of individuals using structured self-report data and demographic information.
descriptions.approach: The data is analyzed through statistical modeling to evaluate internal consistency, factor structure, and relationships between items. A model is fitted to verify that observed patterns align with expected underlying constructs, ensuring the tool performs consistently across different groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Evaluation of the ventriculocholecystic shunt—an overview of present practice in adult and pediatric hydrocephalus

descriptions.problem: A clinical decision is made regarding the suitability of a bodily cavity for diverting a fluid that accumulates in the brain to manage a neurological condition affecting cognitive and motor function.
descriptions.approach: A systematic review of published outcomes is conducted, comparing long-term results across different anatomical sites used for fluid drainage, evaluating complications, effectiveness, and patient survival over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Socioeconomic status and cardiovascular health in the COVID-19 pandemic

descriptions.problem: A pattern of health outcomes is assessed across different social conditions, evaluating how exposure to stressors and economic instability influence the likelihood of adverse health events in vulnerable populations.
descriptions.approach: A model maps social conditions to health outcomes by analyzing trends in stress exposure, access to resources, and behavioral patterns, then identifies interventions that improve access, reduce risk factors, and support long-term well-being.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Principals Managing the Expectations of Instructional Leadership

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how individuals in a complex organization balance multiple responsibilities and adapt to changing needs. It seeks to identify the key factors that influence their ability to do so.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of interviews and coding to analyze the processes and structures established by key figures in the organization. It follows a qualitative approach, focusing on themes and patterns in the data to inform recommendations for improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A central figure in an educational setting is assessed on their ability to coordinate diverse responsibilities while maintaining focus on improving learning outcomes through consistent, adaptive practices.
descriptions.approach: A structured process is developed where multiple stakeholders contribute to decision-making, and regular feedback loops are established to adjust strategies in response to evolving conditions and performance indicators.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A case of acute myocardial infarction in a patient with congenital atresia of the left coronary artery

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a rare heart condition in a patient, based on their age and medical history. It predicts the patient's heart condition and compares it to a normal heart condition.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of clinical observations, laboratory tests, and modern medical technologies to understand the patient's condition. They followed a step-by-step procedure to identify the underlying cause of the patient's heart condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A sudden onset of cardiac damage is observed in a patient with a rare anatomical variation of the heart's blood supply, and the link between this variation and a viral infection is investigated to explain the triggering event.
descriptions.approach: The patient's medical history, lab results, and imaging data are analyzed to trace the sequence of events, with a focus on identifying patterns between a known infectious agent and the timing of tissue damage.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Adaptive behaviour and learning in slime moulds: the role of oscillations

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the role of a specific pattern in the brain-like network of a certain type of living being, which uses information from past experiences to adjust its behavior. It compares this pattern to the brain's own way of organizing activity.
descriptions.approach: The researchers describe the network's behavior and its patterns of activity, and then explore how these patterns might be related to learning and memory. They use this information to evaluate the network's ability to process information and sustain learning.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system adapts its structure and dynamics based on past interactions, adjusting how information flows through interconnected pathways in response to environmental inputs.
descriptions.approach: The system maintains and modifies internal patterns of activity across a network, where the timing and synchronization of these patterns influence how information is processed and stored over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Market Allocations under Ambiguity: A Survey [Allocations des biens et ambiguïté : une revue de la littérature]

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of uncertainty on market behavior, comparing theoretical models of decision-making under uncertainty to experimental evidence. It aims to explain how these models affect the optimal arrangement of resources in a competitive market setting.
descriptions.approach: The researchers start with a theoretical result and test its applicability to a competitive market. They then explore the implications of these models on market behavior, including the potential for non-revelation of information and optimal arrangements.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system predicts how agents choose among options when they lack precise knowledge of outcomes, and how these choices affect overall market outcomes and information sharing.
descriptions.approach: It models agent behavior using two rules: one where decisions average outcomes with varying confidence, and another where agents pick the most favorable outcome among possible beliefs. It then simulates how these rules influence group-level decisions and market dynamics over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of the new ring system benzo[ f ]pyrimido[1,2- d ][1,2,3]triazolo[1,5- a ][1,4]diazepine and its cycloalkane and cycloalkene condensed analogues

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new compound against five types of cancer cells, comparing its performance to that of existing treatments. It aims to identify the compound's potential as a new cancer treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of chemical synthesis and biological testing to evaluate the compound's properties. They applied a specific reaction sequence to create the new compound and then tested its effects on cancer cells.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A new fused ring structure is designed and synthesized, with its biological effect measured across multiple cancer cell types to assess its ability to inhibit uncontrolled cell growth.
descriptions.approach: A reaction pathway is reversed to build the target structure efficiently, and the resulting compounds are evaluated for their impact on cell survival under conditions mimicking disease progression.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Discovery of Host-Directed Antiviral Therapies

descriptions.problem: This work aims to identify the key interactions between a pathogen and its host, in order to find potential therapeutic targets. It estimates the impact of these interactions on the pathogen's ability to infect and replicate within the host.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a technique to 'knock out' specific genes in host cells, allowing researchers to study the effects on the pathogen. The results are then combined with data from patients and medical records to identify potential treatments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to identify key host components that influence the replication and spread of a pathogen in living systems, by measuring how changes in host biology affect pathogen behavior across different biological contexts.
descriptions.approach: A systematic perturbation method is applied to living systems to test how altering specific host elements affects pathogen dynamics. Results are analyzed using computational models to predict outcomes and link genetic variations to biological effects in real-world health data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: How the wisdom of crowds, and of the crowd within, are affected by expertise

descriptions.problem: This research investigates how the accuracy of individual predictions is affected by the level of expertise and the amount of data considered. It aims to understand how combining multiple predictions from experts or non-experts impacts the overall accuracy.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a numerical estimation task where participants estimate the number of objects they see. They compare individual predictions to those of groups of participants and to expert predictions, and optimize their approach by providing feedback and adjusting their strategy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The accuracy of individual predictions is evaluated and compared to the performance of a group of similar predictions, especially when individuals have refined their judgment through experience.
descriptions.approach: Predictions are collected and combined across individuals, but only if individual responses show meaningful variation. When variation is minimal, the group's performance is improved by including diverse, independent judgments rather than repeating the same outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Caveat Emptor Doesn’t Cut It

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of international medical services on the health and safety of patients in host countries, compares the economic benefits to the potential risks and drawbacks, and optimizes the allocation of resources to ensure equitable access to medical services.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves analyzing the relationships between economic disparities, cultural differences, and the provision of medical services, using data on international medical services, economic indicators, and cultural norms to inform the analysis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine the responsibility for outcomes when services are delivered across borders, especially when those services involve high-risk interventions and are influenced by financial incentives and cultural differences.
descriptions.approach: A framework compares risk distribution, legal jurisdiction, and cultural context across regions, using patterns of service delivery, financial arrangements, and patient outcomes to assess accountability and equity in decision-making.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Facial Nerve Paralysis Treatment and Research
title: Effectiveness of Early Electrical Neuromuscular Stimulation in Functional Recovery of the Facial Nerve after Excision of Benign Superficial Lobe Lesions of the Parotid Gland

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine if a specific therapy can help recover a common complication after a surgical procedure, and whether it can be done safely and effectively at home. It estimates the recovery rate of a specific function after the therapy is applied.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a therapy that sends electrical signals to help a specific function recover, and they tested it on a group of patients who had a similar surgical procedure. They compared the results to a group of patients who did not receive the therapy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The rate of functional recovery in a specific neural pathway is measured over time and compared to a baseline group that did not receive intervention.
descriptions.approach: Patients receive a consistent, timed external signal applied immediately after surgery, with recovery progress assessed at multiple time points using standardized functional scoring.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Comparative Epigenome-Wide Analysis Highlights Placenta-Specific Differentially Methylated Regions

descriptions.problem: This work compares the patterns of changes in the way genes are turned on or off in a specific type of tissue to another type of tissue. It aims to understand the unique characteristics of this tissue by comparing its patterns to those of another tissue.
descriptions.approach: The researchers compared the patterns of changes in the way genes are turned on or off in 444 samples of this specific type of tissue with 444 samples of another type of tissue. They used a computer program to identify patterns that were unique to this tissue.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of biological regions is analyzed for changes in chemical modification patterns across two related tissues, with the goal of identifying functional associations linked to specific cellular processes.
descriptions.approach: A computational model compares modification levels across tissue samples, then maps these patterns to known biological functions using statistical enrichment analysis to detect significant associations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Market Research and Design of a New Dental Medical Vehicle Based on Digital Technology

descriptions.problem: A system estimates public interest in mobile health services that provide accessible medical care in underserved locations, using feedback from user surveys and geographic usage patterns.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates potential routes and service frequencies by analyzing population density, travel behavior, and demand signals to determine the most effective deployment strategy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Chronotoxicity of Semen Strychni is associated with circadian metabolism and transport in mice

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the toxicity of a substance in two different groups of subjects over time, comparing the levels of a toxic compound in their bodies and determining the impact of their natural rhythms on this compound's levels and breakdown. It also compares the effectiveness of different dosing times.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of experiments to study the effects of the substance on the subjects' bodies, including measuring the levels of toxic compounds in their blood and urine, and analyzing the breakdown of these compounds in different parts of their bodies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The timing of exposure to a compound influences its biological effects and systemic availability, with peak adverse outcomes occurring at specific times of day and reduced effects at others, depending on biological rhythms.
descriptions.approach: Exposure is administered at various times, and the resulting concentration in blood and tissue is measured. The rate of breakdown and removal of the compound is assessed across time points, revealing patterns tied to internal biological timing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Health Promotion Among Home-Dwelling Elderly Individuals in Turkey

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify and describe the most effective health-promotion practices for individuals who need support with daily tasks and maintaining their physical, mental, and emotional well-being. It estimates the benefits of these practices on the quality of life and cost-effectiveness.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a holistic approach, considering physical, social, spiritual, and cultural resources, and applies a positive model to support individual health and coping. It follows a procedure that involves analyzing data on health-promotion practices and their outcomes, and optimising these practices for maximum benefit.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to predict and optimize well-being outcomes for individuals living independently, based on social, environmental, and personal resource availability.
descriptions.approach: It evaluates patterns in daily support networks and service usage, then applies a holistic framework that strengthens resilience by integrating physical, emotional, and social inputs to promote long-term stability and adaptive functioning.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Participative modelling of a micro insurance scheme for African swine fever (ASF) in a peri-urban pig farming (PF) in Kinshasa, democratic republic of Congo (DRC)

descriptions.problem: Estimate the average number of animals lost annually due to a serious health risk, and compare the costs of losses to the total value of the affected animals. The data should be based on historical records and expert opinions.
descriptions.approach: Use a mathematical model to calculate the average number of animals lost, and then apply a formula to estimate the costs of losses based on the total value of the affected animals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is estimated that assigns financial risk exposure to small and large agricultural units based on loss frequency and unit size, using historical data on production decline and economic impact.
descriptions.approach: A two-part risk-sharing model is applied: one assigns 90% risk coverage to small units and 60% to large units, with compensation thresholds adjusted to reflect unit vulnerability and recovery timelines.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Using an Artificial Real-Time Response Audience in Online Sales Education to Improve Self-Efficacy in Sales Presentations: An Online Classroom Innovation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of using AI technology to help people improve their ability to deliver presentations confidently and effectively, by comparing the results of students who used AI technology with those who did not.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a statistical test to compare the results of two groups, and then used the results to explain how AI technology can be used to improve people's confidence in delivering presentations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how well an individual performs in real-time verbal communication by analyzing and adjusting vocal characteristics such as tone, rhythm, and intensity during a performance.
descriptions.approach: The system generates a responsive, interactive feedback loop that mimics human behavior in real time, adjusting vocal parameters based on observed patterns and providing immediate, personalized guidance to improve performance quality.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Microtia: A Data Linkage Study of Epidemiology and Implications for Service Delivery

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the number of cases of a birth defect in a specific population over a long period, comparing the results to a larger population. It also compares the characteristics of patients who received different types of treatment for this defect.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a method called data linkage to combine data from different sources, such as birth records and medical records, to identify patients with the defect. They then analyzed the data to identify patterns and trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rate is estimated for a condition occurring in live births over time and space, and differences in access to a medical procedure are assessed across various personal and geographic factors.
descriptions.approach: Patient records are linked across databases to identify individuals with a diagnosis and their procedural history. Groupings are formed based on procedure type and personal attributes, then compared across demographic and location-based variables.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Measurement and Crosstalk Analysis of Hexagonal TSV Bundle in 3D ICs

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of a specific type of connection in a complex device, comparing the results of measurements and calculations to determine the best design. It also compares the performance of different types of connections to identify the most effective one.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of measurements and calculations to analyze the connection. They extract the necessary information from the measurements and use it to validate their calculations, which are based on a mathematical model of the connection's behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The performance of a multi-conductor system is evaluated under electromagnetic coupling, comparing signal integrity across adjacent channels with and without a grounded reference structure. Return and insertion losses are measured and modeled across a wide frequency range.
descriptions.approach: Electromagnetic field distributions are computed and validated against experimental data. A de-embedding technique is applied to isolate segment-level behavior, and coupling effects are quantified through field-based analysis across frequency bands.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pengaruh Penambahan Jahe (Zingiber Officinale) Pada Sirup Rosella (Hibiscus Sabdariffa l.) Terhadap Tingkat Kesukaan Konsumen

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of adding a certain ingredient to a drink on consumer preference, comparing different levels of the ingredient to see which one is most preferred. It also explains why the addition of the ingredient affects some parameters but not others.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a controlled experiment with multiple groups, each with a different amount of the ingredient added. The results are analyzed using statistical tests to determine if there is a significant difference between the groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment is made to determine how varying amounts of a natural additive influence consumer perception of a liquid product across sensory attributes such as visual appeal, flavor, and scent.
descriptions.approach: A controlled experiment is designed with multiple dosage levels, each tested in random order across a group of evaluators. Differences in preference are statistically evaluated using variance analysis and post-hoc comparisons to identify the most favored condition.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Integral imaging display with enhanced depth of field based on bifocal lens array

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the depth of a 3D object from a set of 2D images, and compares the results to a conventional method. It aims to optimise the depth of field by combining two reconstructed images.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a combination of two lens arrays with different shapes to create two central depth regions. The reconstructed images are then compared to estimate the depth of the 3D object.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system reconstructs a three-dimensional scene by combining views from two distinct depth layers, producing a more immersive and detailed spatial representation than standard methods.
descriptions.approach: A structured optical element divides incoming light into two spatial patterns, each focused on a different depth range, then merges the resulting views into a unified spatial output using alignment and spatial mapping.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Predicting the Presence and Abundance of Bacterial Taxa in Environmental Communities through Flow Cytometric Fingerprinting

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the presence and abundance of certain types of microorganisms in a community, using data from a variety of sources. It compares these estimates to data from other sources, such as observations of the community's behavior, to improve accuracy.
descriptions.approach: The research uses a combination of machine learning models to analyze data from a type of laboratory equipment that measures the size and properties of individual microorganisms. It follows a two-stage process: first, a model predicts whether a certain type of microorganism is present, and second, a model predicts how abundant it is.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the presence and quantity of specific microbial groups in a mixed community based on physical and chemical traits measured in real-time across time.
descriptions.approach: A two-step model first determines whether a group is present using pattern recognition in measured traits, then estimates its relative quantity using statistical relationships derived from known trait-group associations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Targeting CD8 + T Cell Immunopathology to Improve Survival of Viral Pneumonia in Mice

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the impact of a specific treatment on the outcome of a disease, comparing the effects of different treatments on a group of subjects. It predicts the outcome of a disease based on the treatment and the characteristics of the subjects.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves administering a treatment to a group of subjects, then analyzing the effect of the treatment on the outcome of the disease. The approach follows a rule: if the treatment is administered early, it may worsen the outcome, but if it is administered late, it may improve it.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The extent and timing of a specific immune cell population's infiltration into infected lung tissue is measured to determine its impact on disease progression and outcome.
descriptions.approach: A treatment is administered at a defined time point after infection, and the number of immune cells in the lung is quantified at a later stage to assess changes in cellular response and disease outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Comprehensive dielectric performance of alternately doped BST multilayer films coated with strontium titanate thin layers

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the performance of a specific type of material used in energy storage and microwave applications. It estimates and compares the properties of this material under different conditions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created a new material by combining two other materials in a specific order and using a modified process. They then studied the material's structure and properties using various techniques, such as X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's ability to store and release energy efficiently while minimizing unwanted energy loss is evaluated under varying electrical conditions and structural constraints.
descriptions.approach: A layered structure is engineered with controlled atomic substitutions and interface layers to balance conductivity, energy retention, and signal integrity across frequency ranges.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Cancer, Stress, Anesthesia, and Immune Response
title: Effects of Systemic Lidocaine on Postoperative Recovery Quality and Immune Function in Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Radical Gastrectomy

descriptions.problem: A quantity representing patient well-being is measured over time and compared across three treatment groups to determine how different dosing levels affect recovery speed and immune response after a surgical procedure.
descriptions.approach: Patients are assigned to one of three groups with varying doses of a substance administered intravenously. Outcomes are tracked using standardized scores and biological markers, and recovery timelines are analyzed using statistical modeling to detect differences in recovery patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Local structural heterogeneity induced large flexoelectricity in Sm-doped PMN–PT ceramics

descriptions.problem: This work investigates the relationship between a certain property of materials and the amount of a specific element added to them. It aims to understand how this element affects the property and whether it can be used to create materials with a certain characteristic.
descriptions.approach: The researchers prepared several samples of a material with a specific element added and measured the effect of the element on the material's property. They compared the results to understand the relationship between the element and the property.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's ability to generate an electrical response under mechanical strain is measured across different compositions. The strength of this response is compared across variants and linked to the degree of variation in local atomic arrangements.
descriptions.approach: A systematic variation in composition is applied to induce structural irregularities. The resulting electrical output is monitored and correlated with the complexity of atomic-scale variations in the material's structure.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: DC-STGCN: Dual-Channel Based Graph Convolutional Networks for Network Traffic Forecasting

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the future state of a complex system with many interconnected parts, using historical data to make predictions about its behavior over time. It aims to improve the accuracy of these predictions by capturing the relationships between the system's parts.
descriptions.approach: The model uses a combination of two main components: one extracts patterns in the system's behavior over time, and the other captures the relationships between the system's parts. It then uses these patterns to make predictions about the system's future state.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates future patterns in a dynamic process influenced by both repeating daily and weekly cycles, and spatial relationships among entities. It analyzes sequences of observations over time and across interconnected units to predict future values with high accuracy.
descriptions.approach: It splits the data into two temporal streams, each processed through a module that captures local and global relationships. A recurrent unit refines temporal patterns, while a dual-path mechanism separately models connectivity and proximity-based dependencies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Intertemporal Utility with Heterogeneous Goods and Constant Elasticity of Substitution

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal way to allocate resources over time, considering how different things change in value over time and how they can be substituted for each other. It predicts the best way to make decisions about how to use resources now and in the future.
descriptions.approach: It uses mathematical models to find the optimal way to allocate resources, following a procedure that involves comparing different options and choosing the best one. The model is based on a set of rules that ensure consistency and simplicity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A model predicts how preferences evolve over time across different types of resources, balancing consumption choices that vary in nature and timing. It determines when and how decisions today affect future choices, based on observed patterns in resource use and time preferences.
descriptions.approach: The model evaluates how choices across time and types of resources are linked through a consistent rule. If choices are made uniformly across time or follow a simple power law, the pattern is stable and predictable across all time periods.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 하부 구조의 고유 진동수비에 따른 돔 구조의 고유 진동 특성에 관한 연구

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the natural oscillations of a complex system, comparing the effects of different lower-level components on the overall system's behavior. It predicts how changes in the lower-level components' stiffness will influence the system's natural frequencies.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a mathematical model to analyze the system's behavior, controlling the stiffness of the lower-level components to study their impact. They identify the most dominant modes of oscillation for different angles and stiffness levels.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system's dynamic response is assessed under varying stiffness conditions of a supporting base, to determine how the overall behavior changes with the base's rigidity.
descriptions.approach: A model is built where the base's stiffness is adjusted systematically, and the resulting frequency response of the entire system is computed, revealing shifts in dominant motion patterns based on the base's rigidity level.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Homophily dynamics outweigh network topology in an extended Axelrod’s Cultural Dissemination Model

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of different network structures on the spread of cultural features in a group, comparing the outcomes of different models. It predicts how the structure of the group's relationships affects the spread of ideas over time.
descriptions.approach: The model uses a set of traits to define the features of the culture, and applies this to empirical data on people's attitudes. It tests different network structures and compares the results to see which has the most influence on the spread of ideas.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The evolution of group beliefs is studied based on interactions among individuals, using observed patterns from structured surveys. The outcome focuses on how shared traits spread and stabilize across a group, regardless of the specific connections between individuals.
descriptions.approach: Individuals update their beliefs by aligning with neighbors who share similar traits. The process runs over time, and results are compared across different connection patterns, showing that shared similarities dominate over structural links.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Meckel's diverticulum causing simultaneous hemoperitoneum and hematochezia

descriptions.problem: An estimate or prediction is made about the likelihood of a specific condition (a pouch-like protrusion in the digestive tract) causing two types of bleeding (bright red and dark) in a patient. This prediction is based on data from previous cases.
descriptions.approach: A general discussion is conducted to understand the variability and diversity of this condition, following the presentation of a specific case.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rare condition is identified where a single abnormal structure causes two distinct types of external fluid loss from the same internal source, one through the digestive tract and one into the abdominal cavity.
descriptions.approach: The system monitors physiological signals over time and detects a pattern where two separate output events originate from a shared internal anomaly, using temporal and spatial consistency to infer a singular underlying cause.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Learning in 3D: Adjusting and Assessing an Introductory Biology 3D Printing Project for Virtual Learning

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a 3D printing project in teaching students about the structure-function relationships of biological entities. It compares the results of different versions of the project, with and without hands-on manipulation, to assess their impact on learning outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The project involves three steps: researching a biological entity, designing a 3D printed learning aid, and presenting a learning module incorporating hands-on manipulation. The approach follows a procedure of designing, testing, and refining the project to improve learning outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A learning activity is designed to help learners connect the structural features of complex biological systems to their functional roles, using hands-on or digital representations.
descriptions.approach: Learners investigate a system, create a tangible or digital model to represent its components, and present their understanding through interactive manipulation or explanation to peers.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: PEMIKIRAN FAISAL TEHRANI BERDASARKAN NOVEL-NOVEL PILIHAN

descriptions.problem: This study estimates and explains the common themes and ideas expressed in a set of 6 works, comparing and contrasting them to identify patterns and trends in the author's writing.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a qualitative approach, involving an in-depth reading of each work to identify and analyze the underlying ideas and concepts, and to compare and contrast them across the different works.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of recurring ideas across a sequence of works is identified and categorized by theme, including socio-political, religious, and personal perspectives, based on textual content from multiple sources.
descriptions.approach: Each work is examined through detailed analysis to extract and group central concerns, then compared across time and context to detect consistent and evolving thematic trends in the underlying intellectual framework.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Arsenii Vetushko-Kalevich, Compilation and Translation: Johannes Widekindi and the Origins of his Work on a Swedish-Russian War, Studia Graeca et Latina Lundensia 26 (Lund: Lunds universitet 2019). 219 s.

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the origins of a historical event, comparing different sources of information to determine the most likely explanation. It also explains the context and significance of the event.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses a combination of historical texts and other evidence to build a narrative about the event. They follow a step-by-step procedure to evaluate and synthesize the information, ultimately producing a coherent and well-supported account.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A historical narrative is reconstructed from fragmented records to explain the emergence of a geopolitical account involving two major powers and a contested boundary region.
descriptions.approach: A systematic review of surviving documents is performed, cross-referencing linguistic patterns, temporal sequences, and regional references to infer the development of a formalized account from earlier, informal sources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Ripening Response of Sugarcane Varieties to Chemical Ripeners and Economic Benefits during the Early Period of Harvesting at Wonji-Shoa and Metahara Sugarcane Plantations, Central Rift Valley of Ethiopia

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of different treatments on the growth and yield of a certain crop, comparing the results to a control. It predicts the optimal treatment for a specific condition, and explains the economic benefits of each treatment.
descriptions.approach: The experiment uses a combination of different crop varieties and treatments, with multiple replications to ensure accuracy. The results are compared to a control, and the treatment with the highest benefit is identified.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The performance of different crop varieties under environmental stress is assessed to determine how effectively they can increase yield and quality when exposed to specific chemical treatments.
descriptions.approach: A factorial design applies treatments to multiple crop types across different environmental conditions, measuring outcomes like growth, output, and economic return through controlled field trials with repeated observations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Enzymatic Synthesis of alpha‐Ketobutyrate from Methionine: Characterization of Methionine gamma lyase deaminase (Mgld) from Porphyromonas gingivalis

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the rate of a chemical reaction, compares the efficiency of different substrates, and optimizes the conditions for the reaction to occur. It explains the underlying mechanisms and identifies the most rate-limiting steps.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of experimental methods, including spectroscopy and kinetic analysis, to study the reaction. They also used computational models to simulate the reaction and predict the activation energies for different steps.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A biochemical transformation converts a sulfur-containing amino acid into a four-carbon keto acid, with reaction progress monitored through spectral shifts indicating intermediate states. Kinetic performance varies across substrates, and the rate depends on the stability of a key reaction intermediate.
descriptions.approach: A purified enzyme catalyzes the conversion through a sequence of proton transfers and bond breakages. Reaction rates are measured under varying conditions, and a linear relationship is established between observed speed and computed energy barriers for bond rupture in the transition state.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Double ‐ Stranded RNA Analog Poly I:C Enhances the Expression of Lectin‐Like Oxidized LDL Receptor‐1 in Macrophages: Role of ERK1/2 Signaling

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a viral mimic on the activity of a specific receptor in cells, comparing the results to a control condition. It predicts the role of a particular pathway in the pathogenesis of a disease.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a specific molecule to stimulate cells, observing how it affects the activity of a receptor. They then tested the effect of blocking this pathway, confirming the role of the pathway in the disease process.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A stimulus is applied to cells, and the resulting increase in a receptor-mediated response is measured over time and at varying strengths. The effect is evaluated across different cellular conditions and inhibited by a specific blocker to determine its dependence on a particular intracellular pathway.
descriptions.approach: A cellular response is triggered by a synthetic RNA analog, and its effect is monitored through downstream gene activity. The response is suppressed by a targeted inhibitor, and genetic reduction of a key kinase pathway confirms its role in amplifying the effect.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Relationship between physical activity time and intramuscular adipose tissue content of the thigh muscle groups of younger and older men

descriptions.problem: This study investigates the relationship between the amount of time spent being physically active and the amount of fat stored in the leg area of people who are not yet elderly and those who are. It aims to understand how much fat is stored in the leg area when people are moderately active.
descriptions.approach: The researchers measured the size of the leg area using a special machine and the amount of time spent being physically active using a device that tracks movement. They compared the results to see if there was a connection between the amount of physical activity and the amount of fat stored in the leg area.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The amount of fat stored within a specific bodily region is assessed across individuals with varying levels of movement intensity over time, and compared between groups with different movement patterns.
descriptions.approach: Movement intensity is tracked using wearable sensors, and movement duration is segmented into defined activity levels. Fat content in the region is measured non-invasively, and statistical relationships are evaluated between movement duration and fat accumulation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Xanthoma of Tendoachilles: Management and Follow-Up

descriptions.problem: A rare growth of abnormal cells and fatty deposits is estimated to be present in a specific area of the body, likely associated with a genetic disorder that affects the body's ability to process a certain type of fat. This growth is compared to a known condition that affects the same area.
descriptions.approach: A patient's symptoms and test results are used to determine the presence and severity of the growth, and to predict the outcome of a treatment. The treatment involves surgically removing the growth and repairing the damaged area, and the patient's progress is monitored over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A persistent, localized mass in soft tissue is observed and monitored over time to assess its stability and response to intervention.
descriptions.approach: A treatment plan is initiated based on laboratory indicators of metabolic imbalance, followed by surgical removal and tissue reinforcement. Post-intervention recovery is tracked through functional assessments and long-term observation for recurrence.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Green, Closed Loop, Circular Bio-Economy

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how effectively resources are reused and recycled across different stages of production and consumption to reduce dependency on new inputs and minimize material loss.
descriptions.approach: A model tracks the flow of materials through various stages, assigning value to by-products and reusing them in new processes, adjusting operations to maximize retention and minimize loss over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Mechanism of obesity suppression by adipose tissue creatine energetics

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a specific enzyme on the energy production in a type of fat cell, and compares it to the effect of a lack of a specific nutrient on the same process. It also optimizes the understanding of how a particular molecule regulates energy production in these cells.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use genetic experiments to study the role of a specific enzyme in regulating energy production in fat cells. They compare the effects of the enzyme and the nutrient on the cells' energy production and identify the key molecule involved.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's response to high-energy input is measured and compared under different stimulation conditions to determine how energy dissipation is regulated in metabolic tissues.
descriptions.approach: A specific enzyme isoform is identified as central to energy dissipation in response to stimulation. Its activity is quantified in isolated cellular compartments and linked to metabolic output under varying conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Performance, carcass and internal organs characterizes of broiler chickens with phytase supplementation from Burkholderia sp. Strain HF.7

descriptions.problem: A system's output mass and internal tissue composition are measured across different dietary treatments to assess performance and physiological balance.
descriptions.approach: A controlled experiment applies varying nutritional inputs to a group of animals over time, then evaluates resulting body mass and organ proportionality using standardized measurement protocols.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: Uncialamycin-based antibody–drug conjugates: Unique enediyne ADCs exhibiting bystander killing effect

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new type of compound that kills cells, and compares it to a control. It predicts how well the compound will work in different situations, and optimizes its design to make it more effective.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of chemical reactions and experiments to create and test the compound. They follow a procedure that involves creating the compound, testing its effects on cells, and adjusting its design to make it more effective and selective.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to deliver a potent cytotoxic payload selectively to cells expressing a specific surface marker, with the ability to kill neighboring cells that do not express the marker.
descriptions.approach: A payload is attached to a targeting molecule via a bond that can be broken under specific conditions. The system is evaluated for its ability to kill cells in a microenvironment where only a subset of cells express the target.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Structuring clinical text with AI: Old versus new natural language processing techniques evaluated on eight common cardiovascular diseases

descriptions.problem: This work aims to extract useful information from unstructured text about common health conditions, and to improve the accuracy of codes used to describe these conditions. It does this by comparing the text to a set of known codes and predicting which codes are most likely to be correct.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a combination of old and new techniques to analyze the text, and then using a statistical model to predict the correct codes. The model is tested on two different sets of data to see how well it generalizes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to infer structured labels from unstructured narrative records, predicting specific disease categories based on textual content and evaluating performance across diverse datasets.
descriptions.approach: A set of text representations is generated from narrative inputs, then used to assign labels via a linear model. Key terms in predictions are identified to ensure clinical relevance, and performance is assessed across different data sources with consistent labeling outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: "Sclerostin in Oral Tissues: Distribution, Biological Functions and Potential Therapeutic Role"

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the distribution and biological functions of a hormone in specific parts of the body, and to predict its potential role in preventing or treating a certain condition. It also compares the hormone's effects in different groups of people.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from various studies to identify patterns and relationships between the hormone and its effects. They then used a mathematical model to analyze and predict the hormone's behavior in different situations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of protein expression is mapped across a biological sample, and its functional impact is assessed in response to varying environmental or physiological conditions.
descriptions.approach: A computational model analyzes spatial and contextual data to infer how a molecular factor influences cellular behavior, using known interactions and observed changes to predict outcomes under different scenarios.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Control of tissue development and cell diversity by cell cycle-dependent transcriptional filtering

descriptions.problem: This work estimates how changes in the time it takes for a population to grow affect the diversity of different types of individuals within that population. It also compares these estimates to data from individual organisms to see if the patterns hold.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use mathematical models to simulate how changes in growth rate might influence the variety of different types of individuals. They then compare their predictions to real-world data from individual organisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how temporal dynamics of division timing influence the diversity and proportions of distinct tissue states during growth.
descriptions.approach: It models how the timing of division events affects the output of long molecular products, simulating how variation in division speed alters the stability and persistence of different tissue states over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A New Design of Smart Plug for Real-time IoT Malware Detection

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a device being compromised by a cyber-attack based on its energy usage patterns. It compares these patterns to known normal patterns to determine if the device is at risk.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a universal model to compare the device's energy usage patterns to a set of known normal patterns. It then optimizes the model to detect anomalies in real-time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system continuously monitors and analyzes behavioral patterns from a networked device to identify deviations that indicate unauthorized or anomalous activity.
descriptions.approach: It collects real-time signals from a device’s physical operation, processes them through a set of defined thresholds, and compares the resulting patterns against known baseline behaviors to detect inconsistencies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The pantropical moss Plagiomnium rhynchophorum (Mniaceae) disjunct to the Southern Appalachians and Hawaii

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the genetic relationships between different species of plants, compares their genetic and morphological characteristics, and optimizes the classification of these species. It explains the genetic origins of these species and how they combine the genomes of other species.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of genetic and morphological data to identify the genetic relationships between the species. They compare the genetic and morphological characteristics of the species and use this information to optimize their classification.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of genetic similarity is identified across geographically separated populations, suggesting shared ancestry despite distinct environmental conditions. The relationship between populations is assessed using molecular markers and morphological traits to determine whether they share a common origin or represent independent evolutionary events.
descriptions.approach: Genetic data from multiple loci are analyzed to detect shared alleles and hybrid signatures. Population traits are compared across locations using a set of diagnostic markers to infer lineage origins and hybridization events.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Chemical evolution of shallow and deep groundwaters in a Triassic sandstone aquifer (Buntsandstein), SW-Germany

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the chemical composition of water in a specific geological formation, comparing it to the composition of the surrounding rocks. It predicts the levels of certain substances in the water based on the formation's properties.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data from the formation's rocks and the water's chemical composition to make these predictions. They follow a procedure that involves analyzing the data, applying mathematical models, and drawing conclusions about the water's chemical state.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is analyzed to track how chemical compositions change as fluids move through layered rock formations over long periods, comparing fluid properties at different depths and flow rates.
descriptions.approach: Fluids pass through distinct rock layers with varying chemical interactions; at each stage, the concentration of key ions is measured and modeled based on dissolution, precipitation, and transport dynamics over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Building National Branding Strategy in Medical Tourism and Production of Generic Medicines

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the potential of a country to improve its international influence and attract investment by linking its name with high-quality products or services. It compares the country's current situation with the desired outcome and identifies the necessary policies to achieve the goal.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing data on the country's products or services and their international reputation, and then using this information to identify the necessary policies to improve the country's influence and attract investment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A country assesses its ability to attract patients seeking specialized healthcare services and to establish a recognized identity for its production of affordable, widely available health products.
descriptions.approach: The analysis evaluates the alignment between healthcare accessibility, service quality, and production efficiency, using data on patient flow, treatment outcomes, and supply chain performance to identify strategic synergies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Enhancing Thermal Properties of Steam Turbine Blades by Coating with Nanomaterials

descriptions.problem: An object is being tested for its ability to withstand high temperatures, and the goal is to find the best material to use to protect it. The object is being tested under conditions that are similar to how it will be used in real life.
descriptions.approach: A material is being mixed with other substances to create a new material, and then it is applied to the object being tested. The object is then tested to see how well the new material protects it from high temperatures.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's ability to retain structural integrity under high-temperature exposure is evaluated across multiple compositional variants to identify the most effective formulation.
descriptions.approach: A layered formulation is applied to a surface, with variable proportions of two components adjusted in a controlled environment. Performance is measured under sustained thermal stress, and the variant demonstrating optimal stability under those conditions is selected.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: M01 as a novel drug enhancer for specifically targeting the blood-brain barrier.

descriptions.problem: A small molecule is identified that transiently disrupts the tight junctions between endothelial cells, enabling passage of small therapeutic agents through a protective cellular barrier.
descriptions.approach: The molecule binds selectively to a conserved region of a key junctional protein, weakening cell-to-cell adhesion. This triggers internalization and reduced expression of the protein, creating a temporary opening for controlled transport of substances.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: An update to the definition of zero wave overtopping in floods and reservoir safety

descriptions.problem: A threshold is estimated to distinguish between negligible and detectable surface water crossing a barrier under specified flow conditions, based on repeated observations of water behavior under controlled and variable input conditions.
descriptions.approach: A statistical rule is applied to observed surface behavior under varying input intensities, using a normalized metric derived from repeated trials to define a boundary where surface crossing is considered negligible.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Effects of Providing Childcare on Grandmothers’ Employment and Mental Health in Japan, 日本で孫の育児が祖母の就業とメンタルヘルスに及ぼす影響

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of providing care to young children on the ability to work and the mental health of older adults, using data from a large survey of adults aged 50-59. It compares the outcomes of those who provide care to those who do not.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a statistical model to analyze the data, controlling for individual differences that do not change over time. They then apply this model to the data to estimate the effect of providing care on working hours and mental health.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A model estimates how the time and energy devoted to supporting a dependent family member affects an individual's work engagement and psychological well-being, using repeated observations over time from a large, representative group of adults.
descriptions.approach: The model compares patterns of work participation and emotional strain across individuals who provide care and those who do not, adjusting for stable personal characteristics to isolate the effect of caregiving responsibilities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Significant Publications on Infectious Diseases Pharmacotherapy in 2020

descriptions.problem: Estimate the most influential articles published in 2020, considering their impact on a specific area of medical research. Identify the most significant publications from a large dataset of nominated articles.
descriptions.approach: Analyze a large dataset of nominated articles, then conduct a survey of a large group of experts to determine the top articles. The results are then summarized and presented.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of influential scholarly works is identified and ranked based on expert evaluation and collective input from a professional community. The ranking reflects the relative impact and relevance of these works in advancing understanding and practice within a rapidly evolving medical domain.
descriptions.approach: A structured voting mechanism is applied where experts nominate and evaluate a list of works. The most frequently selected and widely recognized works are compiled and presented to highlight key advancements and trends in the field.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Hsa_circ_0014879 regulates the radiosensitivity of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma through miR-519-3p/CDC25A axis

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how a certain type of molecule affects the ability of cancer cells to withstand damage from a treatment. It estimates the impact of this molecule on the cancer cells' ability to grow, migrate, and invade.
descriptions.approach: The researchers measured the levels of this molecule and two other molecules in cancer cells using various techniques. They then tested how these molecules affect the cancer cells' behavior and how they interact with each other.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's response to a stressor is measured across multiple cellular states, including growth, movement, and structural changes, using molecular and functional readouts. The influence of a regulatory RNA on these responses is assessed through its interaction with a microRNA and a downstream protein involved in cell cycle control.
descriptions.approach: A regulatory RNA is shown to sequester a microRNA, preventing it from suppressing a target protein. This interaction is validated through genetic manipulation and functional assays that track changes in cell behavior and molecular expression under stress.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A NEW CONSENSUS STUDY ON THE FUTURE OF NURSING

descriptions.problem: A pattern of future healthcare delivery is estimated based on current trends, expert opinions, and evolving patient needs across multiple healthcare settings.
descriptions.approach: A weighted aggregation of diverse forecasts is computed, adjusting for reliability and consistency, then iteratively refined through consensus review and sensitivity analysis to produce a stable, evidence-informed projection.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Relationship Between Pulmonary Hamartoma and Bronchus: Multislice Spiral Computed Tomography Findings

descriptions.problem: This work investigates the relationship between a specific type of abnormal growth in the lungs and the surrounding airways, estimating the frequency and pattern of this relationship in a large dataset. It aims to explain how these growths affect the airways and whether they can be predicted or optimised.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a type of imaging technology to review images of the lungs and airways, dividing the data into two groups based on the location of the abnormal growths. They then used a specific procedure to classify the relationships between the growths and the airways.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is identified in how a benign lung lesion interacts with nearby airways, based on imaging data. The interaction is classified into five types depending on whether the airway is blocked, compressed, enclosed, or absent.
descriptions.approach: Imaging data is analyzed using cross-sectional views to reconstruct 3D structures. Lesions are categorized by their spatial relationship to airways, with specific rules defining when an airway is cut off, contained, compressed, or not connected.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Artivismo como herramienta de transformacion social

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how communities are creating alternative spaces for living and socializing, and how these initiatives can be used to promote positive change in urban areas.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from university students' discussions and observations of community initiatives to identify patterns and trends in the creation of these alternative spaces.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A social movement is evaluated to determine its effectiveness in fostering collective action and alternative living models in urban environments with limited natural and recreational resources.
descriptions.approach: Community-led initiatives are analyzed through structured dialogues with participants, comparing outcomes across different spatial and demographic settings to assess the impact of collaborative, non-consumptive practices on personal and group well-being.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Bronchodilator Effect of Crataegus azarolus var aronia Unripped Fruit Extracts on Rat’s Tracheal Smooth Muscle

descriptions.problem: This research investigates how different substances affect the muscles in a rat's airway, and whether certain channels in the muscle cells are involved in this effect. It aims to understand how these substances work and what channels are responsible for the response.
descriptions.approach: The researchers tested how different substances affect the muscles in a rat's airway, and used special blockers to see how the channels in the muscle cells respond. They then analyzed the results to understand how the substances work and which channels are involved.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A mechanism is estimated that induces relaxation in airway muscle tissue, with effects mediated by specific ion channels and signaling molecules involved in cellular membrane potential regulation and vascular tone control.
descriptions.approach: A series of compounds are applied to muscle tissue, and responses are measured under conditions where specific ion channels and signaling pathways are inhibited to determine which pathways drive the observed relaxation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: KLF4 transactivates TRIM29 expression and modulates keratin network

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a protein on the expression of another protein, and compares the results of overexpressing the protein to the results of knocking down the protein that is expressed by the protein. It also explains how the protein affects the phosphorylation of a protein that is part of a network.
descriptions.approach: The work uses data from the promoter region of the protein that is expressed by the protein to determine how the protein affects its expression. It then uses data from cells that have been overexpressed or knocked down to compare the effects of the protein on the network of proteins it interacts with.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A factor is identified that increases the expression of a gene involved in cellular structure maintenance, and its effect on cell movement is assessed through interference with that gene.
descriptions.approach: The factor binds to a specific region of the gene's regulatory sequence and enhances its activity. Cellular movement and structural protein modification are monitored under conditions where the gene is either amplified or suppressed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: What is the Role of Mannose-Binding Lectin Gene Polymorphism in the Development of Acute Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis?

descriptions.problem: This study aims to understand how a variation in a specific gene affects the symptoms, treatment response, and long-term outcome of a disease in children. It estimates the frequency of this variation in a group of children with a particular disease and compares it to a group of healthy children.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a technique to identify the variation in the gene and then compared the results to a control group. They looked at various symptoms and test results to see if the variation was associated with any of them.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern in a biological system is assessed to see if it correlates with clinical symptoms, lab markers, or disease progression over time in individuals who have experienced a specific illness.
descriptions.approach: A group of individuals is tested for a particular genetic variant using a molecular technique. Their health outcomes and biomarker levels are then compared across different variants to determine if any association exists.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE AS A FACTOR OF AGRO-FOOD SECTOR DEVELOPMENT IN THE REPUBLIC OF SERBIA

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the importance of unique, traditional practices in a specific area for long-term economic and non-economic benefits. It compares the value of preserving traditional values with the need for sustainable development.
descriptions.approach: The study follows a procedure where experts analyze the benefits of integrating traditional knowledge with new technologies to support sustainable development and long-term economic interests.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how long-standing human practices influence the growth and resilience of rural economic activities, particularly in relation to local resource use and sustainability.
descriptions.approach: A framework maps historical practices to current economic outcomes, assessing how integration of local experience with modern tools affects productivity, investment, and community-based value creation over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: KLF9 suppresses cell growth and induces apoptosis via the AR pathway in androgen-dependent prostate cancer cells

descriptions.problem: A factor is measured that decreases when a stimulus is removed and increases when a stressor is applied, and its effect on growth and survival is assessed across different conditions.
descriptions.approach: The factor's activity is enhanced to inhibit growth and promote death in sensitive cells, and its interaction with a receptor pathway is evaluated by measuring downstream changes in response to varying external signals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: DNA methylation as a tool to explore ageing in wild roe deer populations

descriptions.problem: A quantitative estimate of biological age is derived from molecular markers in cells, comparing it to known life spans across individuals exposed to different environmental conditions.
descriptions.approach: A model is trained on molecular profiles from biological samples, adjusting parameters by sex and environment to predict age-related changes, then identifies key genomic sites where variation patterns differ between sexes and environments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Features of marketing in healthcare (The example of medical tourism for the older adults)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a specific strategy in a particular context, comparing the outcomes of different approaches to understand what works best. It predicts the impact of a particular action on a specific group, based on data from previous studies and original research.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves analyzing data from literature and original research to identify key features of a particular strategy. It then uses this information to optimize the strategy for a specific context, aiming to improve outcomes for a particular group.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of behavior is identified in individuals seeking specialized services across geographic boundaries, based on personal preferences, health goals, and available options. The frequency and nature of such decisions are compared across different populations and service environments.
descriptions.approach: A structured framework maps decisions made by individuals when selecting services based on perceived benefits, accessibility, and personal alignment. This framework evaluates how external influences and personal characteristics shape choices over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Lynx D2.7 Catalogue of relevant legal and regulatory datasets

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the publication status of a large collection of rules and court decisions in a specific geographic region, comparing the completeness and accessibility of these records across different sources.
descriptions.approach: It uses a systematic review of existing records to identify gaps and inconsistencies, then optimizes the data by creating a unified, standardized format for easy access and comparison.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies and organizes official rules and judicial decisions across multiple jurisdictions, tracking their publication status, access conditions, and formats to support consistent retrieval and interpretation.
descriptions.approach: It maps authoritative rulings and regulations into a structured network, linking them through shared criteria, formats, and access policies, enabling automated discovery and cross-jurisdictional comparison.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Investigating immunological interaction between lymphatic filariasis and COVID-19 infection: a preliminary evidence

descriptions.problem: This research investigates the relationship between a certain disease caused by parasites and another disease caused by a virus. It aims to determine if the presence of parasites in a community affects the effectiveness of a treatment for the virus.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected blood samples from people living in areas where parasites are common. They tested the blood for signs of the virus and the parasites, and analyzed the results to see if there was a connection between the two.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A statistical assessment is made to determine whether exposure to a chronic parasitic infection correlates with the presence of an acute infectious response in a shared population.
descriptions.approach: Blood samples are collected and tested for markers of both infections. The frequency of each marker is recorded. A measure of association between the two markers is computed using a ratio-based estimate, with confidence bounds derived from observed frequencies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Advancements in PLL and VCO Technologies
title: High Resolution Asynchronous Digital Event Timer

descriptions.problem: It estimates the exact interval between two distinct occurrences, achieving finer precision than conventional methods, especially when events happen rapidly and must be recorded with sub-nanosecond accuracy.
descriptions.approach: It uses a high-frequency reference signal and a parallel sampling mechanism to resolve tiny time gaps by comparing event timestamps across multiple independent sampling phases.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Alternative Basic Education: teaching and learning of adults through virtual means in Peru

descriptions.problem: This work aims to understand the relationship between the effort put in by instructors and the progress made by learners in a specific type of training, where participants are isolated from their peers. It also seeks to identify which factors contribute most to the learners' success.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a method where they collected data on the learners' progress and the instructors' work, and then analyzed the data to find patterns and connections. They used a statistical test to compare the data and determine the strength of the relationships between the variables.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effectiveness of instructional support in improving learning outcomes for individuals in disadvantaged circumstances is assessed using observed interactions and performance metrics.
