descriptions.approach: A model evaluates how different facets of human engagement—such as emotional connection and digital interaction—relate to learning gains, using statistical analysis to identify which elements most strongly influence progress.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Toward Reconfiguring Sociotechnical Systems Design: Digitally Infused Work Systems and the “Platform-STS”

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of new kinds of work systems that have emerged as a result of digital transformation. It compares these systems to existing ones and suggests ways to improve them.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves identifying a new class of systems that are 'distributed' and governed by market mechanisms, and introducing a design principle called 'redundancy of connectivity' to guide design.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is analyzed to determine how interactions between human actors and digital tools evolve across networks, predicting how performance, resilience, and control shift under decentralized coordination and market-driven incentives.
descriptions.approach: A model maps how connectivity between components increases through multiple, overlapping pathways, with performance evaluated under variable levels of autonomy, feedback, and external influence across dynamic networks.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Automated Detection of Pneumothorax Using Frontal Chest X-rays

descriptions.problem: A system estimates whether an image shows a deviation from normal tissue structure, based on patterns in pixel intensity and spatial arrangement across a two-dimensional visual field.
descriptions.approach: The method identifies boundaries of structured regions using gradient-based edge detection, then analyzes surface texture and intensity variation to classify the image as normal or abnormal using a statistical classifier trained on labeled examples.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: An Andrographolide from Helichrysum caespitium (DC.) Sond. Ex Harv., (Asteraceae) and Its Antimicrobial, Antiquorum Sensing, and Antibiofilm Potentials

descriptions.problem: This study aims to estimate the effectiveness of a compound from a plant extract against certain types of bacteria, and to compare its ability to inhibit the growth of these bacteria and prevent them from forming clusters. The compound is also compared to other substances in terms of its ability to prevent bacteria from producing a certain pigment.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of chemical analysis and biological testing to isolate and purify the compound, and to test its effects on different types of bacteria. The results are compared to other substances and to the effects of the compound on the bacteria's ability to form clusters and produce a certain pigment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A compound is identified and tested for its ability to block communication signals among microorganisms and prevent the formation of structured, protective communities that promote resistance and persistence.
descriptions.approach: The compound is extracted from a plant-based source and evaluated in controlled lab settings using assays that measure inhibition of signal production and suppression of microbial group behavior in response to environmental cues.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Quantification of Semi-Truck Cab Decontamination

descriptions.problem: The effectiveness of various cleaning procedures is assessed across different surface types to determine how well they reduce pathogen load over time, based on measurable signal strength from biological samples.
descriptions.approach: Multiple surface types are exposed to different cleaning protocols, then sampled and analyzed for residual biological activity. Results are compared across surface type and treatment to identify which combinations yield the lowest residual signal.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: An asynchronous P system with a DPLL algorithm for solving a satisfiability problem

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the number of steps required to find a solution to a complex problem, and compares it to the number of steps required by other methods. It predicts the efficiency of a proposed algorithm for finding solutions to a specific type of problem.
descriptions.approach: The algorithm uses a set of rules to find a solution to the problem, and it can work in parallel or sequentially. The approach involves applying the rules in a specific order to find a solution that satisfies the conditions of the problem.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to determine whether a set of logical constraints can be simultaneously satisfied by assigning truth values to a finite set of variables.
descriptions.approach: It processes the constraints in parallel using a rule-based mechanism that iteratively refines candidate assignments, reducing the search space through systematic elimination of inconsistent configurations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Evolution of Gram+ Streptococcus pyogenes has maximized efficiency of the Sortase A cleavage site

descriptions.problem: A system evaluates how efficiently a specific molecular signal is processed by two competing mechanisms in a cellular membrane environment, determining which pathway leads to stable attachment of a surface-bound component.
descriptions.approach: The system tests variations of a key residue in the signal sequence, measuring the outcome of two distinct enzymatic reactions that act on the same substrate but produce different functional results, favoring one over the other based on residue identity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Antipsychotic drug treatment of schizophrenia in later life: Results from the European cross-sectional AMSP study

descriptions.problem: This work investigates how the age of patients affects the selection and amount of a specific type of treatment for a mental health condition, and how this affects the treatment of patients over 65 years old. It also compares different types of treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers looked at data from a large database of patients' treatment records, comparing the treatment given to patients of different ages and sexes. They also reviewed current guidelines for treating patients over 65 years old.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is estimated in how treatment decisions change with patient age and gender, based on observed prescribing behaviors over time.
descriptions.approach: Patient records are analyzed to map treatment choices and levels across age groups, adjusting for gender. Guidelines are reviewed to assess how well they address treatment in older individuals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: GRaNIE and GRaNPA: Inference and evaluation of enhancer-mediated gene regulatory networks applied to study macrophages

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to infer how molecular regulators influence cellular responses across different conditions by linking regulatory elements to downstream outcomes based on observable expression patterns.
descriptions.approach: It integrates chromatin accessibility and expression data across samples, then constructs a network of regulatory relationships. It evaluates the network's predictive accuracy by testing how well it forecasts expression changes in specific cell states.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: COMPARATIVE STUDY OF EDGES OF THERMAL IMAGES USING GRADIENT, LAPLACIAN, CANNY OPERATORS: A CRITICAL REVIEW

descriptions.problem: A system identifies and characterizes boundaries in visual data under low-illumination conditions, evaluating how well different computational techniques extract and preserve structural details in the presence of noise and variation.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of filtering and thresholding operations is applied to input data, using local gradient and curvature analysis to detect transitions, with a focus on preserving fine structural features while suppressing irrelevant variations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Calculation of the Shaping of a Space Umbrella Antenna During Strong Bending of Radial Rods Connected Along Parallels by Tensile Cables

descriptions.problem: An object is bent into a curved shape, and its shape is compared to a given surface. The goal is to estimate the forces acting on the object at specific points, and to determine the stiffness of a material that connects these points.
descriptions.approach: The object is modeled as a series of flexible, inextensible elements connected at nodes. The forces acting on the elements are calculated using a combination of geometric relationships and approximations, and the stiffness of the material is determined by solving a system of nonlinear equations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of interconnected flexible segments is deformed under controlled forces until its structure conforms to a specified curved surface, with the shape determined by the balance of internal forces and geometric constraints at connection points.
descriptions.approach: The deformation of each segment is modeled using known bending functions with quadratic displacement correction. Iterative adjustments compute internal forces at joints until the final shape matches the target surface through local equilibrium and geometric alignment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The United States index of socioeconomic deprivation for individuals (USiDep)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the level of deprivation in individuals, comparing it to their income and other measures related to deprivation. It aims to explain the relationship between deprivation and physical and mental health outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves administering a validated measure to participants, calculating correlations between the measure and other variables, and analyzing the results to identify patterns and associations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A score is estimated for each individual based on self-reported experiences reflecting access to resources, health, and stability. This score is compared across individuals to assess its relationship with health outcomes and other measurable factors like income, education, and physical condition.
descriptions.approach: A short, structured set of questions is used to gather self-reported data. The responses are processed using a standardized scoring system that assigns a value reflecting the level of deprivation, based on patterns in the data and known associations with health outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: In vitro evaluation of antibacterial activity of fluorescein 0.5% eye drops

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine the effectiveness of certain substances in preventing the growth of certain types of microorganisms, and to identify any potential risks or false negatives in diagnostic tests.
descriptions.approach: The researchers tested the substances against a range of microorganisms in a liquid medium, using a method that involves adding a small amount of the substance to a liquid and observing the growth of the microorganisms over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A liquid formulation's effect on microbial growth is assessed under controlled conditions to determine if it suppresses the development of specific pathogens.
descriptions.approach: A series of dilutions are prepared from the liquid formulation and exposed to microbial cultures. Growth is monitored over time to identify the lowest concentration that prevents visible microbial development.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Benchmarking Global Carrier Status in the Airline Industry

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of an airline being a major global carrier based on its fleet size, number of international destinations, and continents served. It aims to provide a basis for assessing an airline's global reach and potential future status.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using three key metrics to gauge an airline's global reach, ranking airlines based on these metrics, and comparing the airline's performance to its competitors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A score is assigned to each entity based on its operational scale, geographic spread, and network diversity to determine its standing among peers in a global network.
descriptions.approach: A composite score is computed by combining fleet size, number of international connections, and continent coverage, with continent coverage weighted more heavily. The entity’s position is then evaluated relative to its immediate neighbors in the ranking to assess its competitive context.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Secondary parkinsonism and normal pressure hydrocephaly because of cranioencephalic trauma: a case report

descriptions.problem: This work investigates the relationship between brain damage and an imbalance in the brain's fluid system, which can lead to symptoms such as urinary incontinence, dementia, and stiffness. It aims to identify the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in improving outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing symptoms and imaging studies to diagnose the condition, and then using a medical procedure to test the brain's fluid system and assess its response to treatment. The goal is to optimize treatment and improve patient outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of neurological symptoms is assessed to determine whether they stem from a disorder involving fluid accumulation in brain cavities, particularly when those symptoms appear after a prior injury.
descriptions.approach: A diagnostic test is performed to evaluate the response to fluid removal; if symptoms improve significantly and persist over time, it suggests the disorder is linked to impaired fluid drainage and reabsorption.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Association between exposure to pesticides and allergic diseases in children and adolescents: a systematic review with meta-analysis

descriptions.problem: A quantitative synthesis estimates the strength of a relationship between environmental exposure and the likelihood of a health condition in young individuals, comparing results across multiple studies to determine consistency and statistical significance.
descriptions.approach: A structured search identifies relevant studies, extracts outcome measures, combines results using statistical weighting, and evaluates the overall effect size while assessing heterogeneity and confidence in the estimate.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Effect of Learning Strategy and Writing Motivation on the Ability to Write Short Texts during Covid-19 Pandemic

descriptions.problem: This research aims to compare the effectiveness of two teaching methods on students' ability to create short texts, and to identify the impact of students' drive to produce these texts on their quality. It also seeks to understand the relationship between the teaching method and the students' drive.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a quantitative approach, comparing the results of two groups of students who received different teaching methods. It employs a pre-test and post-test design, measuring students' ability to create short texts and their drive to produce them.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A difference in performance is estimated between two instructional methods and between individuals with varying levels of engagement in a learning environment, based on observed outcomes and self-reported involvement.
descriptions.approach: Students are assigned to one of two teaching approaches and tracked over time. Performance is measured before and after intervention, and statistical analysis determines whether differences are influenced by the interaction between teaching style and learner engagement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
title: Altered T lymphocyte subtypes and cytokine profiles in follicular fluid associated with diminished ovary reserve

descriptions.problem: A pattern of immune activity is assessed in a fluid surrounding reproductive structures, measuring changes in specific immune cell types and their secreted signaling molecules that may indicate declining biological function.
descriptions.approach: Immune cell populations are categorized and analyzed for activation markers. Signaling molecule levels are measured and linked to cell behavior. A key signal is shown to attract specific immune cells through a known receptor interaction.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Projection Transformation Method for Eliminating Crosstalk in Networked Thermopile Arrays

descriptions.problem: A two-dimensional thermal map is reconstructed from indirect sensor readings affected by unintended signal mixing due to parallel pathways between adjacent elements.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical transformation is applied to align measured signals with a known non-linear response pattern, then iteratively refined to minimize discrepancies between predicted and observed values using local gradient updates.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: SAR and Optical Image Matching Eased on Phase Congruency and Template Matching

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the similarity between images taken from different sources, and it compares them to determine the most accurate match. It aims to improve the matching process by considering the underlying patterns and features in the images.
descriptions.approach: The method uses a template matching procedure to find the most similar area in the entire image. It relies on a non-dimensional metric that focuses on the patterns and features of the images, rather than their light and dark changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system aligns two images taken under different physical conditions, where one has ambiguous brightness and contrast, and the other is clear but sensitive to lighting. It estimates the spatial position where features from one image best correspond to features in the other.
descriptions.approach: It identifies key structural patterns using a metric sensitive to consistent wave-like variations in intensity. It then searches for the best spatial alignment by comparing these patterns across the entire image.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: GASTROPROTECTIVE EFFECT OF STANDARDIZED GINKGO BILOBA EXTRACT (EGB761) AGAINST INDOMETHACIN-INDUCED GASTRIC ULCERS IN RATS

descriptions.problem: A compound's ability to mitigate tissue damage caused by a known irritant is evaluated by measuring changes in oxidative stress markers and inflammatory response indicators in biological samples.
descriptions.approach: A compound is administered before exposure to an irritant, and after a set time, levels of oxidative byproducts, antioxidant enzyme activity, and inflammatory signaling molecules are measured to assess protective effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The “Life” in the Living Law: Law, Emotion and Landscape

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of daily experiences on the collective understanding of a shared concept, which is shaped by the interactions of three key aspects: the physical environment, common sense, and social atmosphere. It compares these aspects to understand the complexity and instability of this concept.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a combination of semantic analysis and case studies to examine the relationships between these aspects. It follows a procedure that involves identifying patterns and meanings in the data, and then using these insights to anticipate the behavior of the concept.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of collective beliefs and spatial patterns is analyzed to understand how human interactions and environmental contexts co-evolve over time, producing observable behaviors and societal responses.
descriptions.approach: A model maps interactions between people and places using observed patterns in daily decisions, identifying feedback loops where environment and behavior mutually influence each other over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Peter Goodrich, Advanced Introduction to Law and Literature (Edward Elgar, Cheltenham, UK and Northampton MA, USA), 2021.pp. 119

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the importance of literature in understanding a particular field, compares it to other related fields, and optimizes the way this field is introduced to new readers. It explains the significance of rhetoric and hermeneutics in this field.
descriptions.approach: The author reviews a new book that provides an introduction to this field, highlighting its key principles and stimulating critical thinking. The review aims to pinpoint essential ideas and offer insights that can help readers understand the subject.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of meaning in structured texts is analyzed to determine how interpretive frameworks influence the understanding of complex societal rules and their underlying motivations.
descriptions.approach: A systematic model maps how narrative elements and rhetorical structures interact to shape interpretations of formal systems, using comparative analysis of textual examples and their contextual applications.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: EPIZOOTIC MONITORING OF AFRICAN SWINE FEVER IN THE SUMY REGION

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the number of cases of a contagious animal disease in a specific geographic area over several years, based on data from testing samples from domestic animals. It also compares the incidence rate of the disease in different types of animal-keeping settings.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a specific laboratory test to analyze samples from domestic animals, and compared the results to historical data on the disease. They identified patterns and trends in the data to inform their conclusions and recommendations for improving disease monitoring.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of disease spread is tracked across a geographic area using repeated observations from multiple ownership groups. The frequency and location of cases are analyzed to identify high-risk zones and potential sources of infection.
descriptions.approach: Samples are collected from various population segments and tested for the presence of a pathogen. Results are aggregated over time and space to detect trends, and risk factors are evaluated to inform preventive actions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Globalization, Historical Perspectives, and International Relations
title: Global histories and cosmopolitan ethics

descriptions.problem: A framework is developed to assess how interconnected human experiences across time and place challenge the idea of unified moral standards, evaluating the extent to which boundaries between groups are maintained or dismantled in practice.
descriptions.approach: A model maps patterns of interaction and separation across diverse human societies, using longitudinal data to simulate how shared values emerge or fade under conditions of integration or fragmentation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Composition of the Poetic Verse in The Poetry of Al Wahb Family

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify the structural patterns of verse in a specific family of writers, analyzing their use of literary devices such as simile, metaphor, and rhythm to convey meaning. It seeks to understand how these patterns contribute to the overall effect of their work.
descriptions.approach: The researcher breaks down the analysis into five key steps: gathering information, organizing it, identifying patterns, testing hypotheses, and drawing conclusions. This process involves examining the structure of the verse and the devices used to convey meaning.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is identified in a sequence of structured expressions, analyzing how recurring elements are arranged and modified across multiple instances to reveal underlying design rules.
descriptions.approach: A systematic framework is applied to break down expressions into units and examine how they are assembled, altered, or omitted to form larger structures, using defined operational rules for each component.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: NCOA4 is a Prognostic Biomarker Associated with Immune Infiltrates in Glioblastoma

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between the expression levels of a protein and patient survival, and compares the survival rates of patients with varying levels of protein expression. It also aims to explain the underlying mechanisms and identify potential biomarkers for patient survival.
descriptions.approach: The study uses various computational tools to analyze data from a large dataset, including statistical tests, regression analysis, and network analysis. It follows a procedure of data collection, analysis, and model creation to identify patterns and relationships in the data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative measure is estimated from patient data to predict survival outcomes based on the level of a specific gene's activity and its associations with immune system components.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model is built using patient records and gene expression levels, applying rank-based tests and survival analysis to link gene activity to survival time and immune component levels.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Analysis and Optimized Design of a Novel Compact Orthogonal Controllable Reactor

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the performance of a device that regulates a physical quantity, such as a magnetic field, by minimizing its size and increasing its range. It estimates the device's behavior under different conditions and compares it to a traditional design.
descriptions.approach: The work starts by analyzing the device's magnetic circuit theoretically, then uses a simulation model to test its behavior. It uses a combination of mathematical rules and a search algorithm to find the best parameters for the device, and finally builds a prototype to test its performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's ability to adjust its resonant behavior over a wide range is evaluated, and its physical footprint is minimized while maintaining performance under varying operational conditions.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical model captures the relationship between structural dimensions and dynamic response. Parameters are iteratively refined using evolutionary rules to balance performance and size, with validation through physical testing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Thermal vacuum tests for the ESA’s OPS-SAT mission

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the performance of a complex system under extreme conditions, comparing its actual performance to its predicted performance, and optimising its design to meet the required standards. It uses data from past experiments and simulations to make these estimates and predictions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers followed a procedure that involved identifying a comprehensive test scenario, using a combination of technical expertise and data analysis to design the test, and then executing the test to gather data and evaluate the system's performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's performance under extreme environmental conditions is evaluated to ensure it maintains functional stability and operational integrity across a range of external exposures and internal load variations.
descriptions.approach: A series of controlled environmental exposures are applied, with real-time monitoring of internal state changes. Test scenarios are iteratively refined based on physical constraints and observed deviations to ensure coverage of operational boundaries.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: rTMS Reduces Craving and Alcohol Use in Patients with Alcohol Use Disorder: Results of a Randomized, Sham-Controlled Clinical Trial

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the effect of a specific treatment on two outcomes: the amount of a certain substance used and the level of a specific urge. It compares the results of two groups: one that received the treatment and one that did not.
descriptions.approach: The researchers applied a treatment to a group of people, and then compared the results to a group that did not receive the treatment. They used a specific statistical method to analyze the data and identify any differences between the two groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A treatment is evaluated for its effect on reducing strong urges to consume a substance and decreasing actual consumption over time, using longitudinal data from individuals who have recently stopped using it.
descriptions.approach: A structured intervention is applied to a group of individuals over a set period, and its impact is compared to a placebo-like intervention using repeated measurements over time to detect changes in behavior and urges.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Diffuse Mesangial Sclerosis

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the likelihood of a child's kidney disease being fatal, based on the presence of a specific abnormality in the kidney tissue. It compares the outcomes of children with this abnormality to those without it.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a case study approach, where they examine a single child's kidney tissue and compare it to a control group of children without the abnormality. They follow the child's health over time to determine the outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rare condition in young individuals is identified through tissue examination, where a specific pattern of cellular changes is detected early, often before symptoms become severe. The goal is to predict the likelihood of a poor outcome based on the presence and characteristics of this pattern.
descriptions.approach: A model analyzes microscopic images of tissue samples to detect a distinct cellular arrangement. It then evaluates the pattern's consistency and spatial distribution to assess the risk of adverse progression.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Institute for the Protection of Confidential Information: industry-specific features of legal regulation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of various methods for managing information in different industries, comparing the outcomes of different approaches to optimise information security. It aims to explain the most suitable strategies for each industry.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of data analysis and comparison of industry-specific features to identify the most effective methods. It follows a procedure of data collection, analysis, and comparison to determine the best approach for each industry.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: It identifies patterns in how rules are adapted across different sectors to address unique operational challenges and risk profiles.
descriptions.approach: It compares regulatory frameworks across domains using structured analysis of policy responses, then maps commonalities and divergences to infer underlying design principles and adaptation strategies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Research and Practice of Differential Classroom

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a new approach to learning, where the focus is on individual learners and their progress is tracked. It compares the outcomes of this approach to traditional methods.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data on learner progress and outcomes to test the effectiveness of the new approach. They followed a procedure where the approach was applied in a controlled environment and the results were analyzed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A structured learning environment is designed to adapt content and pace to individual needs, measuring how well diverse engagement strategies support varied understanding levels and outcomes.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic framework assigns tasks and feedback cycles based on real-time performance, adjusting complexity and support in response to individual progress and interaction patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Teaching Case Discussions with Dr. Sonmezturk

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a specific approach to facilitating discussions among medical professionals, using a series of case studies to compare the outcomes of different methods.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a set of pre-defined rules to evaluate the quality of discussions, based on a model that assesses the level of engagement and understanding among participants.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of clinical decision-making is inferred from sequences of patient encounters involving diagnostic uncertainty and real-time intervention choices.
descriptions.approach: A structured model analyzes temporal patterns in patient interactions, identifying recurring sequences of observations, responses, and outcomes to predict how decisions evolve under pressure and ambiguity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Influence of Ultrasonic Vibration towards the Microstructure Refinement and Particulate Distribution of AA7150-B4C Nanocomposites

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a specific technique on the properties of a material made from a metal alloy and a ceramic reinforcement. It predicts how the properties will change when the technique is applied to different amounts of the ceramic reinforcement.
descriptions.approach: The technique involves mixing the metal alloy and ceramic reinforcement together using a special method, and then applying a high-frequency vibration to the mixture. The researcher then examines the resulting material using various methods to analyze its properties and structure.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of a controlled vibrational process on the uniformity and alignment of ceramic particles within a metal matrix is assessed, using physical and mechanical measurements to evaluate performance improvements.
descriptions.approach: A material is prepared with varying amounts of ceramic particles, subjected to a controlled vibrational treatment during mixing, then analyzed for internal structure, bonding, and strength under different conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Blue lupin (Lupinus angustifolius L.) ‒ the results of varieties and accessions study according to adaptivity and a set of commercialbiological traits

descriptions.problem: This research aims to find the best performers among a set of different types of plants, based on their yield, ability to thrive in different conditions, and other desirable traits. It estimates and compares the performance of these plants to a standard one.
descriptions.approach: The researchers tested a group of different types of plants on a specific type of soil and compared their performance to a standard one. They used a procedure that involved measuring and comparing the yield and other traits of the plants over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of crop lines is evaluated based on yield, growth duration, biomass production, and biochemical composition to identify those with superior performance under specific environmental conditions.
descriptions.approach: Multiple crop lines are grown under uniform conditions; their output and growth characteristics are measured over time. Statistical analysis compares results to a baseline, identifying lines that outperform in yield, biomass, and key biochemical traits while maintaining consistent performance across environments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Application Analysis of Several Basement Exterior Wall Construction Schemes in Compacted Pile Foundation Treatment Engineering

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the costs, efficiency, and construction periods of three different methods for building a foundation in a region with unstable ground. It compares these methods to determine which one is the most cost-effective and efficient.
descriptions.approach: The work uses data from the three methods to compare their costs, efficiency, and construction periods. It follows a procedure of describing each method, comparing the results, and drawing conclusions based on the analysis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of methods for building a structural boundary beneath a foundation are evaluated based on cost, speed, and labor intensity. The performance of each method is compared across different conditions to determine which offers the best balance of efficiency and expense.
descriptions.approach: Each method is modeled as a sequence of steps involving ground interaction, support placement, and labor deployment. The outcome is computed by simulating resource use and time required under varying site constraints.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Potential of vision-enhanced floating car data for urban traffic estimation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the accuracy of speed measurements based on incomplete data from a network of vehicles equipped with cameras or sensors, and compares it to the accuracy of measurements based on data from vehicles that are not equipped with these devices.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a specific algorithm to fill in missing data points and then using this data to make speed measurements, with the goal of improving the accuracy of these measurements.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how accurately movement patterns in a network can be inferred from a subset of moving agents equipped with observational tools, and how this accuracy changes with the fraction of agents providing such observations.
descriptions.approach: A model reconstructs movement rates across time and space using incomplete observations, applying a method that fills gaps in observed patterns by leveraging temporal and spatial consistency in movement behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Unfolding Water Quality Status During COVID-19 Lockdown for the Highly Polluted Santiago River in Jalisco, Mexico

descriptions.problem: This research estimates and compares the quality of a certain environment over time, using data from multiple sampling points. It aims to identify changes and improvements in the environment's condition.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from 13 sampling points to compare the quality of the environment over three time periods: a recent period, a pre-period, and an eleven-year trend. The data is analyzed using statistical methods to identify changes and improvements.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A temporal pattern in environmental conditions is assessed across multiple monitoring sites, comparing current and prior periods to detect shifts in key indicators influenced by reduced human activity.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model aligns and compares measurements from repeated observations over time, using multivariate analysis to identify dominant sources and quantify changes in pollutant loads and overall system health.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Ensemble Learning Methods

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of different methods for classifying complex patterns in data, comparing their accuracy and optimising their use for specific types of problems.
descriptions.approach: It uses a combination of methods to predict the best approach for each type of problem, following a procedure that involves evaluating and comparing the performance of multiple methods, and selecting the most effective one.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies patterns in input signals to assign a value to each signal based on historical examples of similar signals and their outcomes.
descriptions.approach: Multiple models process the same input independently, then combine their outputs using a weighted average, where each model's contribution depends on its past accuracy in predicting outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Fluorescence Studies of Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor and Its Associated Lipid Milieu: The Influence of Erwin London’s Methodological Approaches

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the influence of certain substances on the behavior of a specific type of molecule, which is crucial for understanding how these substances interact with the molecule and affect its function. The study aims to explain how these substances shape the formation and maintenance of specific structures within the molecule.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used various techniques, including fluorescence methods, to investigate the interactions between the molecule and the substances. They applied these techniques to different systems, including purified molecules and cells with modified structures, to gain insights into the underlying mechanisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's behavior under varying environmental conditions is assessed to determine how specific molecular components influence structural stability and functional dynamics within a membrane-like environment.
descriptions.approach: Fluorescent probes are used to track changes in local environment stiffness and molecular proximity. Energy transfer and quenching events are monitored to infer spatial organization and binding preferences under different compositional conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Expert System of Pest Diagnosis in Passion Fruit Plants using the Bayes Theorem Method

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a pest being present on a certain type of object, based on characteristics of the object and the pest. It predicts the most likely pest and provides countermeasures.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a mathematical model to calculate the probability of a pest being present, based on evidence from the object. It follows a procedure of calculating probabilities and making decisions based on those probabilities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood of a specific condition in a crop based on observed symptoms and environmental factors, comparing how well different hypotheses explain the available data.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates each possible cause by updating the probability of a hypothesis as new observations are input, using a rule that adjusts confidence based on how consistent the evidence is with each potential explanation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Potential of Biomass Sources for Fural-Based Fuel Production in the Consideration as a Green Fuel

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the potential of using certain materials to improve the efficiency of a type of machine that converts energy from one form to another, with the goal of reducing the amount of a certain substance released into the environment. It also compares the effectiveness of different methods for achieving this goal.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from experiments and tests to develop and test new methods for improving the efficiency of the machine, with a focus on reducing the release of a certain substance. They follow a procedure that involves combining different techniques to achieve the desired outcome.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the efficiency and environmental impact of converting organic material into a liquid energy form using thermal and chemical processing methods.
descriptions.approach: It applies rapid heating followed by chemical treatment to transform raw organic matter into a usable liquid product, evaluating performance across different input conditions and processing parameters.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Latour

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the diversity of social life in a large system, comparing it to the complexity of the system's interactions. It aims to explain whether the diversity is a result of the system's actions or a necessary illusion.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves combining data from various sources to understand the relationships between the system's components and the diversity of social life. It uses a rule-based model to identify patterns and make predictions about the system's behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is inferred that maps how complex interactions among entities grow in scale and variety over time, based on patterns observed in large-scale, interconnected behaviors.
descriptions.approach: A model iteratively clusters and traces patterns across vast networks of interacting units, identifying recurring structures and emergent behaviors that persist under varying conditions of input and connection density.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Transportation lead time in perishable food value chains: an Indian perspective

descriptions.problem: This research aims to identify the main reasons for long transportation times for fresh produce in a specific region, which affects the quality and ultimately leads to wasted products. It seeks to understand the impact of transportation on the quality of these products.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from surveys and interviews to analyze the factors affecting transportation times. It examines the effects of various factors on transportation times and identifies practical measures to reduce them.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The time it takes to move fresh goods from origin to a major distribution hub is estimated and analyzed to identify key contributors to delays.
descriptions.approach: Data from field operators is collected and segmented by product type. Factors influencing delay are assessed through structured interviews and statistical analysis to determine patterns and actionable insights.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: ‘She who creates havoc is here’

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of a character's free expression of their attraction to multiple genders on societal norms and attitudes, comparing it to traditional conceptions of relationships and identity.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a critical framework to analyze the character's behavior and its implications, following a procedure that involves examining the representation of the character's identity and relationships through a lens of social and cultural critique.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A social narrative is analyzed to understand how non-conforming personal identities challenge established norms and provoke societal resistance or change.
descriptions.approach: A structured interpretation maps character behaviors to societal expectations, identifying contradictions and tensions that reveal hidden power dynamics and alternative forms of personal agency.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Reablement in A Small Municipality, A Survival Analysis

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the risk of long-term dependence and death in two groups of people who need help with daily activities, and compares these risks. It aims to explain whether one group has a lower risk of needing long-term help and dying.
descriptions.approach: The researchers matched people who need help with daily activities based on their age, sex, and ability to perform daily tasks, and then analyzed the risks of long-term dependence and death in the two groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the risk of transitioning to a sustained, high-intensity support pathway and the likelihood of an adverse health outcome over time, based on individual characteristics and service exposure.
descriptions.approach: Individuals are paired based on age, gender, and baseline functional status. A statistical model tracks the probability of transitioning to a high-intensity support pathway or an adverse health event, adjusting for observed differences in starting conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Experimental Examination on Utilization of Processed Mine Overburden Sand by Substituted to River Sand in Construction

descriptions.problem: Estimate the suitability of a substitute material for construction, comparing its properties to those of a natural resource. The goal is to determine if the substitute can be used as a reliable alternative.
descriptions.approach: Compare the properties of the substitute material to those of the natural resource, using data from experiments and measurements. The procedure involves preparing concrete samples with both materials and analyzing their strengths.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material derived from waste rock layers is evaluated to determine if it can substitute for a scarce natural resource in building applications by comparing its physical and mechanical performance under controlled conditions.
descriptions.approach: The material is processed and tested for key physical traits like particle size distribution, water retention, and strength. Samples are then mixed into construction units, and their performance is measured over time to assess structural suitability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Strategies for Drug Targets Selection of Mycobacterium Tuberculosis H37rv

descriptions.problem: Estimate the effectiveness of different targets for a pathogen that causes a serious infectious disease, and compare their potential to disrupt the pathogen's life cycle.
descriptions.approach: Use data from the pathogen's genome sequence and study its interactions with the host's outside components to identify promising targets.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is identified that regulates key biological processes through reversible modification events, with potential to disrupt essential functions when inhibited. The goal is to evaluate which components at the periphery of a complex network are most likely to be influenced by external interventions.
descriptions.approach: A computational model analyzes functional interactions across molecular pathways, focusing on dynamic regulatory events at the interface between internal and external environments. It ranks candidates based on connectivity, stability, and response to external signals.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Digital dogma

descriptions.problem: A pattern of behavior is identified in individuals who engage in same-gender relationships within culturally constrained environments, and the extent to which these behaviors align with traditional beliefs is assessed through personal accounts and digital interactions.
descriptions.approach: Personal accounts are analyzed for consistency with established cultural norms and non-traditional practices, using iterative interpretation to detect subtle shifts in behavior and identity expression across digital and physical contexts.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 30 Subcortical Mapping During Intracranial Surgery in Children

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the location of important brain networks in children, predicting which areas are essential for brain function and which ones can be safely removed without causing permanent damage. It also compares the effectiveness of different methods for mapping these networks.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data and evidence to identify the functionally defined but anatomically ambiguous eloquent areas and their white matter connectivity. They follow a procedure that involves mapping the brain's networks and comparing the results to determine the best approach for each child.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The task is to identify and preserve key functional connections between brain regions that support essential behaviors, such as movement, sensation, and cognition, based on real-time neural responses during intervention.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic model analyzes electrical signals from brain tissue to detect patterns associated with specific functions, then maps the strength and timing of interactions between regions to guide decisions on which pathways to protect.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Anti-inflammatory effects of flavonoids in Citrus jabara fruit peels

descriptions.problem: This research investigates the effects of a specific compound found in a certain type of food on inflammation in the body. It aims to understand how this compound works and whether it can be used to alleviate symptoms of allergic diseases.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed data from a specific type of food to identify the compound and its effects on inflammation. They then tested the compound's effects on various biological processes and found that it has inhibitory effects on certain enzymes and pathways involved in inflammation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A biological compound is identified that, when metabolized, produces a known active form with measurable suppression of inflammatory markers in cellular environments.
descriptions.approach: The compound is administered and observed for metabolic conversion; its metabolite is tested for inhibition of key inflammatory pathways, with activity measured under controlled conditions involving cellular response to stimulation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Awareness Program of Pesticides Used among Farmers using Difficulty-Usefulness Pyramid (A Suggestion for Health Laws and Policies Regarding the Use of Pesticides)

descriptions.problem: This study aims to identify the most important factors that influence the safe use of toxic substances in agriculture, and to prioritize these factors to inform health laws and policies. The goal is to estimate the most critical elements that need to be improved to prevent negative effects on people.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data from 100 respondents who have knowledge about these toxic substances. They used a questionnaire to gather information on various aspects of their use, and then analyzed the data to determine the priority of these aspects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies which behavioral practices in agricultural operations are most critical to modify to reduce health risks, by evaluating how difficult and useful each practice is to implement.
descriptions.approach: Each practice is scored on difficulty and usefulness from one to ten. The difference between scores is computed, and practices are ranked by the smallest gap, forming a prioritized list of actions to improve safety.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Use of Cloud, Multimedia, and QR Codes to Enhance Print Maps

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the value of maps by adding multimedia content and comparing it to the value of maps without this content. It predicts that the value of maps will increase when multimedia content is added.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves adding QR codes to maps, storing multimedia content on a cloud, and using a camera and internet to access and interpret the codes. The procedure follows a simple rule: attach a QR code to a map, store multimedia content on a cloud, and use a camera and internet to access and interpret the code.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A static visual representation is augmented with linked digital content to expand its informational depth and interactivity.
descriptions.approach: A physical object is assigned a unique identifier that directs users to a remote digital repository, where associated media or data can be accessed and retrieved upon user request.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Antibody Characterization Report for SPARC-related modular calcium-binding protein 1 (SMOC1)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the quality of a protein by comparing how it interacts with different substances in a controlled environment. It predicts which substances will bind well to the protein and optimizes the selection of these substances.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves using a standardized protocol to compare how a protein interacts with different substances in two types of cells: ones that don't have the protein and ones that do. The model follows a step-by-step process to evaluate the interactions and select the best substances.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment of a biological reagent's reliability is made by comparing signal intensity and pattern across genetically modified and unmodified cell systems under controlled conditions.
descriptions.approach: Signal strength and consistency are evaluated across multiple cell types with and without a specific genetic alteration, using standardized detection methods and reproducible experimental conditions to determine reagent performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Experimental Study on Recentering Behavior of Precompressed Polyurethane Springs

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between the stiffness of a material and its ability to return to its original shape after being compressed. It also predicts how much force is needed to achieve this, based on the amount of initial compression.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created 160 samples of the material and tested how they behaved under repeated compressions. They used a mathematical model to analyze the results and find the optimal level of initial compression that prevents the material from deforming permanently.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative relationship is established between an initial condition and a resulting force, where the force is observed to scale linearly with the initial condition across multiple material samples under repeated loading.
descriptions.approach: A linear model is fitted to data points from repeated load cycles, where the force response is expressed as a constant multiplier times the initial state, and the optimal initial state is identified where no residual deformation occurs.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Cancer, Stress, Anesthesia, and Immune Response
title: AB101. SOH22ABS235. Does intrao perative use of opioids increase the risk of cancer recurrence?

descriptions.problem: A quantity of interest is assessed across different conditions: the influence of a substance administered during a medical procedure on biological processes related to cell behavior and growth signals in living systems.
descriptions.approach: A systematic review of existing studies is conducted, filtering data based on experimental models and observed changes in cellular activity. Evidence from both controlled lab settings and living organisms is evaluated to determine patterns and potential causal links.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Feature Space Particle Inference for Neural Network Ensembles

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the performance of a group of models by making each model more diverse and robust in its predictions. It estimates the best way to make each model capture unique characteristics that will lead to better overall predictions.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves optimizing the models to capture distinct characteristics in a specific layer of their internal workings, which is expected to improve the overall predictions and make them more robust.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system learns to generate diverse and effective model instances by focusing on intermediate outputs during processing, aiming to improve prediction stability and accuracy across different input patterns.
descriptions.approach: It iteratively refines a set of model variants by adjusting their behavior based on how they respond to internal processing stages, promoting distinct responses to similar inputs while maintaining overall performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Environmental Gradients Shaping the Freshwater Bryophyte Communities of Croatia (Western Balkans)

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the distribution of certain types of plant communities across different geographical areas, based on various environmental factors such as climate, soil type, and water quality. It also compares the diversity of these communities across different regions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of data analysis and classification techniques to identify patterns and relationships between environmental factors and plant community types. They then compared the results to understand the geographical distribution of these communities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The structure and distribution of plant communities are inferred from patterns in climate, geology, and water chemistry across a landscape, identifying distinct groupings based on environmental conditions and their spatial relationships.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model groups sites by similarity in environmental conditions and identifies dominant community types, then maps their spatial distribution based on climate, soil type, and hydrological flow characteristics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Robotic Surgery for Endometrial Cancer Increases Intraocular Pressure: A Pilot Study [A314]

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the effect of a specific medical procedure on a particular physiological parameter, comparing the changes in this parameter before and after the procedure. It aims to explain the relationship between the procedure and the parameter.
descriptions.approach: The researchers measured the parameter in question before and after the procedure, at various stages, and compared the results using statistical tests. They followed a specific procedure, involving multiple steps and measurements, to evaluate the changes in the parameter.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A change in pressure within a bodily cavity is monitored over time during a medical procedure, comparing values before and after specific procedural steps to detect statistically significant shifts.
descriptions.approach: Pressure measurements are taken at multiple time points during a procedure, with each measurement averaged across paired sites. A statistical test compares the baseline value to subsequent values to determine if a significant change occurs.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Relationship of Neuropeptide S with Clinical and Metabolic Parameters of Patients during Rehabilitation Therapy for Schizophrenia

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between a certain brain chemical and how patients feel and behave during a treatment program. It compares the levels of this chemical in patients who received a structured treatment program versus those who received a standard support program.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a procedure that involves analyzing data from two groups of patients and comparing it to data from a group of healthy individuals. They also used various mathematical models to understand the relationship between the brain chemical and the patients' symptoms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A biological marker in the bloodstream is assessed to determine its association with changes in symptom severity and metabolic stability over time in individuals undergoing structured intervention.
descriptions.approach: Blood levels of the marker are monitored alongside structured behavioral and cognitive assessments. Statistical models are applied to identify which symptom clusters correlate most strongly with changes in the marker, while controlling for baseline metabolic variables.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Facial Nerve Paralysis Treatment and Research
title: 105. Long Term Surgical and Patient Reported Outcomes After Cross Face Nerve Graft Reconstruction in Pediatric Facial Paralysis

descriptions.problem: The long-term change in a physical movement pattern is measured over time, and patient perceptions of function and well-being are assessed across different life stages using standardized scoring systems.
descriptions.approach: Movement data is collected from images at multiple time points and analyzed for changes in magnitude and consistency. Patient feedback is gathered through structured questionnaires and interviews, then quantified and compared across time and individual reports.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Piperine Derivatives Enhance Fusion and Axonal Transport of Mitochondria by Activating Mitofusins

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a certain compound on the movement and transport of a specific type of cell organelle, comparing the results to a control. It predicts which compounds will be most effective at improving this process.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of experiments to test the compound's effect, including measuring the compound's ability to stimulate the movement and transport of the organelle. They compare the results to a control and identify the optimal structure of the compound to achieve the desired effect.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A compound is tested to determine its ability to promote the merging of cellular energy-producing units, enhancing their movement and coordination within a cell's network.
descriptions.approach: A series of structurally modified versions of a known compound are designed with specific spatial relationships between key functional groups. Their effectiveness is measured in live cells using assays that track the movement and fusion of these units in response to the compound.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Strong Resistance to Early and Late Leaf Spot in Peanut-Compatible Wild-Derived Induced Allotetraploids

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of various genotypes in resisting two types of disease, which can cause severe plant damage and yield loss. It predicts which genotypes are most resistant and compares their resistance levels to those of other genotypes.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a bioassay to test the resistance of 13 genotypes to these diseases. They measured the resistance of each genotype and compared the results to identify the most resistant genotypes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies and quantifies resistance traits in genetically diverse plants under controlled disease exposure, measuring how effectively they limit pathogen spread and symptom development across different environmental conditions.
descriptions.approach: A set of plant lines is exposed to pathogen-induced stress in isolated leaf conditions, and the resulting disease progression is monitored over time. Traits such as lesion size, spread rate, and pathogen reproduction are recorded and correlated across different genotypes to detect consistent protective patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Medically Attended Illness due to Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection Among Infants Born in the United States Between 2016 and 2020

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the burden of medically attended illnesses caused by a common virus among young people born in the United States between 2016 and 2020. It compares the number of illnesses across different types of insurance data to understand the scope of the problem.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed data from insurance claims to identify the number of medically attended illnesses, and then compared the results to understand the scope of the problem. They used different definitions to estimate the burden of illnesses and stratified the results by factors such as birth weight and medical care level.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The proportion of medically attended respiratory infections occurring in a specific population group during their first exposure season is estimated, broken down by gestational age, preexisting health conditions, and level of medical care involved.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model analyzes health records from diverse insurance sources to identify and categorize cases of respiratory illness in early life, adjusting for risk factors and care settings to determine the relative contribution of different demographic and health profiles.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The semiotic scoubidou – a short intellectual biography of Per Aage Brandt

descriptions.problem: This text estimates the significance of Per Aage Brandt's life and work, comparing his achievements in science, art, and scholarship to provide an overview of his impact.
descriptions.approach: The author presents a summary of Brandt's key contributions, following a procedure that involves identifying and summarizing his main ideas, artistic practices, and scholarly accomplishments.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of thought is inferred from a sequence of creative and analytical outputs over time, relating them to contextual influences and evolving perspectives.
descriptions.approach: A structured narrative is built by mapping transitions between ideas, identifying recurring themes, and linking them to external stimuli, using chronological and thematic clustering as organizing principles.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Essential Amino Acids-Rich Diet Decreased Adipose Tissue Storage in Adult Mice: A Preliminary Histopathological Study

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a specific type of food on the body's fat storage and muscle mass in a certain animal model. It compares the results of two groups of animals, one that eats a standard food and one that eats a food rich in a certain type of nutrient.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a procedure where they gave two groups of animals a standard food and a food rich in a certain type of nutrient, and then examined the changes in their body fat and muscle mass after a certain period of time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how a specific nutritional input affects body fat distribution and metabolic activity in a living organism over a short period.
descriptions.approach: A controlled intervention is applied, and changes in fat cell size, hormone expression, and energy-burning capacity are measured through microscopic analysis of tissue samples and associated molecular markers.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Maladaptive Daydreaming: Epidemiological Data on a Newly Identified Syndrome

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the frequency of a certain type of excessive, narrative, emotional fantasy activity in a large group of people, and compares it to a control group to see if there is a significant difference. It also tries to explain why this activity might be more common in certain age groups.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of self-reported data and clinical interviews to gather information. They then analyze the data to see if it supports the idea that this activity is a legitimate psychological phenomenon, and if so, what its characteristics might be.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A rate is estimated for a behavior pattern involving immersive, emotionally charged mental simulations that interfere with daily functioning, based on self-reported experiences and clinical validation in diverse populations.
descriptions.approach: Participants report on the frequency and intensity of such simulations using a standardized scale. Those meeting a threshold are assessed through structured interviews to confirm the presence and impact of the behavior, adjusting the final estimate based on interview outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A graph-theoretical approach to DNA similarity analysis

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how closely different biological samples share structural patterns based on repeated motifs and their spatial arrangements in a linear order.
descriptions.approach: It constructs a structured representation from repeated pattern occurrences, then defines a distance measure between such representations to quantify how closely two samples align in pattern frequency and arrangement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Formulation and Evaluation of Liposome Moringa Oleifera Seed Oil (Moringa oleifera L.) as Anti-aging

descriptions.problem: This work aims to find the best way to deliver a natural substance with antioxidant properties to improve skin health, using a combination of ingredients to improve its stability and effectiveness.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a method to mix and test different combinations of ingredients, and then used a device to measure the size and stability of the resulting mixture, and another device to measure how well the substance was trapped and released.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A stable delivery system is designed to encapsulate a natural antioxidant compound to enhance its effectiveness in slowing age-related cellular decline, using physical and chemical properties of the formulation as evidence.
descriptions.approach: A mixture of phospholipid and sterol components is prepared via film-based hydration, then evaluated for consistency, suspension stability, and internal payload retention through optical and size-based analysis.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Understanding Cybercrime and the Phenomenon of "Broutage" (Grazing) For a Media Education of Pupils and Students in Côte d'Ivoire

descriptions.problem: A pattern of unregulated online behavior by young users is observed and analyzed to understand its social and educational implications, using available reports and guidelines as evidence.
descriptions.approach: A structured thematic review is applied to group and interpret diverse sources, using a framework that links individual actions to broader societal and environmental influences to identify key behavioral and educational factors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Children's Diabetes Management Using the Internet of Things and Robot Assistants

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new system for managing a chronic condition in children, using a combination of robotic assistants and data from various sources. It aims to compare the outcomes of different approaches to managing this condition.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a model that combines data from sensors and user input to predict the child's condition and provide personalized advice. It optimizes the delivery of support services based on the child's needs and the availability of resources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system continuously monitors physiological signals and environmental conditions to predict health fluctuations and adjust treatment parameters in real time.
descriptions.approach: Sensors collect data from a user's body and surroundings; a model processes this data to detect patterns, then triggers automated responses like adjusting medication delivery or alerting caregivers based on changing conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Green Chiryata (Andrographis paniculata): A potential blood purifier

descriptions.problem: A pattern of biological activity is inferred from long-term observations of natural substances used in traditional medicine, focusing on their effects in managing chronic conditions and supporting bodily function under stress.
descriptions.approach: A structured review aggregates historical and recent studies to identify consistent outcomes across diverse populations, then maps these outcomes to known mechanisms and usage contexts to evaluate potential effectiveness and reliability of the substance in complex health scenarios.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Materials Data on Rb2V3O8 by Materials Project

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the structure of a material, Rb2V3O8, and describes the arrangement of its constituent parts. It compares the distances between these parts to understand the material's properties.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data on the material's structure to create a model of its arrangement. They then used this model to compare and understand the material's properties.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A three-dimensional arrangement of atoms is inferred from known spatial and chemical interactions, where specific sites hold elements with distinct local environments and distances to surrounding entities.
descriptions.approach: A model maps positions of elements based on their connections to neighbors, using consistent distance ranges and coordination numbers to define local structures across multiple repeating units.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Materials Data on Ba(YS2)2 by Materials Project

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the structure of a material, Ba(YS2)2, and describes the arrangement of its constituent parts, including Ba, Y, and S, in three-dimensional space. It compares and contrasts different types of arrangements to understand the material's properties.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data analysis and geometric modeling to understand the material's structure. They apply mathematical rules to predict the arrangement of Ba, Y, and S in the material's crystal lattice.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A three-dimensional arrangement of ions is analyzed to determine how different types of sites are structured and how their interactions vary in terms of distances and angles.
descriptions.approach: The structure is built by assigning positions to ions based on coordination rules, where each ion is surrounded by a specific number of neighbors, and the distances and angles between them are constrained by geometric and chemical consistency.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Materials Data on Cs2LiBr3 by Materials Project

descriptions.problem: This work describes the structure of a material, estimating the arrangement of its constituent parts and comparing it to known patterns. It predicts the distances between these parts and explains how they fit together.
