descriptions.approach: The researchers used data on the material's shape and size to create a model of its internal structure. They applied rules to this model to determine the arrangement of the material's parts and the distances between them.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A three-dimensional arrangement of ions is analyzed to determine how different positions of cations and anions are connected through shared interactions, and how these connections vary in strength and pattern across multiple sites.
descriptions.approach: A model assigns each position to a set of neighboring units, with specific interaction strengths and coordination numbers. It maps how each unit links to others, forming a network where connections vary in length and number across distinct locations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pharmacist‐driven interventions to de‐escalate urinary antimuscarinics in the Programs of All‐Inclusive Care for the Elderly

descriptions.problem: A measure of drug exposure is tracked over time to assess changes in treatment intensity following expert-driven suggestions. The change is compared across individuals who follow the suggestions and those who do not, and factors influencing adherence are identified.
descriptions.approach: A set of recommendations is issued and evaluated for follow-through at multiple time points. Exposure levels are monitored and adjusted based on whether a treatment plan is adopted. Statistical models identify patterns linked to higher likelihood of adoption.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Key abiotic parameters for the management of the richness of bryolichenic communities in bogs of North Patagonia (Chile)

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how well different environmental conditions support the presence of diverse, non-vascular life forms in wet, water-saturated environments. It identifies which environmental variables most strongly influence the number and variety of life forms found in specific habitat zones.
descriptions.approach: It evaluates environmental gradients across a landscape, focusing on moisture levels and substrate stability. It assigns weights to environmental features based on their correlation with observed life form diversity, then recommends preserving areas where these features peak.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Material and technical resources of enterprises and the efficiency of their use

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of resource availability on the efficiency of a system, comparing different factors such as economic, production, financial, social, and environmental elements to determine the effectiveness of resource use.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of analysis and synthesis, comparative analysis, and generalization of data to identify the key conditions for successful system operation and optimize resource use.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system evaluates how well various inputs—such as land, labor, and materials—are combined and utilized to produce outputs, aiming to identify factors that influence performance and outcomes across different operational contexts.
descriptions.approach: The system models input-output relationships by analyzing how changes in resource allocation and environmental conditions affect production results, using comparative and aggregated patterns to identify optimal configurations and performance drivers.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 4-bit adhesion logic enables universal multicellular interface patterning

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and predicts the optimal arrangement of different types of biological structures to achieve specific functions, using a minimal set of information. It compares and optimizes the arrangement to achieve universal patterns.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a mathematical model to generate and test different patterns, and then identifying the most efficient and effective arrangement using a set of rules and algorithms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to generate and control spatial arrangements of interacting units based on defined rules, using a limited set of interaction signals to produce predictable and repeatable structural layouts across diverse conditions.
descriptions.approach: A set of four distinct interaction signals is applied to units in a structured environment, where each signal can be present or absent to define a spatial rule. These signals are combined in all possible combinations to generate a complete set of spatial configurations through a tiling-based algorithm.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Home, university, and other spaces

descriptions.problem: This research estimates how the COVID-19 pandemic has changed the way people conduct research in different locations, and predicts future trends. It compares data from two countries to understand the impact on research habits.
descriptions.approach: The study compares data from two countries, using a questionnaire to gather information about people's research habits and location choices. The data was analyzed to identify patterns and trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of human activity across different physical settings is analyzed to determine how shifts in routine and environment affect productivity and decision-making during a period of widespread disruption.
descriptions.approach: A structured survey collects self-reported data on location preferences and activity patterns over time, then compares trends across regions with differing levels of flexibility in daily operations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Trends in pediatric ambulatory community acquired infections before and during COVID-19 pandemic: A prospective multicentric surveillance study in France

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the trends of a certain type of illness in children before and after a significant change in how people interacted with each other, and compares these trends to what happened before the change. It also explains why some of these trends changed.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data from a large group of doctors who specialize in treating this type of illness, and used this data to compare the number of cases over time. They used a statistical method to analyze the data and identify patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A time-series analysis estimates how the frequency of common childhood illnesses changes before and after a major societal intervention, comparing periods with and without strict control measures.
descriptions.approach: A model tracks recorded cases over time, applies statistical comparison to identify shifts in frequency, and uses regression to quantify changes, detecting patterns like drops and rebounds in occurrence across different conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Amrose Skin Tag Remover Review, Results, Scam or Side Effects

descriptions.problem: A set of user-reported outcomes is evaluated to determine the effectiveness and safety of a treatment method based on subjective experiences and observed results across diverse individuals.
descriptions.approach: Multiple sources are systematically reviewed to aggregate and compare individual reports, then a weighted assessment is formed based on consistency, detail, and reported adverse effects to infer overall reliability and potential risks.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Integrasi Nilai-nilai Keislaman dalam Pembelajaran Sains di Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Ma’arif 01 KH. Shiddiq Jember

descriptions.problem: This research aims to describe how to combine two seemingly separate concepts: the pursuit of knowledge (science) and the understanding of a higher power (spirituality). It seeks to explain how to integrate these concepts in a way that is both intellectually stimulating and spiritually fulfilling.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses a qualitative approach, gathering data through observation, interviews, and documentation. They then analyze this data using a specific method to identify patterns and insights.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A method is developed to embed moral and spiritual principles into the teaching of scientific concepts, ensuring that learning fosters both intellectual understanding and a deeper connection to a higher purpose.
descriptions.approach: Scientific content is taught by referencing foundational texts and traditional teachings, then using guided inquiry and dialogue to help learners connect factual knowledge with ethical and existential dimensions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effect of Ti reinforcement on the physical and mechanical properties of AZ91/Ti composites

descriptions.problem: This work investigates how adding a certain metal to a mixture of materials affects its density, strength, and ability to withstand pressure, as well as its tendency to break or deform.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created a mixture of materials by adding a small amount of metal to the mixture, then tested its properties using various experiments, such as measuring its weight, density, and strength.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The performance of a material is evaluated across multiple physical and structural metrics under varying composition, including density, resistance to deformation, and strength under load, as a function of added component concentration.
descriptions.approach: A systematic variation of component content is introduced, and the resulting material is subjected to controlled testing conditions to measure its response. Observed changes are attributed to improved internal cohesion and reduced void content.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Video Abstract

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the feasibility of a minimally invasive surgical approach for a specific type of abdominal growth, aiming to remove the growth while preserving surrounding nerves. It compares the effectiveness of this approach to traditional methods.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves a step-by-step removal of a specific type of tissue, followed by the removal of nerves that are at risk of damage. The approach is based on a model that simulates the surgical process and evaluates its outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A surgical procedure is designed to remove a lesion from a high-positioned site in the lower abdomen, ensuring complete removal while preserving surrounding structures and minimizing damage to critical nerves.
descriptions.approach: The procedure follows a step-by-step sequence involving careful dissection of a deep anatomical layer, followed by targeted removal of specific nerve bundles to reduce postoperative complications.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: [Clinical Significance of IgG4 Level in Predicting the Activity and Outcome of Phospholipase A2 Receptor-associated Membranous Nephropathy].

descriptions.problem: The degree of disease progression and patient response to treatment is estimated from repeated measurements of a specific immune protein in blood and urine over time.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model compares fluctuations in the protein level across individuals and time points, identifying patterns that correlate with worsening or improvement, then uses these patterns to forecast future disease states.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Evaluation of a multiplex PCR kit for detection of 17 respiratory pathogens in hospitalized patients

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the presence of 17 common pathogens in clinical samples from patients, predicts the likelihood of infection based on the sample, compares the results to a standard method, optimizes the detection of certain pathogens, and explains the limitations of the approach.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves analyzing a large number of samples using a sensitive detection method, comparing the results to a standard method, and evaluating the performance of the detection method based on its sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the presence of 17 distinct disease-causing agents in clinical samples, comparing detection rates to established diagnostic results, and evaluates accuracy across various pathogens and co-occurrence patterns.
descriptions.approach: A set of parallel biochemical reactions detects specific genetic markers for each agent; results are processed to determine presence, absence, or co-occurrence, with performance assessed through comparison to a reference diagnostic method.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Determination of Vitamins, Trace Elements, and Phytochemical Compounds in Ginkgo Biloba Leaves Extracts

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the amount of certain substances in a plant-based material, compare the results to identify the most abundant substances, and explain the relevance of these substances to the material's properties.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used two solvents to dissolve the material, then used a machine to measure the amount of substances in the solvents, and another machine to identify the types of substances present.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The relative abundance of various organic and inorganic components in a plant-based material is estimated and compared across two different solvent-based processing methods.
descriptions.approach: A sample is processed using two distinct solvent systems, then analyzed via chromatographic and spectroscopic techniques to separate, quantify, and identify key organic and inorganic constituents based on their chemical behavior and interaction with detection systems.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Influence of the glycerin content in the preparation of calcium diglyceroxide from eggshell applied in the residual oil transesterification

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the effect of a certain substance on the efficiency of a chemical reaction involving a solid material, a liquid, and heat. It compares the results of different experiments to find the optimal conditions for the reaction.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of the substance and the solid material to create a new compound, and then tested its performance in a series of chemical reactions. They varied the conditions of the reaction to see how the results changed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The efficiency of a chemical conversion process is evaluated under varying conditions of a key component's purity, and its effect on product composition, reaction stability, and byproduct levels is analyzed.
descriptions.approach: A material is prepared using a base substance and a purified additive in a controlled mixing process. The reaction is run under fixed conditions, and the resulting product's properties are measured across multiple cycles to assess performance and consistency.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Design of a stiffness adjustable magnetic fluid shock absorber based on optimal stiffness coefficient

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal stiffness coefficient for a type of device that helps reduce unwanted movements in a flexible structure, and compares it to the stiffness coefficients of other similar devices. It also optimizes the design of this device by finding the best stiffness coefficient.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves calculating the stiffness coefficient using formulas, fabricating a series of devices with adjustable stiffness, and measuring the relationship between the device's movement and the distance it moves. The results are compared to simulations and experiments to verify the optimal stiffness coefficient.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A quantitative measure of a system's resistance to deformation under load is determined and evaluated across a range of operating conditions to identify the value that maximizes performance in dynamic response.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical model is developed to relate the load applied to a system to its displacement, assuming a linear relationship. Experimental and simulation results are used to validate the model and identify the parameter value that yields the most effective suppression of dynamic response.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Food Security and Health in Diverse Populations
title: Impacts of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Mobile Produce Market Operations: Adaptations, Barriers, and Future Directions for Increasing Food Access

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the impact of a significant event on mobile market operations, comparing the effects on demand and produce distribution. It also predicts the adaptations needed to maintain effective service and explains the future directions for increasing access to essential goods.
descriptions.approach: The researchers distributed a survey to mobile market operators, gathering data on the changes in demand and produce distribution. They then analyzed the responses to identify patterns and trends in the adaptations employed by mobile markets.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system observes changes in service delivery patterns and community demand following a widespread disruption event, estimating how operations adapt in response to new constraints and opportunities.
descriptions.approach: A set of operators reports on shifts in service volume, delivery methods, and operational costs; responses are aggregated and analyzed to identify trends in demand and operational flexibility across different community settings.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Gesundheitsökonomie

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of economic incentives in healthcare systems, comparing the outcomes of different control mechanisms and institutions. It aims to explain how these incentives can be optimised to improve the efficiency and quality of healthcare services.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using concrete subject areas and data to develop and test economic models, linking institutions and actors to inform economic analysis and decision-making.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system of decision-making is analyzed where resource allocation depends on incentives and institutional rules, and the outcomes of different control mechanisms are compared across real-world settings.
descriptions.approach: A set of rules defines how actors respond to rewards and penalties within a structured environment, and the resulting behaviors are simulated under varying conditions to predict system-wide effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Estimating the changing burden of disease attributable to high sodium intake in South Africa for 2000, 2006 and 2012

descriptions.problem: The model estimates how many health events and years of poor health are linked to high levels of a dietary factor that raises blood pressure, across different years and demographic groups.
descriptions.approach: It compares health outcomes under current conditions to a hypothetical scenario where the dietary factor is reduced to a minimal risk level, using population data and known health risks to compute differences in health impacts over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors Are Novel Targets of APETx-like Toxins from the Sea Anemone Heteractis magnifica

descriptions.problem: A set of small, structured molecules is identified that bind to and modulate a specific type of ion channel involved in fast neuronal signaling, and their interaction is assessed across different receptor subtypes and cellular environments.
descriptions.approach: Binding affinity is measured using labeled ligands in a competitive assay. Functional effects are tested by applying a known agonist and measuring resulting ion flow. Structural features are analyzed computationally to explain sequence similarities across related organisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Auto- and Hetero-Catalytic Processing of the N-Terminal Propeptide Promotes the C-Terminal Fibronectin Type III Domain-Mediated Dimerization of a Thermostable Vpr-like Protease

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the efficiency of a process that converts a raw protein into a mature, functional enzyme. It compares the efficiency of this process to another process and optimizes the first process to be more efficient.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of data and evidence to understand the activation and oligomerization mechanisms of a specific enzyme. They apply a procedure that involves processing the enzyme in a specific way to promote its maturation and functionalization.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is analyzed to determine how a structural domain at one end of a protein influences the folding and pairing of a distinct domain at the opposite end, especially in the presence of a regulatory segment.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic model simulates how interactions between a catalytic region and a terminal domain are modulated by a bound regulatory element, with outcomes evaluated under varying concentrations and structural constraints.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effect of breed and graded levels of sun-dried pineapple (Ananas cosmosus) peel on carcass characteristics of growing rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus) bucks

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the effect of varying levels of a certain food additive on the physical characteristics of young animals. It compares the results across different types of animals and levels of the food additive.
descriptions.approach: The researchers randomly assigned a group of young animals to different levels of the food additive and measured their physical characteristics after a set period of time. They then analyzed the data to identify any patterns or differences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The relative weights of various body components are estimated and compared across different genetic lines and dietary treatments to identify patterns in growth and tissue distribution.
descriptions.approach: A group of animals is assigned to distinct dietary regimens and genetic groups. After a set period, body parts are separated and weighed. Statistical analysis determines which combinations yield consistent or divergent outcomes in part weights.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Diagnosis and clinical significance of Human bocavirus 1 in children hospitalized for lower acute respiratory infection: molecular detection in respiratory secretions and serum

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the prevalence of a certain virus in a group of individuals with a specific illness, compares the results to a control group, and optimizes the diagnosis by identifying the most significant factors contributing to the diagnosis. The data used is from paired samples collected from these individuals.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves testing these paired samples using a specific method, and then analyzing the results to identify the most significant factors contributing to the diagnosis, including the time of sample collection and the presence of other symptoms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The presence and persistence of a pathogen in bodily fluids are assessed across different time points and sample types to determine its diagnostic value and clinical associations.
descriptions.approach: Paired samples are collected and tested for pathogen presence using molecular amplification. Results are analyzed by comparing detection rates, co-occurrence, and disease features across time and sample types, adjusting for statistical significance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Hypomagnesemia and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the frequency of a certain condition in a population compared to a healthy group, and identifies factors that contribute to this condition. It also predicts the risk of developing a related condition based on the presence of this condition.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from a population to identify the relationship between a specific nutrient and the risk of developing a related condition. It follows a procedure of data collection, analysis, and comparison to draw conclusions about the relationship.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine the relationship between serum magnesium levels and the development of adverse cardiac outcomes, including arrhythmias and structural heart changes, in individuals with metabolic dysfunction.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model integrates longitudinal biomarker measurements, medication history, and gut microbial indicators to predict the likelihood of adverse cardiac events based on baseline and changing magnesium concentrations over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The CFPC welcomes its 2022-2023 President, Dr Christie Newton

descriptions.problem: A leader is selected through a formal process involving members' participation and voting, with the goal of identifying the most effective and representative individual for guiding organizational direction and decision-making.
descriptions.approach: Members evaluate candidates based on demonstrated leadership, experience, and alignment with organizational values. The selection process involves structured discussion, peer assessment, and a formal vote to determine the most suitable individual for the role.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Salt and Health: public awareness, attitudes, and practices in Sri Lanka to inform a behaviour change communication campaign to reduce dietary salt

descriptions.problem: A pattern of behavior related to dietary intake is assessed based on public knowledge, personal beliefs, and actual actions, using data collected from diverse community groups.
descriptions.approach: A structured model analyzes responses to health-related questions, identifies gaps between beliefs and behaviors, and maps changes in habits across different population segments using survey-based evidence.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Some Pertinent Issues for Interstellar Panspermia Raised after the Discovery of 1I/‘Oumuamua

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the origin of a mysterious object from another star system, compares it to other objects, and optimizes the likelihood of life being transferred between systems. It also explains the nature of the object and the possibility of life transfer.
descriptions.approach: The researchers review various hypotheses about the object's origin, using observations and evidence from multiple objects. They use a process of elimination and falsifiability to determine the most plausible explanation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A hypothesis about the origin of an observed object is evaluated based on its consistency with available observations and the potential for biological material to survive and transfer between systems.
descriptions.approach: Multiple origin scenarios are considered, with only one being testable through direct observation. The most plausible scenario is selected if it aligns with all observed features and allows for a mechanism by which biological material could be transported.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Scalable production of large components by industrial robots and machine tools through segmentation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal way to produce large components by breaking them down into smaller parts that can be made with standard tools. It predicts the best way to assemble these parts into a final product.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves breaking down a 3D model of the component into smaller parts using predefined connections. The parts are then assembled into a final product using a combination of standard tools and a mobile machine tool.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A complex object is divided into smaller, manageable pieces based on the physical and operational limits of available equipment. The goal is to predict how these pieces can be produced efficiently and joined together to form the complete structure.
descriptions.approach: The object's digital blueprint is split into sections matching the capabilities of existing tools. Each section is processed using a rule-based method that matches its shape and constraints to available equipment, then assembled using energy-based joining and refined with localized finishing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Water motion and pH jointly impact the availability of dissolved inorganic carbon to macroalgae

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the impact of two environmental factors on the availability of a key resource to a specific type of organism. It predicts how this resource affects the organism's ability to thrive, and compares the responses of different species to these factors.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from laboratory experiments and field surveys to determine the effect of increased water flow on the organism's ability to take in a vital resource. It then examines how different species adapt to varying levels of this resource.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's uptake efficiency of a key nutrient is assessed under varying environmental conditions, including flow and chemical concentration, to determine how these factors influence performance across different physiological strategies.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates how performance changes with flow intensity and chemical concentration, applying a rule that performance improves with flow when passive uptake is dominant, but remains stable when active mechanisms are engaged regardless of flow.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: BYLER, Darren. 2022. Terror Capitalism: Uyghur Dispossession and Masculinity in a Chinese City. Durham: Duke University Press.

descriptions.problem: A pattern of social control is observed across diverse groups in a densely populated urban environment, where individuals from different cultural backgrounds experience varying levels of monitoring and restriction based on perceived group identity and behavior.
descriptions.approach: Data is collected over time from individuals interacting in public and private spaces, and analyzed to identify how surveillance and behavioral expectations shift in response to group dynamics and institutional presence.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Comportamentos de Consumo da Criança do Ensino Básico Obrigatório em Contexto Rural e Urbano

descriptions.problem: A pattern of decision-making is estimated across different environmental settings and demographic groups, based on observed behaviors and background factors.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model compares patterns across groups using structured observations, adjusting for age and background influences to isolate environmental effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study of the effectiveness of the use of mineral water with a high content of biologically active components in experimental dermatosis

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of using a type of water rich in certain substances to treat a skin condition in animals. It aims to compare the outcomes of using this water to a standard treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a model of the skin condition in rats, applying the water every other day for 20 minutes over 6 sessions. They then examined the rats' skin and blood to see if the water had any beneficial effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's response to a repeated external stimulus is evaluated to determine how effectively it restores normal function after induced disruption.
descriptions.approach: A controlled sequence of applications is administered at regular intervals. Biological markers are monitored over time to assess recovery of cellular balance, metabolic stability, and tissue repair processes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
title: The Relationship Between Nutritional Status and The Incidence of Dysmenorrhea in Adolescent Women

descriptions.problem: This study aims to understand the connection between a person's overall health and a common problem experienced by many during their monthly cycle. It estimates the relationship between this health aspect and the problem, and it compares the results to determine if there is a significant link.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a method that involves looking at a snapshot of a group of people to see if there is a relationship between their overall health and the problem. They analyzed the data using a statistical test to determine if the results are significant.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A statistical relationship is estimated between an individual's daily dietary balance and the frequency of menstrual discomfort, using self-reported data from a group of adolescents.
descriptions.approach: Data is collected through structured questionnaires, then analyzed using a chi-square test to determine if differences in discomfort levels are significantly linked to dietary balance, with a threshold of 5% for statistical significance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: INFLUENCE OF KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT ON SERVICE QUALITY AMONG NON-TEACHING PERSONNEL IN DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION

descriptions.problem: This study aims to understand how knowledge affects the quality of service provided by non-experts in a department. It estimates the impact of different knowledge management practices on service quality.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses a statistical method to analyze data from 202 non-experts in the department. It compares the level of service quality with various knowledge management practices.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's performance is assessed based on how well internal processes support consistent, responsive, and reliable interactions with external stakeholders. The strength and nature of relationships between knowledge practices and service outcomes are evaluated using observed data.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model correlates observed service outcomes with the frequency and effectiveness of knowledge-related activities. Linear relationships are tested across multiple domains to identify which practices most strongly predict performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Effect of a magnetic field on water crystallization in tunnel drainage pipes in karst areas

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how external fields influence the formation and structure of calcium carbonate deposits in a controlled environment, comparing outcomes across varying field strengths and temperature conditions.
descriptions.approach: A computational model simulates the evolution of mineral deposits under different field intensities, adjusting the deposit morphology based on field strength and temperature, then identifies thresholds where structural transitions or formation rates stabilize.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Abstracts from international emergency medicine journals

descriptions.problem: A pattern of urgent care decisions is inferred from real-time patient data streams, including vital signs and clinical observations, to predict outcomes under time-sensitive conditions.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic model processes incoming data sequences, updating predictions continuously, and compares them against known outcomes to refine future responses in high-pressure scenarios.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Relationship between Live-In Grandparents and Grandchild’s Health and Well-Being in Palestinian Refugees in Lebanon

descriptions.problem: This study investigates the relationship between the presence of elderly caregivers in a household and the health and life outcomes of younger family members. It aims to determine whether having these caregivers at home has a positive effect on the health and life outcomes of younger family members.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data through surveys and used a statistical method to analyze the relationship between the presence of elderly caregivers and the health and life outcomes of younger family members. They controlled for other factors that might influence the results.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A statistical model estimates the influence of a household-based caregiver presence on the frequency of acute health events and consistent participation in structured educational activities, using self-reported data from multiple time points.
descriptions.approach: A multivariate regression model analyzes patterns in health event occurrence and activity engagement, adjusting for parental presence and household resource constraints, then identifies associations between caregiver presence and observed outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Mapping intertidal macrophytes in fjords in Southwest Greenland using Sentinel-2 imagery

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the distribution of certain types of underwater plants in coastal areas with limited access and monitoring. It predicts the extent of these plants in different regions and compares the results to understand the impact of certain environmental factors.
descriptions.approach: The study uses satellite images to identify and measure the area of these underwater plants. It follows a procedure that involves analyzing the images, applying certain rules to detect the plants, and then comparing the results to understand the impact of environmental factors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A spatial pattern of surface cover is estimated from high-resolution images taken at different times, where the cover is visible only under specific environmental conditions, such as low water levels or calm runoff.
descriptions.approach: A model computes a surface reflectance index from image bands, then applies a threshold to detect patches of cover. Detected patches are spatially aggregated and analyzed for size and location, with results adjusted for environmental disturbances like water movement or sediment input.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Utility of In Vivo Confocal Microscopy in Diagnosis of Acanthamoeba Keratitis: A Comparison of Patient Outcomes

descriptions.problem: This study compares the outcomes of patients with a certain eye infection, comparing those who were diagnosed and treated with or without the use of a special imaging technique. The goal is to determine if this technique can help diagnose the infection more quickly and improve patient outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The researchers looked back at the medical records of 23 patients who had the infection and compared the time it took to diagnose the infection, the patient's vision, and the need for surgery. They used a special imaging technique to help diagnose the infection in some patients, and compared the results to those who were diagnosed based on other methods.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the time between symptom onset and diagnosis, and compares patient recovery outcomes across two diagnostic strategies based on clinical and treatment records.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes patient data to compute diagnostic delays and visual outcomes, then compares these across groups using culture-based and imaging-based diagnostic methods to determine which leads to faster diagnosis and better recovery.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Facial Nerve Paralysis Treatment and Research
title: Sensory function in the faces of patients with facial palsy: A prospective observational study using quantitative sensory testing

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine the quality of touch and pressure sensations in patients with a condition that affects the muscles on one side of the face, and whether this quality is different on the affected side compared to the unaffected side.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a standardized test to assess how well patients can feel different sensations, such as heat, touch, and vibrations, on both sides of their face. They compared the results to a group of healthy people to see if there were any differences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates the integrity of somatosensory pathways in a region of the body affected by a unilateral neurological disturbance, comparing responses across sides and against established normative values.
descriptions.approach: It applies a standardized set of physical stimuli to assess how well a region detects touch, vibration, and temperature. Responses are averaged per side and compared to a reference group using statistical z-scores, with no significant differences observed between sides or over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study of Serum Calcium and Magnesium Levels in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients.

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the levels of two essential minerals in people with a specific health condition, and compares these levels to those in people who are generally healthy. It aims to explain why these minerals are important for overall health.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a non-random sampling method to select participants, and then measured the levels of these minerals in their blood. They used a statistical test to compare the results between the two groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of physiological markers is measured in individuals with a chronic metabolic condition and compared to a group of individuals without the condition to determine if differences exist and whether those differences are statistically significant.
descriptions.approach: A set of numerical values is collected from each individual and grouped by condition. A statistical test is applied to assess whether the average values differ significantly between the two groups, using a predefined threshold for significance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation
title: DriveSafe DriveAware: A systematic review

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a tool in assessing the safety of people who are no longer able to perform daily activities on their own, and compares it to a traditional assessment method. It aims to determine if the tool is reliable and useful in guiding decisions about whether someone should be allowed to continue driving.
descriptions.approach: The tool is evaluated by comparing its results to a traditional assessment method, and by assessing the tool's reliability and usefulness in different situations. The evaluation is based on a systematic review of existing research, which examines the quality of the studies and the results of the tool.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A method is evaluated to determine how well it predicts a person's ability to perform a complex, real-world task safely, based on performance in a controlled environment, and compared to direct observation in real-time.
descriptions.approach: Performance is assessed through a structured, repeatable procedure involving standardized inputs and outputs. Results are analyzed for consistency across different evaluators and time points, and judged based on time, resources, and practical application in a clinical context.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Cat scratch disease in a 23-year-old male–Case report

descriptions.problem: A pattern of symptoms is observed in a young individual, including systemic weakness and localized swelling, with laboratory tests excluding other known causes of inflammation and infection.
descriptions.approach: A clinical history is reviewed alongside physical signs and lab results. Tissue examination confirms granulomatous inflammation. The pattern is compared to known responses to exposure-based triggers, and treatment is guided by the likelihood of a specific immune-mediated reaction to an external agent.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: General medicine interns’ attitude in continuing their education in emergency medicine residency programs

descriptions.problem: A group of healthcare trainees is assessed for their interest in pursuing a specialized, high-pressure clinical role involving urgent patient care. The level of interest is measured across various personal and situational factors, including financial considerations and prior training background.
descriptions.approach: A structured survey is administered to trainees, collecting self-reported preferences and motivations. Responses are aggregated and analyzed to identify patterns, with statistical comparisons made across demographic and background variables to detect influencing factors.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Parasitic infections in humans and animals
title: Diagnostic and Management Perspectives in Alveolar Echinococcosis: Review of Literature

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the likelihood of a life-threatening condition caused by a parasite, which can lead to death within 10 years if left untreated. It compares the effectiveness of different medical tests and imaging methods to identify the condition.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves combining patient medical history, imaging findings, and test results to make an educated prediction about the presence of the condition. The goal is to optimize early detection and treatment of the condition, especially in cases with cystic growths.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood of a chronic, slowly progressing condition based on clinical history, imaging patterns, and biological test results, especially when lesions appear in a specific organ.
descriptions.approach: The system integrates historical data, visual patterns from scans, and lab markers to evaluate risk, prioritizing early detection when symptoms are absent and the condition mimics benign growths.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Fibromyalgia and Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Research
title: In Memory of Professor Derek Pheby.

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of different treatments for a group of patients with a chronic illness, comparing the outcomes of various interventions. It aims to identify the most effective approach.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from patient records and medical literature to develop a model that predicts treatment outcomes. They then tested this model on a new dataset to validate its accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood of a chronic condition worsening over time based on patient-reported symptoms and longitudinal health records.
descriptions.approach: It uses a statistical model that adjusts predictions by weighting recent symptom changes and medical history, then compares outcomes across individuals with similar profiles to identify patterns of progression.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Resolving equivocal gain modulation of corticospinal excitability

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal timing of a response to a stimulus, and compares the results to predictions made based on the timing of the stimulus. It also optimizes the analysis of the response to avoid errors.
descriptions.approach: The researchers applied a specific type of stimulation to a part of the brain, and then analyzed the response in a different part of the body. They used a technique to filter out errors and get a more accurate measurement of the response.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The pattern of how a system's response changes with the timing of a stimulus is estimated across different phases of a rhythmic cycle, and discrepancies in this pattern are identified as potential artifacts in data processing.
descriptions.approach: A stimulus is delivered at varying times relative to a measured rhythm, and the resulting output amplitude is recorded. The analysis uses broad-band processing to isolate true timing effects, avoiding distortions introduced by narrow-band filtering.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Rare Case of Pancreatic Actinomyces

descriptions.problem: This work identifies a rare case where a certain type of bacteria, commonly found in the digestive system, causes a mass in a specific organ, mimicking a serious disease. It estimates the presence of this bacteria and its impact on the organ.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used imaging tests to detect the mass, took a sample from it, and then treated the patient with antibiotics. They followed up to see if the mass resolved, and their findings emphasize the importance of considering alternative explanations for the mass.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of persistent symptoms is observed alongside a detectable mass in a bodily region, and the likelihood of a noninvasive, slow-growing microbial infection is assessed against the possibility of a rapidly progressing, destructive process.
descriptions.approach: A diagnostic procedure involves analyzing tissue samples for microbial presence and evaluating clinical history for risk factors, then comparing findings to known patterns of infection and disease progression over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Evaluation of the Digital Elevation Model from the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) on the Papaloapan Macro-Basin, Mexico, using LiDAR as benchmark

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and compares the accuracy of a digital map of the Earth's surface in a specific region, using a more precise map as a benchmark. It aims to identify areas where the map is less accurate and to suggest ways to improve it.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a precise map as a benchmark to compare the accuracy of a digital map. It then analyzes the errors and identifies patterns to suggest ways to improve the map, such as calibration or combining multiple sources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A spatial model's accuracy is assessed against a high-resolution reference dataset across diverse terrain types, measuring deviations in elevation values and analyzing how these errors relate to landscape features and orientation.
descriptions.approach: Elevation differences are computed across regions with distinct surface characteristics. Error patterns are mapped and grouped by terrain type, slope direction, and elevation bands to identify consistent biases and propose simple adjustments for improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Chiplet Placement for 2.5D IC with Sequence Pair Based Tree and Thermal Consideration

descriptions.problem: This work aims to find the most efficient way to connect components in a complex system, taking into account the heat generated by these connections. It estimates the minimum amount of material needed to connect the components, and compares it to a baseline.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a tree-like structure to represent the connections, and a method to prune branches that are unlikely to be the most efficient. It then uses a technique to optimize the connections and reduce the heat generated.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the best arrangement of interconnected components on a shared substrate to minimize signal path lengths while managing heat buildup that could degrade performance.
descriptions.approach: It builds a hierarchical structure from component interactions, evaluates arrangements through recursive pruning, and adjusts the layout based on heat propagation models to balance efficiency and thermal stability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Identification and Valuation of Economic Activities Reserves as a Priorityin Strategic Analysis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the potential value of a business's resources based on market demand, competition, supplier and customer availability, and financial indicators. It compares different methods to calculate this value and optimizes the approach to ensure the business's long-term sustainability.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a combination of direct evaluation, comparison, and mathematical programming to identify and estimate the value of the business's resources. It classifies resources into different categories and applies various methods to calculate their value.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the extent to which an organization can sustain or enhance its operations beyond current capacity by leveraging untapped capabilities, based on market demand, supplier reliability, customer behavior, and financial support.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates potential operational flexibility by comparing current performance to historical patterns and external conditions, using statistical and optimization models to assign weights to different factors and predict outcomes under varying conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 20 Best Tweets of All Time About Maxine Moseley Skin Clinics

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of various beauty treatments, predicts the outcomes of combining different treatments, and compares the results of different treatments to explain their benefits. It also optimizes the choice of treatment for individual users.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing data on the outcomes of different treatments, using a combination of non-invasive methods and expert advice to make predictions and comparisons. The procedure follows a step-by-step process of selecting treatments, evaluating their outcomes, and making recommendations for individual users.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of treatments is evaluated for their effectiveness in improving appearance and user satisfaction based on observed outcomes and reported experiences from individuals who have undergone them.
descriptions.approach: A structured sequence of procedures is applied, each designed to remove surface layers, stimulate renewal, and deliver hydration, with combinations tested to determine optimal outcomes for different user profiles.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Why we should teach the History of Ukrainian art to students of Art Schools

descriptions.problem: This research aims to explain the importance of studying the past development of a particular cultural phenomenon, which was shaped by interactions with other cultures, and to correct common misconceptions about its place in the broader cultural landscape.
descriptions.approach: The researcher uses a comparative approach, analyzing the cultural phenomenon in question alongside other similar phenomena from different cultural contexts, and presenting the findings in a way that avoids oversimplification or bias.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of creative development is analyzed across distinct cultural and political contexts, aiming to reveal how local practices are shaped by and interact with broader regional and international influences.
descriptions.approach: A comparative framework is applied to examine how artistic expressions emerge from specific historical and social conditions, integrating diverse influences while maintaining contextual integrity and avoiding oversimplified narratives.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Robust Pseudo-Markets for Reusable Public Resources

descriptions.problem: A system allocates a shared resource to multiple users over time, where each user wants to use it for a continuous period and gains value only if they receive the full period. The goal is to ensure each user receives a predictable fraction of their maximum possible benefit, regardless of how others act.
descriptions.approach: Each user starts with a fixed amount of virtual tokens representing their expected share. On each turn, users submit a request for a continuous period and a value for each unit of time. The one with the highest value for that period is granted access, with a minimum threshold ensuring fairness and stability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Economic mechanism of land use in European countries in conditions of sustainable development

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between land use and sustainable development in European countries, comparing indicators such as land area, land per person, and land prices across different countries. It aims to explain how changes in land prices will impact the formation of a transparent land market.
descriptions.approach: The study groups European countries by land ownership and land price levels, then compares these groups to identify trends and patterns in land use and development.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of resource allocation across regions is analyzed to understand how land value and usage influence long-term planning decisions in diverse settings.
descriptions.approach: Regions are grouped by the cost of accessing land per unit area. Trends in land value and usage are compared across groups to identify how pricing affects distribution and policy outcomes over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Wind turbine power control

descriptions.problem: This work aims to optimize the performance of a system that converts energy from a natural source into a usable form. It estimates the optimal settings for this system based on various environmental factors.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a mathematical model to simulate different scenarios and find the best settings. It then compares the results to real-world data to validate its findings.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system adjusts the orientation of a rotating component in response to environmental conditions to maintain stable output performance across varying input forces and flow directions.
descriptions.approach: The system continuously monitors input dynamics and applies real-time adjustments to a mechanical parameter to align output with operational constraints and external variability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Possible renoprotective mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitors

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a certain class of medications on patients with a specific disease, and compares it to the effect of a different class of medications. It also tries to explain why this effect occurs.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from previous studies to identify the mechanisms behind the effect of these medications. They follow a procedure that involves analyzing changes in blood pressure, nerve activity, and other physiological measures to understand the underlying biological processes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A biological process is investigated to explain how a drug-induced state reduces tissue damage under stress conditions, despite no direct changes in metabolic fuel availability or blood pressure.
descriptions.approach: A model proposes that the body activates a conserved survival mechanism in response to metabolic scarcity, involving changes in vascular function, local growth signals, and reduced oxidative stress to preserve tissue integrity during prolonged stress.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study on Hydrogeological Problems in Engineering Geological Investigation

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the risks associated with construction projects by analyzing the properties of the ground and its impact on the project's stability and safety. It compares the effects of various ground conditions on the project's success.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from construction sites to analyze the properties of the ground and its impact on the project's stability and safety. It proposes effective measures to minimize risks and optimize the project's success.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how underground water movement affects structural stability and project risk during early development stages, using observations from subsurface conditions and environmental signals.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes patterns in water flow through different soil layers and evaluates how changes in moisture levels influence ground behavior, adjusting predictions based on real-time environmental inputs and historical site behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A selective literature review exploring the role of the nicotinic system in schizophrenia

descriptions.problem: A pattern of behavior is assessed across multiple studies to determine whether exposure to a substance correlates with symptom reduction or disease progression in individuals with a known condition.
descriptions.approach: A systematic evaluation of research findings is conducted, filtering only those that report direct or indirect links between substance use and clinical outcomes, then analyzing consistency and strength of reported associations across diverse sources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: O-51 Occupational exposure to triazole fungicides and risk of prostate cancer in the AGRIculture and CANcer (AGRICAN) cohort

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the risk of a serious health problem (a type of disease) in people who have been exposed to certain chemicals used in agriculture, and compares the risk to that of people who have not been exposed. It also tries to explain why some people may be more or less likely to develop this disease.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data on people's exposure to these chemicals over many years, and then used a mathematical model to calculate the risk of developing the disease. They also used statistical methods to analyze the data and identify patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of health outcomes is assessed across individuals based on their exposure history to specific chemical agents used in agricultural practices, evaluating whether prolonged or repeated contact correlates with changes in disease risk over time.
descriptions.approach: Exposure durations and frequencies are mapped to known chemical agents using a crop-specific exposure model. Risk associations are estimated through statistical modeling that adjusts for time and other factors, then refined by combining exposure intensity with duration to compute cumulative exposure scores.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Invariants of a mapping of a set to the two-dimensional Euclidean space

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and predicts the existence of certain transformations that map a set to a two-dimensional plane, and compares and optimizes these transformations based on the properties of the group of orthogonal transformations.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a mathematical model to describe these transformations, which follow a specific procedure: the model uses a set of elements and a two-dimensional plane, and applies a set of rules to determine the relationships between these elements and the transformations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of points is transformed into a plane arrangement, and the goal is to determine if two such arrangements can be aligned through a combination of rotations, reflections, translations, and uniform scaling.
descriptions.approach: For each arrangement, compute a set of numerical values derived from distances and angles between points, then compare these values across arrangements to determine if they can be made identical through rigid or affine transformations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Deep learning based deep-sea automatic image enhancement and animal species classification

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the quality of low-quality images of underwater creatures and classifies them into species. It compares the results to original, unenhanced images and optimizes the classification accuracy.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a complex computer model to generate improved images from raw images, and then uses another model to classify the improved images into species. The model follows a procedure of training on a dataset, generating enhanced images, and then classifying the enhanced images into species.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the type of organism in underwater footage from low-quality visual inputs, using patterns in pixel intensity and spatial structure to assign labels with high confidence.
descriptions.approach: A neural network processes raw visual data by learning to adjust brightness, contrast, and texture to improve clarity, then classifies each frame by recognizing consistent patterns across repeated image sequences.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pseudo-noise active pulse compression thermography and multispectral imaging of the Raffaellino del Colle Sacra famiglia con San Giovanni Battista during painting restoration

descriptions.problem: This work aims to extract hidden information about the layers beneath a painting without damaging it, using a low-power energy source to avoid altering the artwork. It also seeks to understand the layering structure of the artwork.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a technique that combines data analysis and signal processing to gain insight into the hidden layers. They applied this method to a painting during restoration, using data from the painting's temperature changes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The structure and depth of layered materials beneath a surface are inferred from temperature responses induced by controlled energy input, aiming to map subsurface layers without damaging the surface.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of controlled energy pulses is applied to a surface, and the resulting temporal and spectral responses are analyzed to extract subsurface features through time-based and frequency-based signal processing.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Analisa Strategi Implementasi Green Computing pada ITS NU Sriwijaya Sumatera Selatan

descriptions.problem: A set of actions is designed to reduce energy consumption in daily operations by evaluating internal and external factors affecting efficiency and sustainability.
descriptions.approach: A structured framework analyzes existing capabilities and external conditions to identify effective interventions, such as extending device lifespan, consolidating operations, shifting to remote access models, and improving staff expertise through targeted development programs.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Systematical Characterization of the AT-Hook Gene Family in Juglans regia L. and the Functional Analysis of the JrAHL2 in Flower Induction and Hypocotyl Elongation

descriptions.problem: This work identifies and characterizes a family of proteins that help control plant growth and development, specifically flower induction and stem length. It estimates the number of proteins in this family, predicts their functions, and compares their expression in different tissues.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use evolutionary analysis to group these proteins into categories, and then study their expression patterns and subcellular localization to understand their roles in plant development.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of regulatory proteins is characterized across a plant species, with attention to their expression patterns in specific tissues and under stress conditions, and their role in developmental timing and growth regulation.
descriptions.approach: Proteins are grouped by evolutionary relationships and mapped to functional regions in the genome. Their activity is inferred from expression data and subcellular positioning, and their impact on development is tested through overexpression in a model organism.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Data Complexity for Identifying Suitable Algorithms

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the suitability of a job for a given set of tasks, based on the characteristics of the two types of tasks. This helps to choose the most efficient approach to complete the job.
descriptions.approach: A procedure is followed to categorize the tasks into simple, medium, or complex types, based on how well they can be separated. This categorization helps to identify the most suitable approach for each type of task.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A measure is estimated to assess how easily two groups of observations can be distinguished using simple boundary rules, guiding the selection of a model based on the structure of the underlying patterns in the data.
descriptions.approach: A numerical score is computed from the spread and overlap of observation values across different features. Models are then evaluated based on performance across different levels of this score to identify which perform best under varying structural conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Hot extruded Al5SiC-graphite composites: Effect of graphite on microstructure, flexural, compressive and wear resistance behavior

descriptions.problem: This work investigates how adding a certain type of material to a mixture affects its properties. It estimates and compares the effects of this material on the mixture's strength, weight loss, and friction coefficient.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created a mixture by combining the material with a base material and then tested its properties. They used a process to shape the mixture into rods and analyzed its properties using various tests.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's resistance to deformation under load and its performance under sliding contact are evaluated across different reinforcement levels and processing conditions.
descriptions.approach: A continuous process shapes powder-based material into a dense form. The resulting structure's internal arrangement and performance under stress and wear are analyzed through repeated testing under controlled conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Advances in extraction and purification of citrus flavonoids

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of various methods for extracting and isolating active compounds from a specific type of food, and compares their results to identify the most efficient approach. It also explains the characteristics of these compounds and proposes new research directions.
descriptions.approach: The work follows a systematic procedure: it reviews and summarizes existing research on the extraction and isolation of these compounds, explains their characteristics and proposed separation strategies, and describes the technical systems used for extraction and isolation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A method is developed to separate and isolate complex natural compounds from a biological matrix based on their chemical structure and solubility properties, using available physical and chemical conditions to enhance yield and purity.
descriptions.approach: A stepwise process applies solvent-based techniques and selective binding agents to partition components, followed by iterative refinement using physical separation principles like filtration, distillation, or chromatographic interaction.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Detection and Classification of Pneumonia Using Deep Learning by the Dense Net-121 Model

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the presence of a serious illness that can be life-threatening if not identified and treated promptly, based on a visual representation of the body's condition. This is done to provide timely treatment and improve patient outcomes.
descriptions.approach: A complex model is used to analyze the visual representation, and it is trained on a large dataset of examples to learn the patterns and characteristics of the illness. The model then makes a prediction about the presence of the illness based on the visual representation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood of a disease state from visual patterns in medical images, distinguishing between normal and abnormal conditions based on subtle structural differences.
descriptions.approach: A neural network processes image data through multiple layers of feature extraction, learning hierarchical patterns to classify patterns as normal or abnormal with high precision and consistency across diverse inputs.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study on Characteristics and Constituent Elements of Learning Plan from the Perspective of Deep Learning

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the effectiveness of a learning plan in promoting deep learning, predicts the impact of different design elements on student outcomes, compares the results of various approaches to learning plan design, optimizes the learning process by identifying the most effective elements, and explains the underlying principles of deep learning.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a framework that combines learning objectives, knowledge structure, problem design, scenario creation, reflection, and evaluation to create a logical process for deep learning. The approach follows a problem-oriented guide with an ideological development purpose.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A structured process is inferred from observed patterns in how individuals engage with complex tasks over time, aiming to identify key components that drive meaningful engagement and long-term retention of core ideas.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of stages is constructed, each built on prior experience and guided by real-world scenarios, where goals, challenges, and feedback loops are iteratively refined to support deeper understanding and adaptive response.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study of Succession Processes on Frozen Lignin-containing Sediments of OAO "Baikal Pulp and Paper Mill" and Soils Obtained on the Basis thereof

descriptions.problem: The rate and pattern of biological community development on degraded surfaces are monitored over time to assess how diversity and stability evolve under consistent environmental conditions.
descriptions.approach: A long-term observation system tracks changes in plant species composition and soil chemical properties, using standardized thresholds to determine when ecological stability is achieved.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Tapping into the wealth of local banana diversity for pest and disease resistance and consumer acceptability: a catalogue of the most popular cultivars in local markets across the world

descriptions.problem: A set of local varieties is analyzed to identify which ones are most frequently chosen by consumers in markets, based on observed preferences and resilience to environmental stressors.
descriptions.approach: A mapping is constructed linking geographic regions to preferred varieties, then patterns are extracted to determine which traits correlate with high selection frequency and survival under variable conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Use of paclobutrazol and ethylene in the potted production of ornamental pineapple

descriptions.problem: This work aims to understand how to make certain plants grow smaller and produce flowers faster, by testing different amounts of a plant growth regulator and a gas that helps plants produce flowers.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a special way of arranging the plants to test the effects of the plant growth regulator and the gas on the plants' growth and flower production. They tested different amounts of the gas at different times to see how it affects the plants' growth and flower production.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system determines how specific chemical treatments and timing of stimuli affect plant size, shape, and the timing of a reproductive transition, based on measurements of growth dimensions and structural form over time.
descriptions.approach: A structured experiment applies two treatment levels—presence or absence of a growth-modulating agent—and tests five distinct application times of a signaling compound. Outcomes are evaluated by comparing plant dimensions and structural ratios across treatment combinations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: CREATION OF ECOLOGISTIC ENTERPRISES OF THE FOOD AND PROCESSING INDUSTRY IN WESTERN UKRAINE

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to evaluate the economic and environmental viability of integrating sustainable practices into industrial operations, assessing how such integration benefits local communities and improves resource efficiency over time.
descriptions.approach: A phased implementation model is applied, starting with infrastructure for renewable energy generation, followed by waste-to-energy conversion, structured collection systems, and continuous monitoring of compliance with environmental standards.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Study effect of crude alcoholic extract of Hawthorn (Crataegus Oxyacantha) and crude polyphenolic compounds from blackolive (Olea Europae) fruits on some physiological parameters of kidney of male rats treated with hydrogen peroxide

descriptions.problem: A quantitative assessment of how two natural compounds influence key metabolic indicators in a biological system exposed to oxidative stress is performed, comparing outcomes across control and intervention groups.
descriptions.approach: A structured experimental design administers a stress-inducing agent over time, then measures changes in metabolic markers and tissue structure, using a defined dosing regimen and repeated sampling to evaluate protective effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: An area-based description of closed books in general practices in Aotearoa New Zealand

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the likelihood of a general practice closing its doors based on certain characteristics, predicts which areas will be most affected, and compares the impact of different factors on the number of closed practices. It also explains why some practices may close their doors.
