descriptions.approach: High-resolution 3D imaging captures the structure of these connections in multiple tissue regions. Their length, width, and frequency are analyzed, and statistical patterns are derived to reveal regional variations in density and morphology.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: What Determines the Probability of Discovering a Species? A Study of the Completeness of Bryophyte Inventories in Tianmushan National Nature Reserve (Zhejiang, China)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the number of unknown entities in a region, compares the completeness of data collection efforts, and optimizes the sampling strategy to minimize missed discoveries. It explains the importance of considering temporal turnover when assessing the completeness of data.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing the temporal dynamics of data collection, evaluating the sampling strategy, and analyzing the attributes of newly discovered entities. It uses a combination of methods to estimate the number of unknown entities and optimize the sampling strategy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The probability of detecting a new type of organism in a given area is estimated from repeated observations over time, using patterns in how often and which types of organisms appear in each observation.
descriptions.approach: A model tracks changes in observed patterns across time, identifies which types of organisms are most frequently detected in new samples, and evaluates how sampling effort and timing affect detection rates.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Throat Lozenges and Spray Containing Chlorhexidine and Lidocaine Fixed Combination Show Virucidal Activity against Respiratory Syncytial Virus and SARS-CoV-2

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a combination of two substances against two types of viruses. It predicts how well these substances can reduce the presence of these viruses in a test.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a test to see how well these substances can kill viruses. They applied the substances to a mixture of viruses and measured the remaining viruses to see how well they were killed.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effectiveness of a combined chemical agent in reducing the infectivity of airborne pathogens is estimated from repeated exposure tests using controlled environmental conditions and quantified pathogen load measurements.
descriptions.approach: A standardized exposure protocol is applied, where the pathogen is exposed to the agent, and the resulting decrease in biological activity is measured over time through direct counting of surviving units.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Comprehensive Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Profiling of bHLH Transcription Factors in Areca catechu Under Abiotic Stress

descriptions.problem: This work identifies and studies the role of a large family of proteins that help control how plants grow and respond to their environment, specifically in a plant under stress. It estimates how these proteins behave under different conditions and compares their behavior to that of other similar proteins.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of computer analysis and experimental testing to identify and study these proteins. They start by looking at how these proteins are related to each other and then test how they behave under different conditions, such as drought and salt.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is estimated that identifies and tracks the activity levels of a group of regulatory proteins across different tissues under environmental stress conditions.
descriptions.approach: A hierarchical classification is built to group similar proteins based on sequence similarity. Expression levels of selected proteins are then monitored in response to two distinct environmental challenges, revealing patterns of activation in different tissue types.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Quantifying Power Effects of Unbalanced and Nonlinear Consumers in Three-phase Networks: A Theoretical Review and Experimental Verification

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of unbalanced and complex devices on a large-scale energy system, comparing their effects on energy consumption and costs. It aims to optimize the performance of the system by penalizing polluting components and rewarding or discharging others.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a mathematical framework to analyze the energy behavior of these devices, integrating their effects over time to measure and bill energy usage. This framework is applied to experimental data to validate the results and provide a generalizable model.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A method is developed to measure and compare the impact of asymmetric load behavior on three-phase systems, evaluating how energy distribution and consumption patterns deviate under real-world operating conditions.
descriptions.approach: A mathematical framework assigns time-dependent values to energy flow components, separating them into balanced and unbalanced parts, then validates these through controlled experiments with physical systems.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Activity-Based Learning for Literacy Development Among Non-Teaching Staff Strategies and Outcomes

descriptions.problem: This study aims to estimate the effectiveness of a new method for improving the reading skills of non-professional workers in educational settings, using data from their daily activities. It compares the outcomes of this method with traditional learning approaches.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a model that follows these steps: (1) it collects data on the daily activities of non-professional workers, (2) it applies the new method to these activities, (3) it compares the results with those from traditional learning approaches, and (4) it optimizes the new method based on the outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A method is developed to assess how structured, hands-on activities influence the ability of individuals to perform routine tasks involving written information in low-resource environments.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of experiential exercises is designed, delivered in short sessions, and evaluated through performance in real-world scenarios to measure improvement in information processing and response accuracy over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: DysRegNet: Patient‐specific and confounder‐aware dysregulated network inference towards precision therapeutics

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationships between different types of data (e.g. expression levels, mutations, promoter methylation) to identify patterns of regulation that are unique to each individual. It also compares these patterns to known characteristics of the individual (e.g. age, sex, treatment history).
descriptions.approach: The method uses a combination of data from multiple sources to build a network of relationships. It then scales this network to accommodate large amounts of data and highlights the impact of certain factors (e.g. age) on the patterns of regulation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates subtle, individual-specific changes in biological interactions from bulk expression measurements, comparing them across known demographic and treatment variables to detect patterns influenced by external factors.
descriptions.approach: It processes expression data through a scalable network model that adjusts for known covariates, then applies a clustering and weighting rule to highlight interactions that vary systematically with context.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 12-HETE, a Platelet Specific Oxylipin, As an Early Diagnostic Indicator for Thrombotic Risk

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the risk of a serious blood clot forming in the arteries, and identifies a specific molecule that is produced when platelets are activated. It aims to find a reliable way to detect this risk early, so that more aggressive treatment can be given before a serious clot forms.
descriptions.approach: The researchers measured the levels of a molecule in the blood, and compared them to levels in people who are healthy and those who have a condition that increases the risk of blood clots. They also looked at other signs of platelet activation and tested the blood's ability to form clots.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A measurable compound derived from platelet activity is assessed to detect early signs of a hypercoagulable state before clot formation occurs, distinguishing individuals with heightened clotting potential from those without, using blood-based signals.
descriptions.approach: The compound's concentration is measured in blood samples, and its levels are compared across individuals with and without elevated clotting risk, while controlling for known suppressive treatments. A dynamic range and stability over time are leveraged to detect subtle shifts before observable clot events occur.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Does the TruBlue Laser Set Microlaryngoscopy Equipment on Fire? A Systematic Evaluation

descriptions.problem: The risk of unintended ignition is assessed when a focused energy source interacts with various medical devices and materials under controlled exposure conditions.
descriptions.approach: A series of controlled exposures are conducted, varying distance, contact duration, and material composition. Outcomes are recorded for ignition, smoke production, and structural damage to evaluate safety thresholds and failure modes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: MINOCA as the result of coronary artery aneurysm thrombosis

descriptions.problem: A rare mechanism for heart muscle damage is identified when a dilated vessel segment becomes obstructed by a clot, despite no significant narrowing of the vessel itself.
descriptions.approach: Vessel segments are imaged to detect abnormal dilation and the presence of a clot within them. Clinical history and imaging data are analyzed to link the clot formation to a prior surgical event and to assess recovery outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: PREVENTION OF ONCOLOGICAL OCCUPATION DISEASES

descriptions.problem: Estimate the impact of climate change on the availability and affordability of healthy and cheap options for a large population, and assess the effectiveness of current measures to address this issue.
descriptions.approach: Use historical data on global economic recoveries and market transformations to inform predictions about the future, and apply this knowledge to optimize policies and interventions aimed at ensuring universal access to healthy and affordable options.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the impact of external disruptions on essential resource distribution and population access to basic sustenance under changing environmental and structural conditions.
descriptions.approach: It models how shifts in supply networks and external pressures alter resource availability, using historical patterns and real-time indicators to forecast vulnerabilities and recommend adaptive strategies for maintaining stability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A crucial active site network of titratable residues guides catalysis and NAD + binding in human succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the importance of specific residues in an enzyme's active site and how they interact with a crucial molecule. It predicts how these interactions affect the enzyme's function and optimizes the enzyme's performance.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of computer simulations and experiments to analyze the enzyme's behavior. They identified a network of weak bonds between the enzyme's residues and the crucial molecule, which is essential for its function.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A mechanism is inferred that regulates the binding of a cofactor and the transformation of a substrate into a product, where the binding and reaction steps are interdependent and influenced by the chemical environment and pH.
descriptions.approach: A network of residues is identified that stabilizes the cofactor through weak interactions, and a sequence of events is mapped where proton transfer between specific sites enables the reaction to proceed efficiently under physiological conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A Robust and Efficient Representation‐based DNA Storage Architecture by Deep Learning

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the quality of images from noisy data, predicts the original image from the noisy data, and compares the quality of images with different levels of noise. It also optimizes the trade-off between image quality and compression ratio by selecting the best representation channel number.
descriptions.approach: The work uses two deep learning models: one to refine the noisy data and another to generate images from the refined data. It follows a procedure where the models are trained on a dataset of noisy images and then used to generate images from the noisy data.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the most likely original form of a complex visual signal from degraded and corrupted copies, using patterns learned from large sets of similar signals.
descriptions.approach: It uses a deep neural network to compress the signal into a compact, structured form, then refines it using a network trained to generate plausible outputs from noisy inputs, adjusting fidelity based on available copies.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Managing Pneumothorax in Neurofibromatosis Type 1: A Report of a Rare Case

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the effectiveness of a minimally invasive procedure for managing a specific complication in a genetic disorder, and to compare the outcomes of this approach with traditional methods. It also aims to explain the importance of tailored intervention in managing this complication.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves using a mechanical device to remove a specific type of lung tissue, and then using a special powder to help the lung re-expand. The approach is minimally invasive and effective, as shown by the successful recovery of the patient.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A patient with a chronic genetic condition affecting connective tissue presents with a sudden onset of respiratory distress and imaging-confirmed lung collapse. The likelihood and severity of this collapse are assessed based on clinical history and imaging findings.
descriptions.approach: A minimally invasive procedure is performed to relieve pressure and prevent recurrence. The lung's structural integrity is evaluated, and a substance is applied to promote adhesion and prevent future collapse.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Relapsing Polychondritis: A ‘Revival’ in the American Indian/Alaska Native population

descriptions.problem: A pattern of recurrent, severe inflammation affecting connective tissues is identified and documented across multiple individuals from a specific cultural group over time.
descriptions.approach: Clinical records and medical histories are reviewed to detect recurring episodes of inflammation in cartilaginous and supportive tissues, and these are compared across individuals to identify shared features and potential triggers.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
title: Improving fertilization rates in IVF using rutin and quercetin in preculture medium or through oral administration

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the chances of successful reproduction in animals by investigating the effects of certain compounds on their reproductive health. It estimates the impact of these compounds on the reproductive success of animals.
descriptions.approach: The researchers added these compounds to the food or drink of the animals before they reproduced, or gave them to the animals orally, and then measured the outcome. They used mice as test subjects and compared the results to see if the compounds had a positive effect.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The success rate of combining gametes in a controlled environment is enhanced by adding specific bioactive molecules to the culture conditions or through direct delivery to an organism.
descriptions.approach: A compound is introduced into a liquid environment where cells are exposed to it before a key biological interaction. Alternatively, the compound is delivered directly to an organism to influence its internal state and improve outcomes of a reproductive event.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Médecine d’urgence : ce qui a changé en 2024

descriptions.problem: This research aims to estimate the effectiveness of different approaches to managing a specific condition in emergency situations, comparing the outcomes of various interventions and predicting the likelihood of a particular complication. It also seeks to explain the underlying factors contributing to these outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from emergency department records and medical literature to develop and test predictive models, and to evaluate the impact of different interventions on patient outcomes.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is developed to forecast the likelihood of a severe internal infection based on patient symptoms, vital signs, and time-based clinical observations.
descriptions.approach: The system analyzes patterns in real-time health data over time, applying statistical rules to identify early warning signals, then adjusts predictions as new observations are added to improve accuracy.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Is intraoperative neuromonitoring the standard of care for pedicle screw placement surgery? A survey of neurosurgeons’ practices

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the standard of care for a specific medical procedure, comparing the use of a particular technology to determine its effectiveness and necessity. It also compares opinions on the technology's implementation across different practice types and locations.
descriptions.approach: The researchers surveyed a large group of medical practitioners, analyzing their responses using a statistical test to identify patterns and trends. They used a specific statistical method and software to analyze the data and draw conclusions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A practice pattern is assessed across a group of medical professionals to determine how frequently a specific real-time feedback technique is used during spinal procedures, and how strongly it is believed to prevent adverse outcomes.
descriptions.approach: A structured questionnaire is distributed to practitioners, and responses are aggregated and compared across different settings. Statistical analysis evaluates the consistency of usage and beliefs across demographic and operational groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: ASSESSMENT OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF PHYTOTHERAPY FOR SECONDARY IMMUNODEFICIENCY CONDITIONS

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a treatment on a group of people with a common condition, characterised by a specific imbalance in their cells. It compares the results of this treatment to the outcomes of people without this condition.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from patients with this condition to train a model that predicts the outcome of the treatment. They then tested this model on a separate group of patients to see if it accurately predicted the results of the treatment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A measure of disease recurrence frequency is estimated from patient records over time, comparing outcomes under different treatment regimens based on observed health events and environmental exposure levels.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model assigns weights to treatment variables and environmental factors, then predicts infection rates using historical patterns and adjusts for baseline health indicators to identify treatment effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 20-Year income volatility and cognitive function in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (1979) cohort: A replication and extension of CARDIA findings

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the relationship between 20-year changes in income stability and cognitive function in young adults, using data from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth. It compares the effects of income instability on cognitive function, controlling for earlier-life cognitive abilities.
descriptions.approach: The study uses statistical models to analyze the data, averaging z-scores on various cognitive tasks to assess cognitive function. It then examines the association between income instability and cognitive function, adjusting for earlier-life cognitive skills.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A longitudinal pattern is estimated linking financial instability during early to mid-adulthood with performance on cognitive tasks assessed later in life, controlling for earlier cognitive abilities.
descriptions.approach: Annual or semi-annual financial changes are quantified by measuring variation in income levels and the frequency of sharp declines. Cognitive performance is averaged across multiple task outcomes, and statistical models link these financial patterns to later cognitive outcomes while adjusting for early cognitive performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Parasitic infections in humans and animals
title: The Management Pathway of Patients with Cystic Echinococcosis in Iran Prior to Definitive Surgical Treatment

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the time it takes for individuals to receive treatment for a serious illness, compares the effectiveness of different healthcare providers, and identifies the underlying causes of delays in receiving proper care. It also explains the factors that contribute to these delays.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of face-to-face interviews and review of medical records to gather information about the time it takes for individuals to receive treatment. The data is then analyzed to identify patterns and trends in the healthcare-seeking process.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A sequence of healthcare interactions is analyzed to determine how long it takes for an individual to receive a confirmed diagnosis and a curative intervention after initial symptoms appear.
descriptions.approach: Data from multiple medical encounters are collected and reviewed to map the progression of care, including diagnostic tests and decisions made at each stage, to identify delays and underlying barriers affecting timely treatment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A sustainable breakthrough in rodent pest control: laboratory validation of novel neem-andrographolide bait with dual toxic and contraceptive effects

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of a new method for controlling a pest that damages physical structures and spreads diseases. It predicts the impact of this method on the pest's population and breeding potential.
descriptions.approach: The researchers tested the new method by feeding a group of animals a special food for 15 days, and then observed their behavior and physical changes. They repeated the test after 30 days to see if the effects were long-lasting.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A compound is administered to a group of animals to assess its impact on survival, body mass, reproductive organ size, hormonal levels, and mating behavior over time.
descriptions.approach: Animals are exposed to a formulated substance for a set duration under controlled conditions. After exposure, physiological and behavioral outcomes are measured at multiple time points to evaluate long-term effects on population dynamics and reproductive function.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: GEORREFERENCIACIÓN DE FOTOGRAFIAS AÉREAS PARA GIS EMPLEANDO NAVEGADORES GPS

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the location of objects in a map, using limited information about the objects' surroundings. This is done to create a map with accurate locations.
descriptions.approach: The approach is to use a combination of data from GPS devices and software to project images onto a map system, allowing for the creation of accurate locations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: Spatial positions of images are aligned with a known coordinate system using sparse control points derived from precise location data.
descriptions.approach: Image coordinates are mapped to a defined grid using GPS-derived reference points, then transformed into a standard projection system through mathematical alignment, ensuring consistent spatial accuracy across large agricultural areas.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Субъект-объектная интерпретация юриспруденции как деятельности в сфере услуг

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the importance of a concept in a specific context, comparing its impact on various aspects of a system. It predicts how this concept affects the behavior of different entities within that system.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a specific framework to analyze the concept, focusing on its role in shaping rules and standards that govern interactions between entities. They examine the characteristics of these interactions, including the relationships between various participants.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The process estimates how decisions are made and enforced in interactions between service providers, users, and regulatory bodies, evaluating factors that either support or obstruct fair and effective resolution of disputes.
descriptions.approach: A framework maps the roles and behaviors of participants in service-based interactions, analyzing how rules, expectations, and power dynamics influence outcomes and the consistency of fair treatment across different cases.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Investigation on Thermal Conductivity of Soil Under Freeze–Thaw Action Based on Machine Learning Models

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of a certain type of material under specific environmental conditions, comparing the results to a baseline model. It aims to predict the material's behavior based on historical data and evidence.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves training a set of models using a combination of data and optimization techniques to find the best fit. The models are then evaluated based on their accuracy and stability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how a material's ability to transfer heat changes under repeated environmental stress, using observed patterns from controlled experiments involving temperature fluctuations and material composition.
descriptions.approach: A set of adaptive algorithms processes input variables to generate predictions, with parameters refined through iterative optimization. Predictions are evaluated using error metrics and robustness tests to determine consistency across different conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Fibrils of Bambusa tulda Roxb. as a sustainable material for composites: Their characteristics within the culm wall

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal characteristics of different parts of a plant material for use in a specific application, comparing and optimising its properties to determine the best section to use. It aims to explain how to select the most suitable part of the material for a particular purpose.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a combination of morphological, chemical, tensile, and thermal analysis to evaluate the properties of different sections of the material. It follows a procedure where each section is individually examined and compared to determine the best section for use in a specific application.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's physical and chemical traits are assessed across distinct radial layers of a plant structure to determine which layers best suit specific functional applications.
descriptions.approach: The material is divided into segments along its radial axis, and each segment undergoes analysis for composition, mechanical strength, thermal behavior, and surface structure to identify optimal performance under different usage conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Clinical spectrum and outcome of nocardiosis in Oman: a case series from a single center

descriptions.problem: An estimate is made of the spread and severity of a chronic, often undiagnosed infection in a population with weakened immunity, based on observed patterns in patient records over time.
descriptions.approach: Patient data is reviewed to identify patterns in symptoms, progression, and response to treatment. A treatment protocol is applied based on laboratory results, and outcomes are tracked to assess effectiveness and guide future decisions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A New Model Based on Folate Receptor-Positive Circulating Tumor Cells for the Preoperative Prediction of Peritoneal Metastasis in Gastrointestinal Malignancies: A Retrospective Study in China

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a certain type of cancer spreading to a specific part of the body, based on the number of abnormal cells in the blood. It compares this likelihood to the presence of other factors that might indicate a higher risk of spreading.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from past cases to train a model that can predict the risk of cancer spreading. They tested the model by dividing the data into smaller groups and checking how well it performed in each group.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood of a disease spreading beyond a primary site based on circulating cell counts and clinical indicators such as tumor stage and lymph node involvement.
descriptions.approach: It uses a statistical model that assigns weights to cell levels and patient features, then combines them into a score. This score is evaluated across repeated data splits to ensure consistent performance in predicting disease spread risk.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Applications of Generation of ZZ Transform for Solving Linear Volterra Integral Equations of Second Type

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the exact solution to a mathematical problem involving a type of equation that describes how a function changes over time, based on past values of the function. It compares this solution to a known solution, and optimizes the process of finding the solution.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a mathematical transformation to simplify the problem, and then applies a set of rules to find the solution. It uses historical data of the function to train a model that can predict the solution.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A precise solution is derived from a system of sequential dependencies where past values influence future ones, using observed input-output patterns over time.
descriptions.approach: A transformation is applied to convert the sequential dependency into a simpler algebraic form, enabling direct computation of future values from initial conditions through recursive operations.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Functions of strategic risk management of agri-food enterprises

descriptions.problem: This work estimates and predicts the impact of various external factors on a particular type of business, comparing their effects on financial stability and competitiveness. It also explains how to minimize these negative impacts and find opportunities for growth.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves using statistical analysis, scenario modeling, and other methods to analyze and assess risks, and then using this information to make informed management decisions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system continuously monitors and evaluates external and internal variables to anticipate disruptions, diagnose current conditions, prevent adverse outcomes, protect core operations, adjust to environmental shifts, and maintain ongoing oversight of performance.
descriptions.approach: A multi-layered framework processes real-time and historical inputs using statistical patterns, hypothetical scenarios, strength and weakness assessments, and environmental feedback loops to generate adaptive responses and maintain operational resilience.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Factors Influencing Algorithmic News Apps Use and Its Impact on Media Literacy

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the factors that influence how people use a system that recommends content based on their past interactions, and how this use affects their ability to critically evaluate the information they receive.
descriptions.approach: The study compares the impact of different features, such as protecting users' rights and interests, and content preferences, on how people use this system, and optimizes the system's design to improve its effectiveness.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system identifies key personal and environmental factors that influence how frequently and consistently individuals interact with a personalized information stream and assesses how well they understand the sources and context of the content presented.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes user behavior over time, evaluates the design features of the interface, and measures the alignment between user expectations and the content delivered, using statistical models to detect patterns and relationships.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: DO INTERNATIONAL REGULATIONS FORCE TRANSPORT COMPANIES TO REDUCE THEIR CARBON EMISSIONS?

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine whether international regulations require transport operators to reduce their carbon emissions. It estimates the impact of regulations on transport operators' decisions to purchase new vehicles.
descriptions.approach: The study analyzes data from almost 10,000 trucks with a mass of more than 7.5 tons to understand the relationship between earnings, inflation, and the decision to buy new vehicles. It uses a model to compare the influence of these factors on the decision to purchase new vehicles.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how external policy pressures influence the replacement of aging operational units in a network of transport assets.
descriptions.approach: A model correlates economic indicators and infrastructure conditions with decisions to replace or retain older units, using historical data on asset age and economic performance to predict future replacement patterns.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Digital Aesthetic Education: Empowering Innovation and Practice of Traditional Culture

descriptions.problem: This work aims to understand and describe the impact of a new approach to teaching skills that involve creativity and appreciation of traditional culture on students' quality of life and skills. It estimates the effectiveness of this approach based on data from students who have used it.
descriptions.approach: The work uses a combination of data analysis and comparison to evaluate the effectiveness of this approach. It follows a procedure that involves analyzing existing data, identifying trends and patterns, and drawing conclusions about the impact of this approach on students' skills and quality of life.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to assess how effectively cultural practices are preserved and transmitted through interactive, technology-mediated experiences.
descriptions.approach: It maps user engagement patterns across platforms and correlates them with participation in cultural activities, using feedback loops to refine content delivery and learning pathways over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Cytotoxic Effects of Citrus Peels on Breast Tumor: Opportunities for Waste to Raw Material Conversion

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the potential of a certain type of plant material to kill cancer cells, and compares it to other similar materials. It also predicts the effects of these materials on human cells and explains the underlying reasons for these effects.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of laboratory experiments and computer simulations to investigate the properties of the plant material. They isolated and analyzed specific molecules from the material to understand their effects on human cells.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of a natural extract on cancer cell viability is assessed using cell culture models to determine its ability to inhibit cell growth.
descriptions.approach: A series of fractions are separated from a plant-derived extract, and their impact on cells is tested. Molecular simulations support experimental findings by predicting interactions with cellular targets.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Wood-based textile innovations in the Finnish media: A critical discourse analysis

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the level of support for wood-based innovations in the media, predicts their potential impact on the market, compares the coverage of different types of innovations, optimizes the effectiveness of the media in promoting these innovations, and explains the limitations of the current discussion.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a critical analysis of media articles to identify the tone and content of the coverage, and to compare the representation of different types of innovations, using a theoretical framework to guide the analysis and provide recommendations for improvement.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of societal innovations made from renewable biological sources is evaluated based on how they are represented in public communication, focusing on their perceived environmental, economic, and social value and the presence of critical or alternative viewpoints.
descriptions.approach: A systematic review of public media content is conducted, analyzing how these innovations are framed, what benefits are emphasized, and whether challenges or alternative perspectives are included in the narratives.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Abstract 2708: Prediction of radiosensitivity in glioblastoma tumors after standard and low dose rates of ionizing radiation

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of varying levels of energy production on the ability of cells to survive and proliferate, and compares the impact of different levels of oxygen availability on this effect. It also explains how changes in the physical properties of the cells' surroundings affect their response to a particular treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of experiments and data analysis to investigate the relationship between energy production, oxygen levels, and cell behavior. They apply a range of conditions and measurements to understand how these factors influence the cells' response to a treatment.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how cellular energy dynamics and migration behavior change under varying oxygen levels and mechanical stress during exposure to ionizing energy pulses.
descriptions.approach: It simulates energy production shifts under different environmental conditions by applying controlled stress and oxygen fluctuations, then maps how cellular responses evolve over time in response to energy input and physical constraints.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Relationship between the VUCA Environment and Managers' Decision-Making Styles

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand how the level of uncertainty, complexity, and unpredictability in a workplace affects the way people make decisions. It estimates the relationship between these factors and the way people make decisions, using data from a survey of 90 people in a hospital.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a survey to collect data from 90 people, and then analyzed the data to see if there was a connection between the level of uncertainty and the way people make decisions. They also looked for patterns in the data to see if the level of uncertainty affects the way people make decisions over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern is identified in how individuals make choices under conditions of changing, unpredictable, and intricate circumstances. The strength and nature of this pattern are assessed across different experience levels and compared to the level of environmental intricacy.
descriptions.approach: Individuals are observed in real-time or self-reported during periods of dynamic stress. Their choice patterns are analyzed and linked to the duration of exposure to such conditions using statistical correlation and group comparison.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A review on arjuna and hawthorn and their role in cardiovascular health

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of two plants in improving heart health, compares their benefits to other treatments, and optimizes their potential use in treating various heart-related illnesses.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from recent clinical trials to summarize the research on the plants' ability to lower blood pressure, increase circulation, and have antioxidant properties, highlighting their potential synergistic effects.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A model estimates the biological effects of two plant-based compounds on heart function and blood vessel health, based on observed changes in lipid levels, circulation, and oxidative stress markers from clinical and laboratory studies.
descriptions.approach: The model integrates data from trials and traditional observations to predict how these compounds influence metabolic and circulatory systems, evaluating their combined and individual impacts on disease progression and physiological balance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Undefinable True Target Learning

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate or predict something that cannot be precisely defined, and to explain why this is necessary or important. This is done using data or evidence that shows the absence of a clear target.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves proposing a fundamental assumption that the target does not exist in reality, and then using this assumption to develop a theoretical foundation for handling situations where the target cannot be precisely defined.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system must learn to perform a task when the ideal outcome cannot be observed or measured directly in practice.
descriptions.approach: It uses a model that adapts by continuously refining its predictions based on real-world feedback, even when the perfect target is absent, and treats discrepancies as essential signals for improving performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

subfield: Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation
title: Physical education teachers’ experiences of the meaning of feedback in PE

descriptions.problem: This study investigates how new professionals in a field that involves training others in physical activities experience the value of feedback in their work. It aims to understand how feedback is used, its purpose, and what it contains, and whether the training they received prepares them for this task.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected data through interviews and group discussions with eight new professionals, and then analyzed the data to understand how they experience feedback in their work. They used a method that helps identify how people think and feel about something, and how it relates to their goals and activities.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The ways in which instructional responses are interpreted and applied by individuals during practice are examined, particularly in relation to learning objectives and immediate activity outcomes.
descriptions.approach: Participants reflect on specific instances of responses given during instruction, and these are categorized based on how they connect to intended learning goals or remain disconnected from them.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
title: Diazepine Agonists of the 5-HT2C Receptor with Unprecedented Selectivity: Discovery of Bexicaserin (LP352)

descriptions.problem: A compound is evaluated for its ability to modulate a specific biological target with high precision, distinguishing it from closely related targets and assessing its performance in living systems through behavioral and pharmacokinetic outcomes.
descriptions.approach: A scaffold is modified by introducing a specific functional group to enhance target engagement while reducing unwanted metabolic degradation, followed by iterative refinement to improve stability, delivery, and functional response in vivo.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Defect detection in CFRP combining SK-means clustering and probability of detection analysis

descriptions.problem: This work aims to identify hidden flaws in a type of material used in many products, by analyzing images of the material's surface. It estimates the likelihood of these flaws being present, and compares this to other methods of flaw detection.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a modified version of a clustering technique to group similar images together, and then used a probability analysis to determine how likely it is that the flaws are actually present. They tested this approach against other methods and found it to be more effective.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the presence and location of hidden anomalies within a material by analyzing spatial and temporal variations in a measured signal.
descriptions.approach: The system divides the signal into smaller, overlapping segments and clusters them based on similarity patterns. It then evaluates the likelihood that each segment corresponds to an anomaly using statistical thresholds derived from known signal behavior.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 3D reconstruction by holography and pseudo 3D perception by arial 2D image

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the characteristics of 3D perception from 2D images, predicts how objects appear in 3D, and compares these predictions to real-world observations. It aims to optimise the way we understand and interpret 3D visual information.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves creating large, transparent screens using mechanical components and computer technology. It uses computer algorithms to calculate and process visual data, and compares the results to real-world observations of 2D images.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The system estimates how a two-dimensional image can induce a three-dimensional visual experience when viewed under specific conditions, using patterns of light and observer movement.
descriptions.approach: It processes visual input by simulating depth cues through spatial frequency modulation and directional light patterns, then applies a transformation that maps 2D input to a perceptual depth effect based on viewer position and viewing angle.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Productive and economical performance evaluation of V-line male growing rabbits as affcted by feed restriction

descriptions.problem: This study aims to determine how different methods of managing a group of young, healthy animals affect their growth and productivity. It estimates the impact of these methods on their weight, efficiency, and economic value.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a controlled experiment with three groups of animals, each with a different method of managing their food intake. They measured the animals' weight, efficiency, and economic value over a set period of time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The performance of growing animals under different feeding regimes is assessed to compare growth rate, resource use efficiency, and financial returns across groups with varying intake schedules.
descriptions.approach: Animals are assigned to groups with distinct intake patterns: continuous intake, reduced intake, or alternating intake cycles. Growth, resource consumption, and financial outcomes are tracked over time to evaluate which pattern maximizes output per unit of input.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Innovative Projects Pjsc "Chernomorsudo-proekt"for the Offshore Industry

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the performance of various types of vessels, predicts their efficiency, compares different designs, and optimizes their features based on data from existing vessels.
descriptions.approach: The procedure follows a model that evaluates and refines vessel designs by analyzing data on their speed, capacity, and fuel efficiency, and uses this information to identify the most suitable features for each type of vessel.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of vessel designs is evaluated for operational efficiency under diverse environmental and mission conditions, with the goal of identifying configurations that optimize response time, resource delivery, and safety in dynamic, remote settings.
descriptions.approach: A structured framework compares design variants based on performance metrics under varying stressors, using historical operational data and simulated environmental inputs to rank and refine configurations iteratively.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Pneumothorax

descriptions.problem: A system detects a sudden increase in pressure within a confined space, which may impair overall function and cause a shift in bodily balance, leading to reduced efficiency in fluid return and oxygen exchange.
descriptions.approach: Pressure changes are monitored over time; if a rapid rise occurs with signs of reduced performance, a quick release mechanism is activated to restore normal conditions, with a simple tool used in emergencies and a more controlled method applied when the situation is less urgent.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A comprehensive investigation of the 3D printed polylactic acid/yttria-stabilized zirconia nanocomposite scaffold for orthopedic applications

descriptions.problem: This research investigates the properties of a new material made from combining two substances to improve its strength and biological compatibility. It aims to estimate the optimal combination of these substances and the resulting material's performance.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created different versions of the material by varying the proportion of the second substance and examining its properties using various tests. They then compared the results to determine the best combination and its performance.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A material's strength and resistance to bacterial growth are evaluated under varying reinforcement levels and internal structural designs to determine optimal performance for tissue repair applications.
descriptions.approach: A set of layered, porous structures is fabricated with different filler concentrations and internal geometries. Performance is assessed through stress response, degradation behavior, and surface fracture analysis under controlled environmental conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Impact of Audible Sound on In vitro Growth of Algae

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of different sound frequencies on the growth and biochemical changes of a type of plant-like organism that makes its own food. It compares the growth of these organisms in response to varying sound frequencies and intensities.
descriptions.approach: The researchers applied different sound frequencies to a group of these organisms and measured their growth and biochemical changes. They used a specific range of sound frequencies and intensities to test the impact on the organisms' growth and biochemical parameters.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The effect of specific sound frequencies and intensities on the rate of growth and biochemical changes in a photosynthetic, autotrophic organism is measured under controlled laboratory conditions.
descriptions.approach: A set of sound stimuli with defined frequencies and amplitudes is applied to a culture of the organism. Growth and metabolic markers are monitored over time to determine how the stimuli influence development and internal chemical activity.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Inherited Lipodystrophy Associated With POLD1 and CAVIN1 Mutations: Two Cases From the Indian Subcontinent

descriptions.problem: This work identifies the genetic causes of a rare disorder that affects the body's ability to store fat, leading to metabolic problems and other complications. It estimates the likelihood of this disorder based on genetic mutations and compares it to known cases.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a genetic testing method to identify the mutations that cause the disorder. They follow a procedure that involves analyzing the genetic code of the affected individuals to determine the underlying cause.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of systemic symptoms is identified in two individuals, including early onset of metabolic disease and distinctive physical features, and is linked to specific genetic variants through analysis of DNA sequence data.
descriptions.approach: Genomic data is scanned across all protein-coding regions to detect rare, likely causative variants; these variants are then correlated with clinical symptoms to establish a biological association and infer disease mechanism.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The role of nuclear energy in reducing carbon dioxide emissions

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of a certain type of power generation on the amount of a specific pollutant released into the atmosphere, comparing it to other methods of power generation.
descriptions.approach: It uses data on the amount of a certain type of fuel burned to produce power, and the amount of a specific pollutant released as a result, to make a prediction about the overall impact on the atmosphere.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A long-term projection of greenhouse gas output is made based on the operational characteristics of a stable, continuous process that produces power without releasing gaseous byproducts during use.
descriptions.approach: A model simulates the impact of a consistent, weather-independent process on overall gas release over decades, adjusting for known technical and economic constraints and integrating it with variable natural resource availability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Experimental study of cement replacement with tea waste in rigid pavements

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the strength of a new material made by replacing a key component with a cheaper alternative. It compares the results to a standard material to see if the new material is strong enough.
descriptions.approach: The researchers made different batches of the new material with varying amounts of the cheaper alternative, and then tested its strength over time. They used a series of tests to measure the material's strength and compared the results to a standard material.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The mechanical robustness of a composite material is assessed under varying substitution levels and time intervals to determine if it meets performance thresholds required for structural applications.
descriptions.approach: Specimens are prepared with incremental levels of a natural byproduct, tested at multiple time points for flexural, tensile, and compressive resistance, and compared against a standard reference material to evaluate structural integrity over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Beyond Benign or Malignant: A Complex Case of Anomalous Left Main Coronary Artery with Transseptal Course

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the clinical significance of a rare anatomical variant, comparing its impact on heart function and predicting the risk of serious complications. It also explains the importance of comprehensive evaluation and individualized patient management.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of imaging techniques and functional testing to assess the patient's condition, guiding their management decisions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's behavior under varying physiological conditions is assessed to determine whether structural features lead to functional impairment, especially when combined with dynamic mechanical stress.
descriptions.approach: Multiple imaging techniques are integrated to map spatial anatomy and functional responses over time, with stress-induced changes monitored to evaluate risk of tissue damage or performance degradation.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Dysregulation of the Lipidome and Gut Microbiome Advances the Progression of Diabetic Nephropathy After Chronic High-Fat Diet Feeding

descriptions.problem: A system's response to chronic dietary stress is measured to detect changes in metabolic signaling and microbial balance that drive tissue damage over time.
descriptions.approach: Metabolic profiles and microbial composition are tracked across age and diet groups; key inflammatory and repair-related molecules are compared, and shifts in microbial diversity are linked to worsening tissue injury markers.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: GHMP gene family: identification, evolutionary and expression analysis under various exogenous hormones and abiotic stress in tomato

descriptions.problem: This work identifies and analyzes a family of proteins that help regulate growth and development in a certain type of plant, and examines how they respond to different environmental conditions. It estimates the number of proteins in this family, compares their structure and function, and explains their role in the plant's responses.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of computational and experimental methods to analyze the proteins, including comparing their structure and function, identifying patterns in their distribution, and examining how they respond to different conditions. They follow a procedure that involves identifying the proteins, analyzing their structure and function, and comparing their responses to different conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A set of structurally related proteins is analyzed to determine how their expression patterns vary across different tissues and in response to external chemical and environmental signals.
descriptions.approach: Proteins are grouped by sequence and structural similarity, then mapped to regulatory regions and expression profiles. Their activity is assessed under various stimuli using high-throughput sequencing data to identify patterns of activation or suppression.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: 3D Modeling/Printing of Female Reproductive Pathologies: Students Contribution to Pathology Education Through A Research Elective

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new teaching method in a medical education setting, comparing the outcomes of students who used this method to those who did not. It aims to explain how this method can improve learning outcomes and student engagement.
descriptions.approach: The method uses a combination of interactive, annotated content and feedback from a subset of participants to evaluate its effectiveness and identify areas for improvement. It involves collecting and analyzing data from a survey and free-text feedback to inform the development of the teaching method.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A structured learning activity is designed to help learners connect visual observations of biological specimens with detailed, context-rich explanations, using interactive content and real-time feedback to reinforce understanding.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of annotated visual data is paired with targeted questions and explanatory narratives generated by an automated system. Learners engage with faculty and peer facilitators, and their responses to specific components are collected and analyzed to refine the experience iteratively.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Serum magnesium levels as a predictor of coronary artery stenosis and their association with oxidative stress biomarkers

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between levels of a certain mineral and the presence of a narrowing of a major blood vessel, as well as its connection to a type of damage caused by free radicals. It also predicts the likelihood of this narrowing based on the mineral's levels.
descriptions.approach: The researchers compared data from 84 patients to see if the mineral's levels were different between those with the narrowing and those without. They used various statistical tests to analyze the data and draw conclusions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A numerical value is estimated to predict the presence of a specific physiological condition, and its relationship to another measurable biological indicator is assessed. The strength and direction of this relationship are evaluated using rank-based statistical methods, and the predictive power of the value is quantified through a performance curve.
descriptions.approach: A model compares a patient's level of a specific bodily substance to a reference group, using rank-based correlation to assess its link to a biological marker. It then determines a threshold value to classify individuals into a condition group based on performance metrics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Factors Leading to Political Activism in University Students: Case Study of Musa Khan’s Death

descriptions.problem: This research aims to understand the factors that led to a large-scale online movement among university participants, resulting in widespread protests and demands for accountability. It seeks to identify the key events, emotions, and influences that triggered this collective action.
descriptions.approach: The study uses online data from various platforms to analyze the spread of information, emotional responses, and protest calls. It follows the procedure of identifying trends, tracking the movement's growth, and comparing the online activity to the real-world protests and demands for accountability.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A pattern of collective behavior is analyzed to understand how a single event triggers widespread public response and organizational change within an educational institution.
descriptions.approach: An algorithm maps the spread of content across digital networks, tracks the rise of shared symbols, and correlates user engagement with shifts in institutional policies and public discourse over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: PEG‐23 glyceryl distearate, a multifunctional skin‐supporting material, upregulates the expression of factors associated with epidermal barrier and hydration

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a material on the health and appearance of a critical organ, comparing its impact on the organ's protective functions and water retention. It predicts the material's role in maintaining the organ's homeostasis and optimizes its potential applications.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of laboratory experiments and 3D models to investigate the material's effects on the organ's cells and structure, analyzing gene expression and protein levels to understand its mechanisms.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A substance is tested to determine its effect on the expression of genes linked to barrier integrity and water retention in living tissue cultures that mimic real-world tissue structure.
descriptions.approach: The substance is applied to cells and tissue models, and gene activity is measured over time. The effect is evaluated by comparing gene expression levels with and without the substance, and by blocking a key regulatory pathway to assess its influence on downstream molecular responses.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Food Security and Health in Diverse Populations
title: Assessing Food Pantry Usage and Distance to a Food Pantry in El Paso County, Texas

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between the distance of households to a certain type of service and the likelihood of using that service. It compares the usage of this service across different distance measures.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from surveys of households to analyze how the distance to a certain type of service affects its usage. They used a statistical method to identify the relationship between distance and usage.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The relationship between household location and access to a local resource is estimated, specifically how proximity influences usage frequency and patterns.
descriptions.approach: Distance metrics are calculated from household locations to the nearest resource node, then modeled using statistical methods that account for spatial clustering and repeated observations over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Corroles and Hybrid Corroles Bearing 1,4-Dihydropyrrolo[3,2-B]Pyrrole Scaffold

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the synthesis of a specific type of molecule from commercially available reagents, predicts the yield of the reaction, and compares the results to previous methods. It also explains the challenges in preparing a specific type of molecule with a particular functional group.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves combining the reagents in a mixture of water and methanol, with the addition of a catalyst, to facilitate the reaction. The reaction is optimized by adjusting the conditions to increase the yield of the desired molecule.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to create complex ring-based molecules with specific functional groups at defined positions, where one group can both participate in and inhibit a key reaction pathway, and the outcome is evaluated based on structural and optical properties.
descriptions.approach: A reaction combines three components to form a ring structure, but when a reactive formyl group is placed at a specific site, a side reaction occurs, diverting the pathway to form a different ring system with altered properties.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: A quantum machine learning framework for predicting drug sensitivity in multiple myeloma using proteomic data

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the sensitivity of a certain condition to a treatment, using data about the condition's characteristics. It aims to identify the most important characteristics that affect the treatment's effectiveness, and to predict the treatment's success for new patients.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a combination of techniques to analyze the data and make predictions. It starts by reducing the complexity of the data, then uses a special algorithm to identify the most important characteristics and make predictions about the treatment's success.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: Predict the likelihood that a patient will respond poorly to a treatment based on complex biological measurements, where many features are redundant, the minority of cases are hard to detect, and the data is highly variable.
descriptions.approach: Map input features into a high-dimensional space to reveal hidden patterns, reduce irrelevant variables, and enhance separation between responsive and non-responsive cases using entangled state processing and adaptive learning rules.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Labor market effects of a dual-VET apprenticeship: Evidence from Nepal

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the impact of a new type of training program on people's likelihood of finding work. It compares the outcomes of people who received the training to those who did not, using data from phone surveys.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a special statistical method to account for the fact that some people who were not in the training program might have started it anyway. They also looked for patterns in the data to see if the training program had a different effect on people who were already interested in finding work.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A policy intervention is evaluated for its impact on labor behavior and educational choices, comparing participants to a group with similar background but different exposure to the intervention.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model adjusts for selection bias using random assignment and score-based discontinuities. It compares outcomes across groups using differences in observed behaviors before and after the intervention, controlling for pre-existing characteristics.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

topic_name: Food Security and Health in Diverse Populations
title: The food and nutrition assistance landscape

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the total annual budget of 16 large programs that help millions of people, and compares the budget from one year to the next. It also explains changes in the programs' budgets over time.
descriptions.approach: The work uses preliminary data from a large database to calculate the budget, and then compares the budget from one year to the next. It also looks at recent research reports that provide additional information about the programs.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system tracks changes in the scale and participation of 16 structured support programs over time, comparing trends across program types and identifying shifts driven by policy transitions or external events.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes temporal patterns in program activity using historical records, applies temporal filtering to isolate effects of specific policy endings, and models participation rates against funding levels to detect underlying drivers of change.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: The Intestinal Mechanisms in the Excretion of Pepsinogen, Amylase and Lipase in Coprofiltrate in Women During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the activity of digestive enzymes in bodily waste and blood, comparing these levels to those of non-bodily waste and blood. It predicts changes in these enzyme levels over time, specifically during childbirth and the postpartum period.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed data from studies of non-bodily waste and bodily waste from various time points, using different methods to measure enzyme activity. They followed a procedure that involved determining enzyme activity using specific methods and comparing these levels to those of non-bodily waste and blood.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The activity of digestive proteins in bodily fluids is measured over time across different life stages and delivery conditions, comparing changes in secretion levels and their variation based on delivery timing and method.
descriptions.approach: Proteins are detected using substrate-specific reactions that measure enzymatic breakdown rates; data are collected from biological samples and analyzed across groups to identify patterns in secretion dynamics and temporal shifts.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Dangerous arenas: why activists struggle for change in technocratic institutions

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of participating in institutions that shape global systems, and compares the benefits and drawbacks of doing so. It predicts that some individuals will still engage in this activity despite the potential risks.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a 'perspective of investment' to understand why individuals participate in institutions that may not fully align with their goals. They analyze data on economic development and transitional justice to identify patterns and trends.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A group of individuals evaluates whether to engage with structured systems that may dilute their core objectives, and determines the conditions under which such engagement still serves transformative goals despite potential erosion of original intent.
descriptions.approach: They assess the alignment between their vision and the system's operations, then balance short-term gains against long-term risks, choosing to participate when the system offers tangible opportunities for solidarity and alternative futures.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Establishing a Co-Culture of Interneurons with Periventricular Endothelial Cells

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the optimal conditions for combining two types of tissue to work together, predicting how they will interact and affect each other's growth. It compares the effects of different setups to find the best one.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a technique where they add the two types of tissue to a special container, let it settle, and then remove the container to allow the tissues to interact and grow together. They follow a procedure where they test different setups and choose the one that works best.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system is set up to observe how two types of biological units interact over time, with one type responding to signals from the other, under controlled environmental conditions.
descriptions.approach: Two distinct populations are introduced into a confined space, then separated to allow independent growth. After stabilization, they are allowed to exchange signals and influence each other, with interactions monitored over time.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Monitoring of veterinary drug residues in livestock products with antimicrobial resistance

descriptions.problem: The presence and levels of certain chemical compounds in food items are assessed across multiple types of products, with a focus on detecting elevated concentrations that exceed established safety thresholds.
descriptions.approach: Samples are processed using a chemical separation and detection technique to identify and quantify specific compounds. Results are compared against predefined safety limits and evaluated for frequency and magnitude across different product types and sources.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Drugs of the future: humic acids

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the potential benefits of a naturally occurring, organic compound on human health, comparing its effects to those of other substances. It aims to explain how this compound can be used to improve health outcomes, particularly in relation to cancer treatment.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data on various types of cancer and their treatment, as well as information on the compound's properties and effects on human physiology. It follows a procedure that involves analyzing and comparing the compound's effects to those of other substances.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: A system's impact on biological and environmental health is evaluated across diverse applications, including disease resistance, productivity, and protective effects in living organisms and ecosystems.
descriptions.approach: A model analyzes interactions between natural organic compounds and biological systems using empirical observations from varied environments, adjusting predictions based on exposure history and response patterns across species and conditions.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Predicting postoperative complications after cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy: retrospective cohort study

descriptions.problem: A model estimates the likelihood of a negative clinical outcome following a major surgical procedure, based on patient characteristics measured before surgery.
descriptions.approach: The model uses binary logistic regression to identify which pre-surgical factors are linked to adverse events. It then combines these factors into a single predictive score that assigns a probability to each patient.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Human monocyte inflammation in patients with Lp(a) or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is not accompanied by changes in chromatin accessibility in circulating classical monocytes

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of high levels of a certain protein on the behavior of a type of cell, and compares it to cells from people with low levels of the protein. It also predicts the levels of certain chemicals in the blood of people with high levels of the protein.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected blood samples from people with high and low levels of the protein, and analyzed the behavior of a specific type of cell from these samples. They used various techniques to measure the behavior of these cells and the levels of certain chemicals in the blood.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

descriptions.problem: The level of a specific lipid-related protein in the blood is associated with increased expression of a gene involved in interferon signaling, and elevated levels of a chemokine are observed in individuals with high lipid levels.
descriptions.approach: Blood samples are collected from individuals with varying levels of a lipid-related factor and matched for age and sex. Gene expression and protein levels are measured in isolated immune cells. No differences in the openness of regulatory DNA regions are found between groups.
descriptions.author: nicolas-maman

title: Distribution and antibiotic susceptibilities of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates detected in Ümraniye Training and Research Hospital
